knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Uncertain Optimization Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a family of optimization instances indexed by uncertainty and records the structured subclass used in the preceding linear, conic-quadratic, and semidefinite settings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An uncertain optimization problem is a family \(\mathcal P=\{\min_x\{f(x,\zeta):F(x,\zeta)\in\mathbf K\}:\zeta\in\mathcal Z\}\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), \(f(x,\zeta)\in\mathbb R\), \(F(x,\zeta)\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathbf K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\). In the stated structured subclass, \(f\) and \(F\) are affine in each of \(x\) and \(\zeta\) separately, and \(\mathbf K\) is a direct product of the standard cones appropriate to the linear, conic-quadratic, or semidefinite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general uncertain optimization problem is a collection of optimization instances indexed by uncertainty in an uncertainty set. Each instance minimizes an uncertainty-dependent objective subject to an uncertainty-dependent set-membership constraint. In the stated structured subclass, the objective and constraint maps are affine in each argument separately and the constraint set is a product of appropriate standard convex cones.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^n,\quad \zeta\in\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d
f(x,\zeta)\in\mathbb R,\quad F(x,\zeta)\in\mathbb R^m,\quad \mathbf K\subseteq\mathbb R^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P=\left\{\min_x\left\{f(x,\zeta):F(x,\zeta)\in\mathbf K\right\}:\zeta\in\mathcal Z\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertain Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust minimization with objective coefficients or functions depending on uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the deterministic decision set, let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(f:X\times\mathcal U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). The objective is uncertain when the realized cost of \(x\) is \(f(x,u)\) for an unknown \(u\in\mathcal U\). Under strict worst-case evaluation, its robust counterpart is \[\inf_{x\in X}\;\sup_{u\in\mathcal U} f(x,u).\] Thus every decision is ranked by its largest objective value over the prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain objective assigns scenario-dependent cost to each decision; strict robustness minimizes the largest such cost over the uncertainty set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
\(f:X\times\mathcal U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is defined for every admissible decision and uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \inf_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\) is the strict robust objective problem.

notation.meaning: cost of decision x under realization u

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust Objective Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case objective value of a candidate decision over all data realizations in an uncertain linear problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \widehat c(x):=\sup_{(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U}\left(c^Tx+d\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust objective value at a candidate decision is the supremum of its realized linear objective value over all data realizations in the uncertainty set.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^n
\mathcal U\ \text{is the uncertainty set of }\mathrm{LO}_{\mathcal U}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat c(x)=\sup_{(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U}(c^Tx+d)

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertain Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraintwise robust feasibility over a prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(g_i:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The system has uncertain constraints when feasibility depends on the unknown realization \(u\). Its strict robust feasible set is \[X_R=\{x\in X:g_i(x,u)\le 0\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal U\text{ and }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Equivalently, when the suprema are well defined, \(x\in X_R\) exactly when \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g_i(x,u)\le0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision is robustly feasible when every uncertain constraint holds for every realization in the uncertainty set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\varnothing\neq\mathcal U\).
Each \(g_i(x,u)\) is real-valued on \(X\times\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in X_R\iff \sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g_i(x,u)\le0\) for all \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard-Constraint Assumption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Requires constraint violations to be intolerable for every realization inside the prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Ax\le b\qquad\forall(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraints are hard: no constraint violation, even a small one, is tolerated when the realized data belong to the uncertainty set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U\ \text{is the prescribed uncertainty set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax\le b\quad\forall(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U

children.title: Technology-Matrix Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty affecting technological coefficients that link decisions to constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Technology-Matrix Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage linear model with uncertain coefficients multiplying precommitment decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a two-stage linear model, let \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be chosen before \(u\in\mathcal U\) is observed and let \(y(u)\in\mathbb R^q\) be a recourse action. Technology-matrix uncertainty is present when the matrix \(T(u)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) multiplying \(x\) depends on \(u\), as in \[T(u)x+Wy(u)\ge h(u),\qquad u\in\mathcal U.\] It differs from recourse-matrix uncertainty, in which the matrix multiplying \(y(u)\) is itself uncertain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Technology-matrix uncertainty means that uncertain coefficients multiply the precommitted decision inside constraints later completed by recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is selected before \(u\), while \(y(u)\) may depend on \(u\).
The displayed vectors and matrices have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dependence \(T=T(u)\) makes the technology term \(T(u)x\) realization-dependent.

notation.meaning: uncertain technology matrix multiplying the precommitment decision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation is plausible, but the cited stochastic-recourse section has not been shown to support the specific robust-optimization terminology or the distinction between technology-matrix and recourse-matrix uncertainty.

children.title: Recourse Structure
children.top_down_role: Available corrective decisions following uncertainty realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage adjustable robust feasibility represented by a realization-indexed policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) be selected before uncertainty and let a policy \(y:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^q\) be selected from a policy class \(\mathcal Y\). A two-stage robust problem with recourse has the form \[\inf_{x\in X,\,y\in\mathcal Y}\;\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\bigl(c(u)^{\mathsf T}x+d(u)^{\mathsf T}y(u)\bigr)\] subject to \[T(u)x+W(u)y(u)\ge h(u)\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] The policy must be nonanticipative: its value may use the observed realization but no information unavailable when the recourse action is taken.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse augments a precommitted decision with a nonanticipative action selected after uncertainty is observed, while requiring feasibility for every realization.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) and \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(\mathcal Y\) contains only policies measurable with respect to information available at the recourse stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility requires \(T(u)x+W(u)y(u)\ge h(u)\) simultaneously for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is coherent, but a stochastic recourse citation alone does not establish the displayed adjustable robust minimax model or its robust nonanticipativity interpretation. An authoritative adjustable-robust source is required.

children.title: Technology–Recourse Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between uncertain technological coefficients and corrective decision capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Technology–Recourse Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility coupling between uncertain technology and realization-dependent corrective actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a precommitment decision \(x\in X\) and realization \(u\in\mathcal U\), define the recourse correspondence \[Y(x,u)=\{y\in\mathbb R^q:T(u)x+W(u)y\ge h(u),\ y\in Y_0(u)\}.\] Technology and recourse are coupled because the admissible corrective actions depend jointly on \(T(u)x\) and \(u\). Complete robust recourse for \(x\) is the condition \[Y(x,u)\neq\varnothing\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] If this condition fails at any realization, no adjustable policy can make that precommitment decision robustly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Technology and recourse are coupled when the corrective actions available after observation depend on both the precommitted decision and realized technology.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is fixed before \(u\) is observed.
\(Y_0(u)\) specifies realization-dependent restrictions on recourse actions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete robust recourse for \(x\) holds exactly when \(Y(x,u)\neq\varnothing\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The correspondence correctly expresses realization-wise recourse feasibility for a fixed precommitment, but calling this condition “complete robust recourse” requires source confirmation because complete and relatively complete recourse have established, differing meanings.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Worst-Case Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical robust criterion requiring feasibility under every admitted realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), objective \(f:X\times\mathcal U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and constraints \(g_i:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R\). Strict worst-case robustness solves \[\inf_{x\in X}\;\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_i(x,u)\le0\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U,\ i=1,\ldots,m.\] No violation is permitted at any realization in \(\mathcal U\), and no probabilities are required. If the objective is deterministic, the inner supremum is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict robustness permits no constraint violation anywhere in the uncertainty set and evaluates an uncertain objective by its worst realization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
The worst-case objective and all robust constraints are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible \(x\) satisfies \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g_i(x,u)\le0\) for each \(i\).

notation.meaning: set of all protected uncertainty realizations

knowledge_statements.title: Minimax-Regret Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-regret criterion relative to a realization-wise clairvoyant optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\neq\varnothing\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and suppose \(f(x,u)\) is minimized. Define the clairvoyant value \(v(u)=\inf_{z\in X}f(z,u)\) and the absolute regret \(R(x,u)=f(x,u)-v(u)\). A minimax-regret robust decision is any \[x^{\mathrm{MR}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\;\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}R(x,u).\] The benchmark \(v(u)\) allows a separate decision after each realization, whereas \(x^{\mathrm{MR}}\) must be chosen without knowing which realization occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimax regret chooses the decision whose largest loss relative to the realization-wise clairvoyant optimum is smallest.
assumptions_latex: \(v(u)>-\infty\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
The displayed argmin is nonempty when the phrase “a minimax-regret decision” is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathrm{MR}}\) minimizes \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}[f(x,u)-\inf_{z\in X}f(z,u)]\).

notation.meaning: clairvoyant optimal value under realization u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-regret formula is standard, but the cited chapter-opening locator is not specific to minimax regret. The domain of f is also unstated, so finiteness conditions needed to make f(x,u)-v(u) well defined cannot be verified from the citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Penalized Violations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalized robustness allowing controlled deterioration outside a core uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), let \(d(u,\mathcal U_0)=\inf_{v\in\mathcal U_0}\|u-v\|\), and let \(g_i(x,u)\le0\) denote uncertain constraints. For nonnegative penalties \(\rho_i\), a distance-penalized globalized robust requirement is \[g_i(x,u)\le \rho_i d(u,\mathcal U_0)\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U,\ i=1,\ldots,m.\] It enforces the original constraints on \(\mathcal U_0\) and permits violations outside that core only at a rate bounded by distance from it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint violations are forbidden on a core uncertainty set and bounded outside it by a penalty rate times distance from the core.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U_0\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U\).
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm and \(\rho_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(u\in\mathcal U_0\), the requirement implies \(g_i(x,u)\le0\); elsewhere it implies \(g_i(x,u)_+\le\rho_i d(u,\mathcal U_0)\).

notation.meaning: distance from u to the core region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distance-based violation bound is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no citation supports this exact globalized-robustness convention or its interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Protection Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalized robustness expressed through expanding uncertainty regions and deterioration bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\mathcal U(r):r\in[0,\bar r]\}\) satisfy \(\mathcal U(r_1)\subseteq\mathcal U(r_2)\) whenever \(r_1\le r_2\), and let \(\beta_i:[0,\bar r]\to\mathbb R_+\) be nondecreasing with \(\beta_i(0)=0\). A nested-region robust requirement is \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U(r)}g_i(x,u)\le\beta_i(r)\quad\text{for every }r\in[0,\bar r],\ i=1,\ldots,m.\] The inner region \(\mathcal U(0)\) receives strict protection, while the permitted worst violation grows according to \(\beta_i\) as the protected region expands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested protection requires increasingly large uncertainty regions to satisfy correspondingly relaxed violation bounds, with strict protection on the innermost region.
assumptions_latex: The family \(\mathcal U(r)\) is nonempty and nested by inclusion.
Each \(\beta_i\) is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and satisfies \(\beta_i(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U(0)}g_i(x,u)\le0\), and protection on larger \(\mathcal U(r)\) deteriorates by at most \(\beta_i(r)\).

notation.meaning: protection region at radius or level r
allowed worst violation at level r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-region representation is internally consistent and appropriately classified, but no authoritative source is supplied for this exact globalized-robustness formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Robust Violation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust feasibility relaxed by explicit realization-dependent violation envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i(x,u)\le0\) be uncertain constraints on \(X\times\mathcal U\), and let \(b_i:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R_+\) be prescribed violation envelopes. A decision \(x\in X\) has controlled robust violation when \[g_i(x,u)\le b_i(u)\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U,\ i=1,\ldots,m.\] Equivalently, its positive violation satisfies \([g_i(x,u)]_+\le b_i(u)\) uniformly over uncertainty. The envelope is part of the robustness specification: \(b_i\equiv0\) recovers strict robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlled robustness permits violations only within explicit envelopes that bound each constraint’s positive violation for every uncertainty realization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\), \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and \(b_i(u)\ge0\).
Each \(g_i\) and \(b_i\) is defined throughout its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}([g_i(x,u)]_+-b_i(u))\le0\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: allowed violation envelope for constraint i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The envelope formulation is coherent, but no source establishes that it is the intended definition of Controlled Robust Violation within the controlled-robustness family.

knowledge_statements.title: Nominal-Quality Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled robustness constrained to remain near the nominal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a nominal realization \(\bar u\in\mathcal U\), let \(X_0\subseteq X\) be the nominally feasible set, and define \(v_0=\inf_{z\in X_0}f(z,\bar u)\). For minimization, an admissible robust decision \(x\) preserves nominal quality within tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) when \[x\in X_0\quad\text{and}\quad f(x,\bar u)\le v_0+\varepsilon.\] If relative tolerance is intended and \(v_0>0\), the bound may instead be specified as \(f(x,\bar u)\le(1+\varepsilon)v_0\); the chosen convention must be fixed in the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust decision preserves nominal quality when it remains nominally feasible and its nominal objective is within a stated tolerance of the nominal optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar u\in\mathcal U\), \(X_0\neq\varnothing\), and \(v_0\) is finite.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\); relative tolerance additionally requires \(v_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nominal preservation is certified by \(x\in X_0\) and \(f(x,\bar u)-v_0\le\varepsilon\) under the additive convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive nominal-quality condition is mathematically sound, but no source ties it to the specified controlled-robustness family or confirms the additive-versus-relative convention.

children.title: Precommitment Decisions
children.top_down_role: Decisions fixed before uncertain parameters become observable.

knowledge_statements.title: Precommitment Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decisions fixed before uncertainty is observed and shared across all realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) be the set of possible realizations. A precommitment decision is a single vector \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) selected before the realized \(u\in\mathcal U\) becomes known. Formally, its policy is the constant mapping \(\pi_x:\mathcal U\to X\) defined by \[\pi_x(u)=x\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] In a static robust model, this same \(x\) must satisfy all realization-indexed constraints; it cannot be revised after information about \(u\) arrives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precommitment decision is fixed before uncertainty is revealed and must be used unchanged under every possible realization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the available decision set before observation.
The realization \(u\in\mathcal U\) is unavailable when \(x\) is chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(u_1)=\pi_x(u_2)=x\) for all \(u_1,u_2\in\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: decision selected before uncertainty is observed
constant zero-adaptivity policy induced by x

children.title: Zero-Adaptivity Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies without scenario-contingent or history-contingent adjustment.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Adaptivity Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust policies with no decision dependence on observed uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the decision set and let \(\mathcal U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set. A policy \(\pi:\mathcal U\to X\) has zero adaptivity when there exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that \(\pi(u)=\bar x\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). For constraints \(g(x,u)\leq 0\), this constant policy is robustly feasible exactly when \(g(\bar x,u)\leq 0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-adaptivity policy uses one precommitted decision in every scenario; that policy is robustly feasible only if the decision satisfies every scenario constraint.
assumptions_latex: The decision set \(X\) and nonempty uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\) are specified.
For every \(u\in\mathcal U\), feasibility is described by \(g(x,u)\leq 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero adaptivity means \(\pi(u)=\bar x\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\); robust feasibility additionally requires \(g(\bar x,u)\leq 0\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\).

children.title: Static Robustness Limitations
children.top_down_role: Performance and feasibility limitations caused by excluding adaptation.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set is \(\mathcal U=[0,1]\).
The post-uncertainty requirement is the equality \(x=u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No static decision is feasible for every scenario, although the adjustable policy \(x(u)=u\) is feasible for all \(u\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete feasibility failure caused solely by static precommitment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the requirement \(x=u\) for every realization \(u\in[0,1]\). A static policy would require a single \(\bar x\in\mathbb R\) satisfying simultaneously \(\bar x=0\) and \(\bar x=1\), so its robust feasible set is empty. After observing \(u\), the adjustable policy \(x(u)=u\) satisfies the requirement in every scenario. Hence static robustness can be infeasible solely because it forbids responses to information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static robustness may be infeasible even when a simple scenario-dependent response is feasible for every realization.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Robustness Limitations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and fits the limitations leaf, but the cited locator has not been shown to contain or support this specific example.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\) is nonempty.
The first-stage decision \(x\) precedes observation of \(u\), while the recourse decision follows it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adjustable robust feasibility requires one \(x\) and an admissible policy \(y(\cdot)\) satisfying every scenario constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage adjustable robustness; multistage policies additionally obey history-based nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given decision sets \(X\) and \(Y\), an adjustable robust solution consists of \(x\in X\) and a policy \(y:\mathcal U\to Y\) chosen from a specified admissible policy class. It is feasible when \(g(x,y(u),u)\leq 0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). In a multistage model, each component of \(y\) may depend only on uncertainty observed before that component is selected; this is the nonanticipativity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjustable robustness chooses some decisions initially and lets later decisions depend only on uncertainty observed by their decision times.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjustable Robustness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal values of the adjustable and static robust counterparts for model (14.12)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-specific no-benefit-of-adjustability result conditional on the source-defined assumptions 1–2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the source-defined assumptions 1--2 for problem (14.12), its adjustable robust counterpart and its usual robust counterpart without adjustable variables have equal optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For problem (14.12), under the source's assumptions 1–2, permitting adjustable variables does not change the optimal value relative to the ordinary static robust counterpart.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic reformulation and policy recovery for the stated adjustable robust problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem conditional on the source-defined assumptions 1–3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under assumptions 1--3 of the stated uncertain problem, the adjustable robust counterpart has the same optimal value as
\[
\min_{t,u,\{v^\ell\}_{\ell=1}^L}\left\{t:\ p_{\zeta^\ell}u+q^Tv^\ell+d_{\zeta^\ell}\le t,\ P_{\zeta^\ell}u+Qv^\ell+r_{\zeta^\ell}\in\mathbf K,\ \ell=1,\ldots,L\right\}.
\]
Moreover, if \((\bar t,\bar u,\{\bar v^\ell\}_{\ell=1}^L)\) is feasible and, for a given \(\zeta\), \(\lambda(\zeta)\ge0\) satisfies \(\sum_{\ell=1}^L\lambda_\ell(\zeta)=1\) and \(\zeta=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\lambda_\ell(\zeta)\zeta^\ell\), then
\[
\bar V(\zeta)=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\lambda_\ell(\zeta)\bar v^\ell
\]
augments \((\bar t,\bar u)\) to a feasible adjustable-robust solution.

A feasible conic solution yields a feasible adjustable rule by convexly combining its scenario decisions using coefficients that represent the realized uncertainty as a convex combination of the listed uncertainty points.

\lambda_\ell(\zeta)\ge0,\quad \sum_{\ell=1}^L\lambda_\ell(\zeta)=1,\quad \zeta=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\lambda_\ell(\zeta)\zeta^\ell\text{ for policy recovery.}

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive price of robustness for minimization with an unchanged objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) and \(F_R\) be nonempty nominal and robust feasible sets satisfying \(F_R\subseteq F_0\), and minimize the same objective \(c:X\to\mathbb R\) over both sets. Assume that \(z_0=\inf_{x\in F_0}c(x)\) and \(z_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}c(x)\) are finite. Then \(z_R\geq z_0\), and the additive objective-value degradation is \[\Delta_R=z_R-z_0\geq 0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the same objective is minimized and both optimal values are finite, restricting the nominal feasible set to robustly feasible decisions cannot improve the optimum; the resulting nonnegative increase is objective-value degradation.
assumptions_latex: The nominal feasible set \(F_0\) and robust feasible set \(F_R\) are nonempty and satisfy \(F_R\subseteq F_0\).
The same objective \(c:X\to\mathbb R\) is minimized over both sets.
The values \(z_0=\inf_{x\in F_0}c(x)\) and \(z_R=\inf_{x\in F_R}c(x)\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust objective degradation is well defined and satisfies \(\Delta_R=z_R-z_0\geq 0\).

assumptions_latex: The nominal parameter \(u_0\) belongs to the uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\).
Scenario feasibility is expressed by \(g(x,u)\leq 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust feasible region satisfies \(F_R=\bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}F(u)\subseteq F(u_0)=F_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic contraction induced by enforcing every uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(u\in\mathcal U\), define \(F(u)=\{x:g(x,u)\leq 0\}\). The robust feasible region is the intersection \[F_R=\bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}F(u).\] If the nominal model uses \(u_0\in\mathcal U\), then \(F_R\subseteq F(u_0)=F_0\). Enlarging the uncertainty set can only contract this region: whenever \(\mathcal U_1\subseteq\mathcal U_2\), one has \(F_R(\mathcal U_2)\subseteq F_R(\mathcal U_1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust feasibility intersects the feasible sets of all scenarios, so it is contained in the nominal region and shrinks as uncertainty grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Region Contraction
Exact Robust Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact worst-case reformulation of a single robust inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the worst-case constraint function by \(\phi(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)\). Exact robust protection replaces the family of constraints \(g(x,u)\leq 0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\) with the robust counterpart \[\phi(x)\leq 0.\] These formulations have the same feasible set \(\{x:g(x,u)\leq 0\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal U\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact robust protection replaces all scenario inequalities with an equivalent worst-case inequality without changing the robust feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\) is nonempty.
The uncertain constraint is \(g(x,u)\leq 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact robust counterpart \(\phi(x)\leq 0\) is logically equivalent to \(g(x,u)\leq 0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Tractable Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner approximation certified by an upper bound on worst-case constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the decision set, let \(\phi(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)\) for \(x\in X\), and suppose a tractable function \(\widehat\phi:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(\widehat\phi(x)\geq\phi(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then \[\widehat\phi(x)\leq 0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g(x,u)\leq 0\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] Consequently, \(F_S=\{x\in X:\widehat\phi(x)\leq 0\}\subseteq F_R=\{x\in X:\phi(x)\leq 0\}\). Thus surrogate feasibility certifies robust feasibility, although the surrogate may be conservative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a tractable surrogate upper-bounds worst-case constraint violation on the decision set, satisfying the surrogate certifies robust feasibility, though it may exclude some robustly feasible decisions.
assumptions_latex: The decision set \(X\) and nonempty uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\) are specified.
The exact robust feasible set is \(F_R=\{x\in X:\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)\leq 0\}\).
A tractable function \(\widehat\phi:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(\widehat\phi(x)\geq\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The surrogate set \(F_S=\{x\in X:\widehat\phi(x)\leq 0\}\) satisfies \(F_S\subseteq F_R\), so every surrogate-feasible decision is robustly feasible.

notation.meaning: tractable upper bound on worst-case violation

knowledge_statements.title: Enumerated Scenario Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite uncertainty represented by an explicit list of scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u^1,\ldots,u^N\in\mathbb R^m\), where \(N\ge 1\). The enumerated scenario uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}.\] Consequently, for every function \(g:X\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\), robust feasibility of \(x\in X\) means \(g(x,u^i)\le 0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and the worst-case value satisfies \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)=\max_{1\le i\le N}g(x,u^i).\] Repeated scenarios do not change \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An enumerated uncertainty set contains finitely many listed scenarios; robust feasibility checks every scenario, and worst-case evaluation reduces to a finite maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(u^i\in\mathbb R^m\) for \(i=1,\ldots,N\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)=\max_{1\le i\le N}g(x,u^i)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-scenario definition and maximum identity are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source or specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Hulls of Scenarios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of finitely many scenario vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scenarios \(u^1,\ldots,u^N\in\mathbb R^m\), their convex-hull uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i u^i:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^N,\ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i=1\right\}.\] For any fixed decision \(x\), if \(u\mapsto g(x,u)\) is affine, then \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)=\max_{1\le i\le N}g(x,u^i).\] Thus affine robust constraints over the convex hull are equivalent to enforcing the constraint at every listed scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull contains all convex combinations of the scenarios. An affine uncertain constraint is robust over this hull exactly when it holds at every listed scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(u^i\in\mathbb R^m\) for \(i=1,\ldots,N\)
For fixed \(x\), \(g(x,\cdot)\) is affine
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)=\max_{1\le i\le N}g(x,u^i)\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex-hull representation and affine-extreme-value property

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-hull representation and affine-function maximum identity are correct and appropriately classified, but they lack cited evidence with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Interval Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise uncertainty with no cross-coordinate coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell,r\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfy \(\ell_j\le r_j\) for every \(j\). The independent interval uncertainty set is the box \[\mathcal U=[\ell_1,r_1]\times\cdots\times[\ell_m,r_m]=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ell_j\le u_j\le r_j\ \text{for all }j\}.\] Equivalently, with center \(c=(\ell+r)/2\) and half-widths \(d=(r-\ell)/2\), \[\mathcal U=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d).\] Each coordinate may attain any value in its interval independently of the others.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent interval set is a Cartesian product of coordinate intervals, equivalently an affine image of the unit infinity-norm ball by a diagonal scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,r\in\mathbb R^m\)
\(\ell_j\le r_j\) for every \(j\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u:\ell\le u\le r\}=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box and diagonal affine-image descriptions are consistent and fit Independent Interval Sets, but no inspectable supporting source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Interval Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval bounds augmented by joint restrictions across coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell,r\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfy \(\ell\le r\), and let \(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\). A linearly coupled interval uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ell\le u\le r,\ Cu\le d\}.\] The inequalities are interpreted componentwise. Unlike an independent interval set, feasible choices of one coordinate can restrict feasible choices of another through \(Cu\le d\). The set is a polytope whenever it is nonempty, because the finite interval bounds make it bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled interval set intersects a coordinate box with joint linear inequalities, so coordinate values cannot necessarily vary independently. A nonempty such set is a polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,r\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(\ell\le r\)
\(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ell\le u\le r,\ Cu\le d\}\) is bounded and polyhedral

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-plus-linear-coupling model is mathematically sound, including the nonempty-polytope conclusion, but the exact meaning of “coupled interval set” varies and requires a supporting source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: V-representation of a bounded polyhedral uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty bounded polyhedral uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) has a vertex representation if vectors \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\in\mathbb R^m\) are given such that \[\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i v^i:\lambda\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i=1\right\}.\] If the listed vectors are precisely the extreme points of \(\mathcal U\), the representation is irredundant with respect to deleting vertices. Every polytope admits such a finite representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex representation expresses a polytope as all convex combinations of finitely many points, which may be chosen as exactly its extreme points.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, bounded, and polyhedral
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\) for finitely many vertices
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard V-representation of a polytope

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The V-representation statement and extreme-point irredundancy claim fit the leaf and are standard, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: H-representation of polyhedral uncertainty by finitely many halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality, or H-, representation of a polyhedral uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:A u\le b\},\] where \(A\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^q\), and the inequality is componentwise. Each row defines a closed halfspace, so \(\mathcal U\) is their intersection and is therefore closed and convex. It is a polytope precisely when this intersection is bounded and nonempty. Equalities may be represented by paired inequalities without changing the represented set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality representation describes uncertainty as the intersection of finitely many linear halfspaces. The resulting polyhedron is a polytope when it is nonempty and bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:A u\le b\}\) is a closed convex polyhedron
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard H-representation of a polyhedron

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The H-representation, convexity, closedness, and polytope characterization are correct, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Space Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation using auxiliary variables in a higher-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+k}\) be a set in variables \((u,z)\), where \(z\in\mathbb R^k\) is auxiliary. The lifted-space representation induced by \(Q\) is \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\text{there exists }z\in\mathbb R^k\text{ with }(u,z)\in Q\}.\] Thus membership in \(\mathcal U\) is certified by a feasible lift \(z\). Convexity of \(Q\) implies convexity of \(\mathcal U\), because linear coordinate projections preserve convexity; closedness need not be preserved without additional conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted representation describes uncertainty as the coordinate projection of a higher-dimensional feasible set. A feasible auxiliary vector witnesses membership, and convex lifts yield convex projected sets.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+k}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u:\exists z,\ (u,z)\in Q\}=\operatorname{proj}_u(Q)\)

notation.meaning: feasible set in the lifted space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard lifted-set and coordinate-projection definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based lifted representation and its convexity and closedness qualifications are appropriate, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended Polyhedral Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral lift whose projection equals the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended polyhedral representation of \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a system \[E u+F z\le h,\qquad z\in\mathbb R^k,\] satisfying \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\text{there exists }z\in\mathbb R^k\text{ such that }E u+F z\le h\}.\] Here \(E\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{q\times k}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^q\). The lifted feasible region is a polyhedron, and its coordinate projection \(\mathcal U\) is also a polyhedron. The formulation may use fewer inequalities than a direct inequality representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended polyhedral representation projects a higher-dimensional linear-inequality system onto the uncertainty coordinates. Its projection is polyhedral and may have a more compact formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(E\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{q\times k}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{proj}_u\{(u,z):E u+F z\le h\}\) is polyhedral

notation.meaning: coefficients of the lifted inequality system

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard extended-formulation definition for polyhedra

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extended polyhedral representation and polyhedral-projection claim are mathematically correct and fit the representation leaf, but supporting evidence is absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership condition for equivalence between direct and lifted descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) and \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+k}\). The lifted set \(Q\) is projection-equivalent to \(\mathcal U\) exactly when \[\forall u\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad u\in\mathcal U\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists z\in\mathbb R^k\text{ such that }(u,z)\in Q.\] Equivalently, \(\operatorname{proj}_u(Q)=\mathcal U\). Hence every function \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) has the same worst-case value under the two descriptions: \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(u)=\sup_{(u,z)\in Q}g(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted and a direct uncertainty description are projection-equivalent exactly when they admit the same uncertainty vectors. They therefore produce identical worst-case values for functions of those vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\)
\(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+k}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_u(Q)=\mathcal U\)

notation.meaning: set of uncertainty coordinates occurring in Q

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality-of-projection criterion and immediate supremum identity

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured Norm Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty bounded directly by one norm without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\rho\ge0\). The corresponding unstructured norm-ball uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\|u-c\|\le\rho\}.\] It is closed, bounded, and convex. For any \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), its support function is \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+ho\|a\|_*,\] where \(\|a\|_*=\sup_{\|z\|\le1}a^\top z\) is the dual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstructured norm ball bounds the norm of the deviation from a center. Its linear worst case equals the nominal value plus radius times the dual norm.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\)
\(c\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\rho\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+ho\|a\|_*\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard norm-ball definition and support-function formula

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm-ball definition, geometric properties, and dual-norm support formula are correct, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional ellipsoidal uncertainty defined by one quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and \(\rho\ge0\). A single full-dimensional ellipsoidal uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:(u-c)^\top Q^{-1}(u-c)\le\rho^2\}.\] Equivalently, \[\mathcal U=\{c+Q^{1/2}z:\|z\|_2\le\rho\}.\] For every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), its support function is \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+ho\sqrt{a^\top Q a}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single ellipsoid is an affine image of a Euclidean ball. Linear worst-case evaluation has a closed form involving the ellipsoid’s shape matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in\mathbb R^m\)
\(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\)
\(\rho\ge0\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard full-dimensional ellipsoid representation and support function

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definite ellipsoid representation and support-function formula are correct and fit the leaf, but the record lacks inspectable evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Norm-Bounded Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-bounded primitive uncertainty mapped through a prescribed structure matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), \(L\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\), \(\rho\ge0\), and let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^k\). A structured norm-bounded uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\{c+Lz:z\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|z\|\le\rho\}.\] The matrix \(L\) encodes correlations, sparsity patterns, subspaces, or unequal sensitivities among uncertainty coordinates. For every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+ho\|L^\top a\|_*,\] where \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is dual to the norm imposed on \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured norm-bounded set is an affine image of a norm ball. The mapping encodes coordinate structure, and linear worst cases use the dual norm of the transformed coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(L\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\)
\(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^k\)
\(\rho\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+ho\|L^\top a\|_*\)

notation.meaning: dual norm on the primitive coefficient space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard affine-image model for structured norm-bounded uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine image of a norm ball and its support formula are mathematically correct, but the scope of “structured norm-bounded” is terminology-dependent and no supporting source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersections of Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections of affine ellipsoids used as robust uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,p\in\mathbb{N}\). For each \(j=1,\ldots,p\), let \(Q_j\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{m}\), \(c_j\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and \(r_j>0\). The corresponding intersection-of-ellipsoids uncertainty set is
\[\mathcal U=\bigcap_{j=1}^{p}\left\{u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}:(u-c_j)^{\mathsf T}Q_j^{-1}(u-c_j)\le r_j^2\right\}.\]
The set \(\mathcal U\) is closed and convex; it is bounded when nonempty because it is contained in every constituent ellipsoid. It may be empty unless the ellipsoids have a common point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intersection-of-ellipsoids set contains precisely the vectors satisfying every constituent quadratic inequality; it is closed, convex, and bounded when nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_j\in\mathbb S_{++}^{m}\) for every \(j\).
\(r_j>0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bigcap_{j=1}^{p}\{u:(u-c_j)^{\mathsf T}Q_j^{-1}(u-c_j)\le r_j^2\}\) is closed and convex.

notation.meaning: positive-definite symmetric matrices of order m
center, shape matrix, and radius of ellipsoid j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the mathematical claims are standard and internally consistent. No citation or inspectable locator supports the ellipsoid representation and geometric properties.
