knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Deviation Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The continuous, fractional budget set for componentwise normalized deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(d_i\ge0\), and let \(\Gamma\in[0,n]\). The continuous deviation-budget uncertainty set is
\[\mathcal U_\Gamma=\left\{\bar u+Dz:z\in\mathbb R^n,\ |z_i|\le1\ \text{for all }i,\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}|z_i|\le\Gamma\right\}.\]
Thus every coordinate may vary continuously within its prescribed interval, while the aggregate normalized absolute deviation cannot exceed \(\Gamma\). Nonintegral values of \(\Gamma\) permit a fractional final deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each coordinate varies continuously within its interval, but the sum of normalized absolute deviations is limited by the budget Gamma.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
\(0\le\Gamma\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_\Gamma=\{\bar u+Dz:\|z\|_\infty\le1,\ \|z\|_1\le\Gamma\}\).

notation.meaning: maximum absolute deviation of component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes a continuous fractional deviation-budget set and fits the container. An authoritative robust-optimization source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Constrained Deviations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonconvex deviation model limiting the number of perturbed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(d_i\ge0\), and let \(K\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\). The cardinality-constrained deviation set is
\[\mathcal U_K^{\mathrm{card}}=\left\{\bar u+Dz:z\in[-1,1]^n,\ \|z\|_0\le K\right\},\]
where \(\|z\|_0\) counts nonzero coordinates. Hence at most \(K\) uncertain components differ from their nominal values. For \(0<K<n\), this set is generally nonconvex; its convex hull is the continuous budget set with budget \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most K components may depart from nominal values. The model is generally nonconvex, and its convex hull is the continuous budget set with budget K.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i\ge0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal U_K^{\mathrm{card}})=\{\bar u+Dz:\|z\|_\infty\le1,\ \|z\|_1\le K\}\).

notation.meaning: number of nonzero coordinates of z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the cardinality-constrained leaf, and the convex-hull claim is mathematically plausible under the stated integer budget. The nonconvexity and exact convex-hull assertion require cited support with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Band Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component deviations are allocated among magnitude bands with bandwise count limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_K\) be pairwise disjoint intervals whose union is \((0,1]\), and let integers \(0\le L_k\le U_k\le n\) be prescribed. A normalized multi-band uncertainty set is
\[\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{MB}}=\left\{z\in[-1,1]^n:L_k\le\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{|z_i|\in I_k\}\le U_k\ \text{for every }k\right\}.\]
For nominal vector \(\bar u\) and nonnegative diagonal scale matrix \(D\), the uncertain vector belongs to \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{MB}}=\{\bar u+Dz:z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{MB}}\}\). Feasibility requires mutually compatible band bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized deviations are assigned to magnitude bands, and each band has lower and upper limits on how many components it may contain.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_K\) partition \((0,1]\).
\(0\le L_k\le U_k\le n\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{MB}}=\{\bar u+Dz:z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{MB}}\}\).

notation.meaning: lower and upper cardinality limits for band k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but multi-band uncertainty has several materially different formulations. No source identifies this symmetric magnitude-band/count-bound variant or supports its use as the intended local definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Budget Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust counterpart for one linear constraint under continuous budgeted coefficient uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \((\bar a+\widehat a\odot z)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) for every \(z\) satisfying \(\|z\|_\infty\le1\) and \(\|z\|_1\le\Gamma\), where \(0\le\Gamma\le n\). Set \(w_i=\widehat a_i|x_i|\ge0\) and order them as \(w_{(1)}\ge\cdots\ge w_{(n)}\). With \(q=\lfloor\Gamma\rfloor\), the robust constraint is exactly
\[\bar a^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{i=1}^{q}w_{(i)}+(\Gamma-q)w_{(q+1)}\le b,\]
where the last term is omitted when \(q=n\). This inequality protects against every admissible deterministic deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust protection adds the largest floor(Gamma) weighted deviations and the appropriate fraction of the next largest deviation to the nominal constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat a_i\ge0\) for every \(i\).
\(0\le\Gamma\le n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\|z\|_\infty\le1,\,\|z\|_1\le\Gamma}(\bar a+\widehat a\odot z)^{\mathsf T}x=\bar a^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{i=1}^{q}w_{(i)}+(\Gamma-q)w_{(q+1)}\).

notation.meaning: i-th largest value among the weighted deviations
integer part of the deviation budget

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct role for this exact deterministic robust counterpart, and the formula is internally consistent. Its exactness requires an authoritative budgeted-uncertainty citation and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistic Protection Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concentration interpretation under independent, centered, bounded coefficient deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be independent random variables with \(\mathbb E[Z_i]=0\) and \(|Z_i|\le1\) almost surely. For fixed \(x\), set \(c_i=\widehat a_i x_i\), and let
\[\beta_\Gamma(c)=\max\left\{c^{\mathsf T}z:\|z\|_\infty\le1,\ \|z\|_1\le\Gamma\right\}.\]
If \(\bar a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_\Gamma(c)\le b\) and \(c\ne0\), then Hoeffding's inequality gives
\[\mathbb P\bigl((\bar a+\widehat a\odot Z)^{\mathsf T}x>b\bigr)\le\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_\Gamma(c)^2}{2\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i^2}\right).\]
Thus deterministic budget protection admits a distribution-dependent probabilistic interpretation, not a distribution-free probability guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under independent centered bounded deviations, the deterministic protection buffer yields an exponential upper bound on the probability of violating the protected constraint.
assumptions_latex:
\(Z_1,
\ldots,Z_n\) are independent.
\(\mathbb E[Z_i]=0\) and \(|Z_i|\le1\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P((\bar a+\widehat a\odot Z)^{\mathsf T}x>b)\le\exp(-\beta_\Gamma(c)^2/(2\|c\|_2^2))\).

notation.meaning: support function of the normalized budget set in direction c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the probabilistic-interpretation leaf, and its independence, centering, and boundedness assumptions are explicit. The stated concentration bound and constant lack an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Dependence Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of protection interpretations to dependence among uncertain deviations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perfect dependence invalidates protection interpretations derived from independent-deviation concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge2\), choose \(0\le\Gamma<n\), and set \(Z_i=Y\) for every \(i\), where \(Y\) takes values \(-1\) and \(1\) with equal probability. Then each \(Z_i\) is centered and bounded, but the deviations are perfectly dependent. For weights \(c_i=1\),
\[\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_iZ_i=nY,\qquad \beta_\Gamma(c)=\Gamma.\]
Consequently,
\[\mathbb P\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_iZ_i>\beta_\Gamma(c)\right)=\frac12.\]
Hence an independence-based exponential interpretation cannot be transferred unchanged to arbitrarily dependent deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated bounded deviations can exceed a budget buffer with probability one-half, showing that independence-based protection bounds are dependence-sensitive.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge2\) and \(0\le\Gamma<n\).
\(\mathbb P(Y=1)=\mathbb P(Y=-1)=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\sum_i Z_i>\Gamma)=1/2\).

notation.meaning: common Rademacher factor driving all deviations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Counterexample is the correct content kind, and the construction matches dependence sensitivity. No source or inspectable locator supports the failure interpretation.

children.title: Budget Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between selected deviation budgets and realized uncertainty behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Underestimating the realized aggregate deviation budget destroys deterministic protection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(0\le\Gamma_d<\Gamma_t\le n\), where \(\Gamma_d\) is the design budget and \(\Gamma_t\) is the realized budget. For weights \(c_i=1\), the support functions of the continuous budget sets satisfy
\[\max_{\|z\|_\infty\le1,\,\|z\|_1\le\Gamma_d}\sum_{i=1}^{n}z_i=\Gamma_d,
\qquad
\max_{\|z\|_\infty\le1,\,\|z\|_1\le\Gamma_t}\sum_{i=1}^{n}z_i=\Gamma_t.\]
Thus a constraint whose available slack equals \(\Gamma_d\) is robust for the design set but is violated by some deviation in the realized set whenever \(\Gamma_t>\Gamma_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the true aggregate deviation budget exceeds the design budget, a constraint protected exactly to the design level can fail under an admissible realized deviation.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\Gamma_d<\Gamma_t\le n\).
\(c_i=1\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma_t>\Gamma_d\) implies that design-budget protection need not cover the realized budget set.

notation.meaning: budget used when constructing the robust constraint
aggregate budget of the realized deviations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample fits the budget-misspecification leaf and is internally consistent. The support-function and protection-failure claims have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Protection Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where nominal protection interpretations cease to be reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Protection Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership boundary for universal linear protection by a closed convex budget set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\mathcal Z_\Gamma=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\|z\|_\infty\le1,\ \|z\|_1\le\Gamma\}\]
and let \(\sigma_{\mathcal Z_\Gamma}(c)=\sup_{v\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma}c^{\mathsf T}v\). A realized deviation \(z\) satisfies every protected linear bound
\[c^{\mathsf T}z\le\sigma_{\mathcal Z_\Gamma}(c)\quad\text{for all }c\in\mathbb R^n\]
if and only if \(z\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma\). Therefore universal protection breaks down precisely outside the modeled set: if \(\|z\|_\infty>1\) or \(\|z\|_1>\Gamma\), a separating direction \(c\) exists for which the budget protection buffer is exceeded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Budget protection covers every linear direction exactly for deviations inside the modeled set; amplitude or aggregate-budget excess creates a direction in which protection fails.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\Gamma\le n\).
\(\mathcal Z_\Gamma\) is interpreted as the modeled normalized deviation set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma\iff c^{\mathsf T}z\le\sigma_{\mathcal Z_\Gamma}(c)\ \text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: support function of the budget set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind, and the statement precisely characterizes universal support-function protection. The separation characterization requires an authoritative convex-analysis source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone-Representable Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct finite representation by affine second-order-cone inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is second-order-cone representable without lifting if there exist integers \(p,m_1,\ldots,m_p\), matrices \(A_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j\times n}\), vectors \(b_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j}\), \(c_j\in\mathbb R^n\), and scalars \(d_j\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[\mathcal U=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\|A_ju+b_j\|_2\le c_j^{\mathsf T}u+d_j,\ j=1,\ldots,p\right\}.\]
Equivalently, each affine image \((c_j^{\mathsf T}u+d_j,A_ju+b_j)\) belongs to the Lorentz cone \(\mathcal Q^{m_j+1}\). Such a set is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directly second-order-cone-representable set is the intersection of finitely many affine inverse images of Lorentz cones, and is closed and convex.
assumptions_latex: \(p,m_1,\ldots,m_p\) are positive integers.
All displayed affine maps are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bigcap_{j=1}^{p}\{u:(c_j^{\mathsf T}u+d_j,A_ju+b_j)\in\mathcal Q^{m_j+1}\}\).

notation.meaning: Lorentz cone consisting of pairs whose scalar component dominates the Euclidean norm
affine representation data for constraint j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits direct second-order-cone representability and is mathematically consistent. No conic-optimization source or inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectrahedral Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty sets defined by affine linear matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_n\in\mathbb S^m\). The spectrahedron determined by these matrices is
\[\mathcal U=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:F_0+\sum_{i=1}^{n}u_iF_i\succeq0\right\}.\]
Here positive semidefiniteness means that
\[v^{\mathsf T}\left(F_0+\sum_{i=1}^{n}u_iF_i\right)v\ge0\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^m.\]
Thus a spectrahedral uncertainty set is an affine inverse image of the positive-semidefinite cone. It is closed and convex, although it may be empty or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrahedron consists of vectors for which an affine symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite; it is a closed convex set that may be empty or unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\in\mathbb S^m\) for \(i=0,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u:F_0+\sum_i u_iF_i\succeq0\}\) is closed and convex.

notation.meaning: symmetric real matrices of order m

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly matches spectrahedral sets, with consistent LaTeX and plain text. An authoritative semidefinite-optimization citation with a specific locator is missing.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Conic Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty sets obtained by projecting affine conic systems with auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times r}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\). A lifted conic set is a projection
\[\mathcal U=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\text{there exists }y\in\mathbb R^r\text{ such that }Au+By+b\in K\right\}.\]
The variable \(y\) is auxiliary and need not have an interpretation in the original uncertainty space. The set \(\mathcal U\) is convex, but it need not be closed because a linear projection of a closed convex conic feasible set need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted conic set is the projection of an affine conic system involving auxiliary variables. It is convex, though not necessarily closed.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A,B,b\) have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{proj}_u\{(u,y):Au+By+b\in K\}\) is convex.

notation.meaning: projection onto the original uncertainty coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits lifted conic sets and correctly distinguishes convexity from possible nonclosedness. Both the representation and the nonclosed-projection qualification require a cited conic-analysis source with a specific locator.

children.title: Cartesian Product Sets
children.top_down_role: Composite uncertainty sets assembled from componentwise set factors.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the component uncertainty set satisfies \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) and is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership is componentwise, and separable linear worst cases decompose as \(\sup_{u\in U} \sum_{i=1}^m a_i^\top u_i=\sum_{i=1}^m\sup_{u_i\in U_i}a_i^\top u_i\), whenever the individual suprema are finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Cartesian products of componentwise uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonempty sets \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), their Cartesian product is \[U:=U_1\times\cdots\times U_m=\{(u_1,\ldots,u_m):u_i\in U_i\text{ for every }i\}.\] Thus no constraint in the set definition links distinct components. If each \(U_i\) is convex, closed, compact, or centrally symmetric, then \(U\) has the corresponding property. Moreover, for vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), separability gives \[\sup_{u\in U}\sum_{i=1}^m a_i^\top u_i=\sum_{i=1}^m\sup_{u_i\in U_i}a_i^\top u_i,\] provided the component suprema are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian-product uncertainty set permits each component to vary independently; its membership and separable linear worst-case calculations decompose componentwise.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Product Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, inherited finite-product properties, and separable support calculation fit the Cartesian Product Sets leaf and are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Intersection Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty sets formed by simultaneous membership in multiple component sets.

assumptions_latex: The sets \(U_j\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(j=1,\ldots,q\), share the same ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A point belongs to \(U\) exactly when it satisfies every constituent membership condition; convexity and closedness are inherited from all constituents.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections used to impose several uncertainty descriptions simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), their intersection uncertainty set is \[U:=\bigcap_{j=1}^q U_j=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:u\in U_j\text{ for every }j=1,\ldots,q\}.\] Hence a robust constraint over \(U\) protects only against realizations satisfying all constituent descriptions. If every \(U_j\) is convex, then \(U\) is convex; if every \(U_j\) is closed, then \(U\) is closed. Nonemptiness is not inherited automatically and must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intersection set contains precisely the uncertainty realizations satisfying every constituent description; it preserves convexity and closedness but may be empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-intersection definition and the convexity, closedness, and possible-emptiness statements fit the leaf and are correct, but the record has no source citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Cross-Component Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependence introduced across components of a composite uncertainty set.

assumptions_latex: The uncoupled reference set is \(U_0=\prod_{i=1}^m U_i\), with each \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\).
A coupling map \(G:\mathbb{R}^{n_1+\cdots+n_m}\to\mathbb{R}^p\) and admissible set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(U\) is generally a strict subset of \(U_0\), and componentwise support-function decomposition need not hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling constraints imposed on an otherwise componentwise product set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_0=\prod_{i=1}^m U_i\) be an uncoupled uncertainty set. A cross-component coupling is an additional joint restriction represented by \[U:=\{u=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\in U_0:G(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\in K\},\] where \(G\) depends on at least two components and \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\). Unless the restriction is redundant or separable, \(U\) is not a Cartesian product. Consequently, even for a separable objective, its worst case over \(U\) need not equal the sum of independent component worst cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-component coupling adds a joint restriction to a product set, creating dependence and generally destroying componentwise worst-case decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Component Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes a joint restriction on a product set and appropriately notes the possible loss of componentwise decomposition. It fits Cross-Component Coupling, but the qualified structural claims lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Union Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty regions composed from multiple alternative component sets.

assumptions_latex: The constituent sets \(U_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(k=1,\ldots,K\), share an ambient space and are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(U\) requires membership in at least one branch; even when every branch is convex, \(U\) need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions representing alternative uncertainty regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), their union is \[U:=\bigcup_{k=1}^K U_k=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{there exists }k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\text{ with }u\in U_k\}.\] For any extended-real function \(f\), \[\sup_{u\in U}f(u)=\max_{1\le k\le K}\sup_{u\in U_k}f(u).\] A finite union of closed sets is closed, and a finite union of compact sets is compact, but a union of convex sets is generally nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union set collects alternative uncertainty regimes. Worst-case evaluation is the maximum of branchwise worst cases, while convexity is generally lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Union Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-union definition, branchwise supremum identity, and stated topological and convexity properties fit the Union Sets leaf, but no citation with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Disjunctive Set Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations that retain explicit alternatives among uncertainty regions.

assumptions_latex: Each branch has the representation \(U_k=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_{kj}(u)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m_k\}\).
The branch index set \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed existential formulation is exactly equivalent to \(u\in\bigcup_{k=1}^K U_k\); it introduces no convexification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact logical representation of a finite union by branch selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_k=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_{kj}(u)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m_k\}\). Membership in the disjunctive set \(U=\bigcup_{k=1}^K U_k\) has the exact representation \[u\in U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists z\in\{0,1\}^K:\ \sum_{k=1}^K z_k=1\ \text{ and }\ z_k=1\Rightarrow g_{kj}(u)\le0\ \text{ for all }j.\] The implication formulation is logical; replacing it by finite big-\(M\) inequalities is exact only when valid branchwise bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union is represented exactly by selecting one branch with binary variables and enforcing all constraints of the selected branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Set Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected content kind is correctly representation, and the existential one-branch formulation is exact without convexification. The big-M qualification is also appropriate, but the record lacks a source supporting the representation and exactness conditions.

children.title: Convexification Gaps
children.top_down_role: Structural loss arising when a disjunctive set is replaced by a convex relaxation.

assumptions_latex: For a nonempty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(v_U(f)=\sup_{u\in U}f(u)\).
The convexified set is \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\), and both displayed suprema are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gap \(v_{\operatorname{conv}(U)}(f)-v_U(f)\) can be positive for nonlinear \(f\), although it is zero for every affine \(f\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the uncertainty set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convex-hull replacement for nonlinear worst-case functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the convexification gap for worst-case maximization by \[\Delta_f(U):=\sup_{u\in\operatorname{conv}(U)}f(u)-\sup_{u\in U}f(u).\] For every affine \(f\), \(\Delta_f(U)=0\). This invariance fails for general nonlinear functions: with \(U=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb{R}\) and \(f(u)=1-u^2\), one has \(\sup_{u\in U}f(u)=0\), whereas \(\operatorname{conv}(U)=[-1,1]\) and \(\sup_{u\in[-1,1]}f(u)=1\). Thus convexifying a disjunctive uncertainty set can strictly enlarge the computed nonlinear worst case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexification preserves affine worst cases but can change nonlinear ones; a two-point set and a concave quadratic produce a unit gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits Convexification Gaps. The affine invariance statement and nonlinear counterexample are internally correct and aligned between plain text and LaTeX, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: Factor-Structured Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty sets organized through a lower-dimensional latent-factor structure.

assumptions_latex: A nominal parameter \(\bar u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), loading matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), factor set \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^r\), and residual set \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting set is the affine image \(\bar u+BZ+E\); its support function separates into factor and residual contributions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine latent-factor model with optional residual uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factor-structured uncertainty set is \[U:=\{\bar u+Bz+e:z\in Z,\ e\in E\}=\bar u+BZ+E,\] where \(\bar u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is nominal, \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) is a loading matrix, \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^r\) bounds latent factors, and \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) bounds residual uncertainty. For any \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\), its support function satisfies \[\sup_{u\in U}a^\top u=a^\top\bar u+\sup_{z\in Z}(B^\top a)^\top z+\sup_{e\in E}a^\top e,\] whenever the suprema are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factor-structured set expresses uncertainty through low-dimensional latent factors plus residual error, enabling a separated support-function calculation.
knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Structured Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine factor-plus-residual definition and support-function decomposition fit Factor-Structured Sets and are mathematically consistent. A specific supporting citation is absent.

children.title: Low-Rank Perturbation Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty sets restricting perturbations to low-rank structure.

assumptions_latex: The uncertain object is a matrix in \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), with nominal value \(A_0\).
A rank limit \(r\le\min\{m,n\}\) and a norm radius \(\rho\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible perturbation has rank at most \(r\); for \(r<\min\{m,n\}\), the set is generally nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-bounded matrix perturbations with an explicit rank cap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), radius \(\rho\ge0\), rank bound \(r\le\min\{m,n\}\), and a matrix norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), a low-rank perturbation set is \[\mathcal U_r:=\{A_0+\Delta:\operatorname{rank}(\Delta)\le r,\ \lVert\Delta\rVert\le\rho\}.\] Equivalently, each feasible perturbation admits a factorization \(\Delta=LR^\top\) with \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times r}\) and \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\), together with the induced norm restriction. When \(r<\min\{m,n\}\), the rank restriction generally makes \(\mathcal U_r\) nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank perturbation set bounds both the rank and norm of deviations from a nominal matrix; the rank restriction is generally nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Perturbation Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-and-norm-bounded matrix set fits the leaf, and the factorization and qualified nonconvexity statements are coherent. The record nevertheless lacks an inspectable source for these claims.

children.title: Rank Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Consequences of selecting an inadequate or excessive rank structure.

assumptions_latex: The modeled vector uncertainty set is \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}=\{te_1:|t|\le1\}\subset\mathbb{R}^2\).
The actual uncertainty set contains the omitted direction \(e_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A constraint can be robustly feasible over \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}\) yet violated by the actual realization \(e_2\), so an underestimated factor rank provides no protection in omitted directions.

notation.meaning: Standard coordinate vectors in two dimensions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by underestimating the uncertainty-factor rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}=\{te_1:|t|\le1\}\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) and the robust constraint \(u^\top x\le0\) for every modeled \(u\). With \(x=e_2\), one has \(u^\top x=0\) for all \(u\in U_{\mathrm{mod}}\), so the modeled constraint is robustly feasible. If the actual uncertainty includes \(u=e_2\), then \(u^\top x=1>0\). Hence underestimating factor rank can omit an entire adverse direction, and no bound based solely on the modeled factor coordinates controls the resulting violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating factor rank can omit an adverse direction, allowing a decision that is robust for the modeled set but infeasible under actual uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Misspecification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind correctly matches Rank Misspecification, and the two-dimensional omitted-direction example is internally valid. No source with a specific locator is supplied for the modeled failure phenomenon.

children.title: Data-Driven Parameter Uncertainty Sets
children.top_down_role: Construction of sets for uncertain coefficients or realizations, distinct from ambiguity sets over distributions.

assumptions_latex: Data \(D\) are sampled under a distribution indexed by an unknown parameter \(\theta\in\Theta\).
A random set \(C(D)\subseteq\Theta\) satisfies \(\mathbb{P}_\theta\{\theta\in C(D)\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any decision feasible for every parameter in \(C(D)\) violates its parameter-indexed constraint with sampling probability at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frequentist confidence regions used directly as parameter uncertainty sets.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) denote data generated under an unknown parameter \(\theta\in\Theta\), and let \(C(D)\subseteq\Theta\) satisfy \[\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb{P}_\theta\{\theta\in C(D)\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Use \(U(D):=C(D)\) as the uncertainty set. If a data-dependent decision \(x(D)\) satisfies \(g(x(D),\vartheta)\le0\) for every \(\vartheta\in C(D)\), then, for each \(\theta\in\Theta\), \[\mathbb{P}_\theta\{g(x(D),\theta)\le0\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Thus the confidence coverage transfers to a sampling-probability guarantee for robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using a valid confidence region as the uncertainty set transfers its coverage probability to the robust decision's parameter-feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Region Constructions

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

children.title: Quantile-Based Sets
children.top_down_role: Data-driven parameter sets formed from estimated distributional quantiles.

assumptions_latex: Scalar observations \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\in\mathbb{R}\) define the empirical distribution function \(\widehat F_N\).
Quantile levels satisfy \(0<p_-\le p_+\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set contains all scalar values between the selected lower and upper empirical quantiles; finite-sample confidence coverage requires separate calibration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar empirical-quantile intervals without an implied finite-sample coverage claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(\widehat F_N(t):=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1\{Y_i\le t\}\) and, for \(0<p\le1\), the left empirical quantile \(\widehat Q_N(p):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb{R}:\widehat F_N(t)\ge p\}\). Given \(0<p_-\le p_+\le1\), the quantile-based uncertainty set is \[U_{p_-,p_+}:=[\widehat Q_N(p_-),\widehat Q_N(p_+)].\] This definition specifies an empirical central or one-sided range. A claimed population-content or confidence level does not follow from the nominal quantile levels alone and requires finite-sample calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantile-based set is the interval between chosen empirical quantiles at levels strictly above zero; its nominal levels alone do not establish finite-sample coverage.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantile-Based Sets

children.title: Order-Statistic Sets
children.top_down_role: Parameter sets constructed from ranked sample observations.

assumptions_latex: The observations \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) are real-valued, with order statistics \(Y_{(1)}\le\cdots\le Y_{(N)}\).
Indices satisfy \(1\le k\le \ell\le N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uncertainty interval is \([Y_{(k)},Y_{(\ell)}]\); under an i.i.d. continuous model its probability content has an exact beta-distribution characterization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar intervals whose endpoints are selected sample order statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given real observations with order statistics \(Y_{(1)}\le\cdots\le Y_{(N)}\), an order-statistic uncertainty set is \[U_{k,\ell}:=[Y_{(k)},Y_{(\ell)}],\qquad 1\le k\le\ell\le N.\] If the observations are independent from a continuous distribution function \(F\), then \(F(Y_{(j)})\) has the \(\operatorname{Beta}(j,N+1-j)\) distribution. Consequently, endpoint ranks can be selected using exact order-statistic probabilities to control tail or content coverage; the uncalibrated interval itself carries no prescribed confidence level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-statistic set uses selected ranked observations as endpoints; exact finite-sample tail or content guarantees require rank calibration.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Statistic Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Order-Statistic Sets, and under an i.i.d. continuous distribution the stated beta law for each transformed order statistic is correct. The distinction between an uncalibrated interval and calibrated coverage is appropriate, but the exact distributional and calibration claims lack a cited source.

children.title: Tail-Coverage Calibration
children.top_down_role: Calibration choices governing coverage of extreme parameter realizations.

assumptions_latex: \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\) are independent and identically distributed copies of \(U\).
The score map \(S:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is measurable, and \(S(U)\) has a continuous distribution function \(F\).
\(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfies the displayed binomial-tail inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P_{\mathrm{data}}\!\left(\mathbb P\{U\in\mathcal U_q\}\geq1-\alpha\right)\geq1-\beta\).

notation.meaning: The measurable scalar score used to construct the uncertainty region.
The kth order statistic of the calibration scores.
Permitted probability mass outside the uncertainty set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-free upper-tail coverage guarantee obtained from a scalar score and its order statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\) be independent copies of a random vector \(U\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(S:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be a measurable score map, and define \(S_i=S(U_i)\). Assume that the distribution function \(F\) of \(S(U)\) is continuous, and write \(S_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq S_{(n)}\). For desired uncovered mass \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and confidence error \(\beta\in(0,1)\), select \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfying \[\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}{n\choose j}(1-\alpha)^j\alpha^{n-j}\geq1-\beta.\] With \(q=S_{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal U_q=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:S(u)\leq q\}\), one has \[\mathbb P_{\mathrm{data}}\!\left(\mathbb P\{U\in\mathcal U_q\}\geq1-\alpha\right)\geq1-\beta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent calibration observations, choose an order statistic whose binomial tail reaches the desired confidence. The score region below that threshold then covers at least probability mass 1 minus alpha with confidence at least 1 minus beta.
knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Coverage Calibration

children.title: Cluster-Conditioned Sets
children.top_down_role: Parameter uncertainty sets conditioned on data-derived cluster membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Conditioned Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A data-driven uncertainty set formed as a union of cluster-specific regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations in \(\mathbb R^d\) be assigned to clusters \(C_1,\ldots,C_K\). For each cluster \(k\), let \(\mu_k\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{d\times r_k}\), and let \(Z_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{r_k}\) be a prescribed latent region. The cluster-conditioned uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\mathcal U_k,\qquad \mathcal U_k=\{\mu_k+A_kz:z\in Z_k\}.\] If the active cluster label \(c\) is observed before optimization, the applicable conditional set is \(\mathcal U_c\); otherwise robustness is imposed over the entire union \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct one uncertainty region per data cluster; use the identified cluster when observed, or their union when the cluster is unknown.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_K\) define the selected clustering of the observations.
Each \(Z_k\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bigcup_{k=1}^K\{\mu_k+A_kz:z\in Z_k\}\).

notation.meaning: The uncertainty region conditioned on cluster k.

children.title: Factor-Based Sets
children.top_down_role: Parameter uncertainty sets generated from latent-factor representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Based Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A low-dimensional factor model with bounded factor and residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) have center \(\mu\in\mathbb R^d\), loading matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}\), factor region \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^r\), and residual region \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). \(B\) and \(\mu\) are fixed before the robust decision is evaluated.

children.title: Cluster–Factor Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Constructions combining cluster-specific behavior with latent-factor structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster–Factor Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A union of cluster-specific low-rank factor uncertainty regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clusters \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(\mu_k\in\mathbb R^d\), \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{d\times r_k}\), \(Z_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{r_k}\), and \(E_k\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Conditional knowledge of cluster \(c\) replaces the union by its component \(\mathcal U_c\); without such knowledge, the union retains both within-cluster and between-cluster uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Endogenous Uncertainty Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A monotonicity condition for decisions that reduce the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set equipped with a preorder \(\preceq\), where \(x_1\preceq x_2\) means that \(x_2\) expends at least as much uncertainty-reduction effort as \(x_1\). A decision-dependent multifunction \(\mathcal U:X\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^d\) exhibits endogenous uncertainty reduction when \[x_1\preceq x_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal U(x_2)\subseteq\mathcal U(x_1).\] The inclusion may be strict for some pair, representing effective investment in sensing, protection, information acquisition, or control.

\(\mathcal U(x)\) is nonempty for every admissible \(x\).

children.title: State-Dependent Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty sets whose admissible realizations vary with system state.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty sets indexed by an observed system state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a state space and \(U\) an uncertainty space. A state-dependent uncertainty specification is a multifunction \(\mathcal U:S\rightrightarrows U\) assigning each state \(s\in S\) a nonempty admissible set \(\mathcal U(s)\). At stage \(t\), after observing state \(s_t\) but before observing uncertainty \(u_t\), a robust constraint has the form \[g_t(x_t,u_t;s_t)\leq0\quad\text{for every }u_t\in\mathcal U(s_t).\] Dependence on past information is represented through the state; the current decision does not redefine \(\mathcal U(s_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The observed state selects the uncertainty set before the current uncertainty is revealed and without being redefined by the current decision.
assumptions_latex: The state \(s_t\) is observed before choosing or evaluating the stage decision.
\(\mathcal U(s)\neq\varnothing\) for every reachable state \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t\in\mathcal U(s_t)\) and robustness requires \(g_t(x_t,u_t;s_t)\leq0\) for all such \(u_t\).

children.title: Policy-Dependent Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Dependent Sets

Consequently, \(\mathcal U(\pi)\) may encode sensing, protection, or information patterns induced by the complete policy, but its membership rule must be evaluable from \(\pi\) without using the adversary's yet-unselected realization.

children.title: Feedback-Induced Set Changes
children.top_down_role: Changes in uncertainty geometry induced by decision or state feedback.

knowledge_statements.title: Feedback-Induced Set Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive uncertainty-set evolution induced by closed-loop state feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider state dynamics \(s_{t+1}=T_t(s_t,x_t,u_t)\), a feedback decision \(x_t=\pi_t(s_t)\), and a state-indexed uncertainty multifunction \(\mathcal U_t\). Closed-loop feedback induces the recursion \[u_t\in\mathcal U_t(s_t),\qquad s_{t+1}=T_t(s_t,\pi_t(s_t),u_t),\qquad u_{t+1}\in\mathcal U_{t+1}(s_{t+1}).\] Hence the next uncertainty set equals \[\mathcal U_{t+1}\!\left(T_t(s_t,\pi_t(s_t),u_t)\right),\] so changing the feedback policy can change future uncertainty sets through the state trajectory even when each stage's set depends only on its predecision state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feedback changes future states, which changes the uncertainty sets indexed by those states, even if the current set has no direct decision dependence.
assumptions_latex: The state transition \(T_t\) and feedback policy \(\pi_t\) are well defined.
Each \(\mathcal U_t(s)\) is nonempty on reachable states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_{t+1}=\mathcal U_{t+1}(T_t(s_t,\pi_t(s_t),u_t))\) along the closed-loop trajectory.

notation.meaning: Stage-t uncertainty set at state s.

children.title: Circular Decision Dependence
children.top_down_role: Circular relationships between decisions and the uncertainty sets they induce.

knowledge_statements.title: Circular Decision Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by defining uncertainty membership through an outcome that itself requires robust evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decision-dependent robust model is circular when its purported uncertainty set cannot be evaluated from the decision and prior information alone. Concretely, suppose \[\mathcal U(x)=\{u:H(x,u,y(x,u))\leq0\},\] while \(y(x,u)\) is itself defined only as a solution of a robust problem over \(\mathcal U(x)\). Then neither membership \(u\in\mathcal U(x)\) nor robust feasibility is defined without solving a fixed-point problem. If that fixed point is absent or nonunique and no selection rule is specified, the robust model has no unique feasible-set semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If set membership depends on an outcome defined through the same set, feasibility requires an unspecified fixed point and may be undefined or ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: The outcome \(y(x,u)\) is defined through optimization or feasibility over \(\mathcal U(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Feasible Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-dimensional example where smooth decision dependence destroys convex robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the decision domain be \(X=[-2,2]\), define the singleton uncertainty set \(\mathcal U(x)=\{x^2-1\}\), and impose the robust constraint \[-u\leq0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U(x).\] Because the uncertainty set is a singleton, feasibility is equivalent to \(-(x^2-1)\leq0\), or \(x^2\geq1\). Thus the robust feasible set is \[F=[-2,-1]\cup[1,2],\] which is nonconvex, although \(X\) is convex, the membership mapping is smooth, and the constraint is affine in \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth singleton uncertainty map can yield two disjoint feasible intervals, so decision-dependent uncertainty does not preserve convex robust geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=[-2,-1]\cup[1,2]\) is nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posedness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for closed robust feasibility and attainment in decision-dependent models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(\mathcal U:X\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, compact-valued, and continuous as a multifunction, and let \(g:X\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Then \[v(x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal U(x)}g(x,u)\] is finite and continuous, so the robust feasible set \(F=\{x\in X:v(x)\leq0\}\) is closed. If \(F\neq\varnothing\) and a lower-semicontinuous objective \(f\) has compact sublevel sets on \(F\), then \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) is attained. Empty values, loss of compactness, or discontinuity of \(\mathcal U\) marks a boundary where these conclusions can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact continuous uncertainty sets and continuous constraints give closed robust feasibility; a coercive lower-semicontinuous objective then attains its minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and closed, and \(\mathcal U\) is nonempty compact-valued and continuous.
\(g\) is continuous.
\(F\neq\varnothing\), and \(f\) is lower semicontinuous with compact sublevel sets on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is continuous, \(F\) is closed, and \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)\) is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraintwise Worst-Case Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supremum representation of separate universally quantified robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set. For each constraint \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(\mathcal U_i\neq\varnothing\) and let \(g_i:X\times\mathcal U_i\to\mathbb R\). Define \(\phi_i(x)=\sup_{u_i\in\mathcal U_i}g_i(x,u_i)\), allowing the value \(+\infty\). Then, for every \(x\in X\), \[g_i(x,u_i)\leq0\ \text{for all }u_i\in\mathcal U_i\text{ and all }i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\phi_i(x)\leq0\text{ for all }i.\] Each constraint may therefore use its own maximizing realization; no single uncertainty realization must maximize all constraints simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each universally quantified robust constraint is equivalent to requiring its own worst-case value to be nonpositive.
assumptions_latex: Each uncertainty set \(\mathcal U_i\) is nonempty.
Each \(g_i(x,\cdot)\) is extended-real supremum measurable or otherwise well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall u_i\in\mathcal U_i,\ g_i(x,u_i)\leq0\iff\sup_{u_i\in\mathcal U_i}g_i(x,u_i)\leq0\), constraintwise for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Worst-case value of constraint i at x.

assumptions_latex: \(U\neq\varnothing\) is an uncertainty set.
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(f_i:X\times U\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i(x,u)\le 0\ \forall i,\forall u\in U\iff \sup_{u\in U}\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x,u)\le 0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite systems sharing one uncertainty realization; no worst-case attainment is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\in X\) and define the joint violation function by \(V(x):=\sup_{u\in U}\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x,u)\). Then the semi-infinite robust system \(f_i(x,u)\le 0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to the single inequality \(V(x)\le 0\). The supremum need not be attained. If it is attained at \(u^\star\), then \(u^\star\) is a joint worst-case realization for the maximum constraint violation, although it need not maximize every constraint separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite robust constraint system is equivalent to requiring that the worst, over uncertainty, of the largest constraint violation is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Worst-Case Representation
Support-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine dependence on finite-dimensional uncertainty, allowing extended-valued support functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be nonempty, and let \(\alpha_i:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(q_i:X\to\mathbb R^k\). For \(x\in X\) and \(u\in U\), define \(f_i(x,u):=\alpha_i(x)+\langle q_i(x),u\rangle\), and define \(\sigma_U(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle\). Then \(\sup_{u\in U}f_i(x,u)=\alpha_i(x)+\sigma_U(q_i(x))\). Consequently, \(f_i(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) if and only if \(\alpha_i(x)+\sigma_U(q_i(x))\le0\). If \(\sigma_U(q_i(x))=+\infty\), the robust constraint is infeasible at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst-case value of an affine uncertain constraint equals its uncertainty-independent term plus the support function of the uncertainty set evaluated at the uncertain coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set and \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) is nonempty.
\(\alpha_i:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(q_i:X\to\mathbb R^k\), with \(f_i(x,u)=\alpha_i(x)+\langle q_i(x),u\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i(x,u)\le0\ \forall u\in U\iff \alpha_i(x)+\sigma_U(q_i(x))\le0\).

notation.meaning: support function of the uncertainty set

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Duality Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear-programming duality for a nonempty polyhedral uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Fu\le g\}\), and suppose \(U\ne\varnothing\). For \(q\in\mathbb R^k\), if \(p(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\), then linear-programming strong duality gives \[p(q)=\min\{\langle g,\lambda\rangle:\lambda\in\mathbb R^\ell_+,\ F^\top\lambda=q\}.\] The dual feasible set is nonempty and the minimum is attained. Hence an affine robust inequality \(\alpha(x)+p(q(x))\le0\) has an exact finite counterpart obtained by introducing such a multiplier \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite support maximization over a nonempty polyhedron equals an attained linear dual minimum, yielding an exact finite robust counterpart.
assumptions_latex: \(F\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Fu\le g\}\ne\varnothing\).
\(q\in\mathbb R^k\) and \(\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{Fu\le g}\langle q,u\rangle=\min_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^\ell_+}\{\langle g,\lambda\rangle:F^\top\lambda=q\}\), and the minimum is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Duality Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic support duality under primal Slater feasibility and finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times k}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^r\), and define \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:g-Au\in K\}\). Suppose there exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^k\) such that \(g-A\bar u\in\operatorname{int}K\), and let \(q\in\mathbb R^k\) satisfy \(p(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\). With \(K^*:=\{y\in\mathbb R^r:\langle y,z\rangle\ge0\ \forall z\in K\}\), conic strong duality yields \[p(q)=\min\{\langle g,y\rangle:y\in K^*,\ A^\top y=q\},\] and a dual minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under primal Slater feasibility and finite support value, conic support maximization equals an attained conic dual minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is a closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times k}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:g-Au\in K\}\).
There exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^k\) with \(g-A\bar u\in\operatorname{int}K\).
\(q\in\mathbb R^k\) and \(p(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(q)=\min_{y\in K^*}\{\langle g,y\rangle:A^\top y=q\}\), and the minimum is attained.

notation.meaning: closed convex cone and its dual

children.title: Closure Requirements
children.top_down_role: Topological closure issues relevant to exact robust-counterpart reformulation.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is a closed convex cone.
\(E:=\{(A^\top y,r):y\in K^*,\ \langle g,y\rangle\le r\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Closedness of \(E\) at \((q,p(q))\), together with finite primal value, supports exact dual representation and dual attainment.

notation.meaning: epigraphical image of dual feasible certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraphical closedness condition for finite-dimensional conic support duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E:=\{(A^\top y,r):y\in K^*,\ \langle g,y\rangle\le r\}\). The relevant closure requirement at a direction \(q\) is: whenever \(A^\top y_n\to q\) and \(\langle g,y_n\rangle\to r\) for some \(y_n\in K^*\), there exists \(y\in K^*\) with \(A^\top y=q\) and \(\langle g,y\rangle\le r\). Equivalently, \(E\) is closed at points over \(q\). When the primal support value \(p(q)\) is finite and equals the lower closure of the dual value, this condition yields an exact attained dual certificate at value \(p(q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact conic reformulation requires the dual epigraphical image to contain its limiting points over the direction being evaluated.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Requirements

children.title: Primal Attainment
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which the relevant primal optimization value is attained.

assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) is nonempty and compact.
\(u\mapsto\langle q,u\rangle\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(u^\star\in U\) such that \(\langle q,u^\star\rangle=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-set sufficient condition for attainment of an affine worst-case problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) be nonempty and compact, and fix \(q\in\mathbb R^k\). Since \(u\mapsto\langle q,u\rangle\) is continuous, there exists \(u^\star\in U\) satisfying \[\langle q,u^\star\rangle=\max_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle=\sigma_U(q).\] Thus the worst-case uncertainty realization is present in \(U\), rather than merely approached by a maximizing sequence. Compactness is sufficient, although other level-boundedness and closedness conditions may also ensure attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous affine uncertainty objective attains its worst case on every nonempty compact uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment

children.title: Dual Attainment

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual attainment supplied by finite-dimensional conic strong duality under primal Slater feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times k}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^r\), and define \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:g-Au\in K\}\). Suppose there exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^k\) such that \(g-A\bar u\in\operatorname{int}K\). For \(q\in\mathbb R^k\), if \(p(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\), then there exists \(y^\star\in K^*\) such that \(A^\top y^\star=q\) and \(\langle g,y^\star\rangle=p(q)\). Hence the dual infimum is attained, and \(y^\star\) is a finite-dimensional certificate for the support-function bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under primal Slater feasibility and finite value, an optimal conic dual multiplier exists and certifies the worst-case bound.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is a closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times k}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:g-Au\in K\}\).
There exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^k\) with \(g-A\bar u\in\operatorname{int}K\).
\(q\in\mathbb R^k\) and \(p(q):=\sup_{u\in U}\langle q,u\rangle<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in K^*}\{\langle g,y\rangle:A^\top y=q\}\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: closed convex cone and its dual

children.title: Positive Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Regimes where primal and dual optimal values differ.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued maximization-primal and minimization-dual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal maximization problem and its weak dual minimization problem, write \(p^*:=\sup\{\text{primal objective values}\}\) and \(d^*:=\inf\{\text{dual objective values}\}\). Weak duality gives \(p^*\le d^*\). The pair has a positive duality gap when both values are finite and \[d^*-p^*>0.\] In this case, replacing the primal worst-case value by the dual value strengthens the robust constraint and is not an equivalent reformulation, irrespective of whether either optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive duality gap means the finite dual infimum strictly exceeds the finite primal supremum, so dual substitution is conservative rather than exact.
assumptions_latex: The primal supremum \(p^*\) and dual infimum \(d^*\) are finite.
Weak duality gives \(p^*\le d^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive duality gap occurs exactly when \(0<d^*-p^*<+\infty\).

children.title: Primal Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Cases where the primal value exists without a primal optimizer.

assumptions_latex: The primal objective is \((s,t)\mapsto -t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{(s,t)\in U}(-t)=0\), but no \((s,t)\in U\) attains this value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete closed convex, noncompact uncertainty set exhibiting finite nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U:=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb R^2:s>0,\ t\ge1/s\}\), which is closed and convex despite the strict condition on \(s\), because every convergent sequence in \(U\) has a positive limiting first coordinate. For the linear objective \(-t\), \[p^*:=\sup_{(s,t)\in U}(-t)=0.\] The sequence \((s_n,t_n):=(n,1/n)\) has objective values \(-1/n\to0\), but every feasible point satisfies \(t>0\), hence \(-t<0\). Therefore the finite primal supremum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective can have a finite unattained supremum on a closed convex but noncompact uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Nonattainment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed, convex, noncompact example and its unattained finite supremum are mathematically coherent and fit the primal-nonattainment leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable source for this nontrivial counterexample.

children.title: Dual Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Cases where the dual value exists without a dual optimizer.

assumptions_latex: The dual objective is \((s,t)\mapsto t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(s,t)\in D}t=0\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(s,t)\in D}t=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete closed convex dual feasible region with a finite unattained infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the closed convex set \(D:=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb R^2:s>0,\ t\ge1/s\}\) as a dual feasible region and minimize the linear objective \(t\). Its value is \[d^*:=\inf_{(s,t)\in D}t=0,\] because \((s_n,t_n):=(n,1/n)\) is feasible and \(t_n\to0\). Yet every feasible point has \(t>0\), so no feasible multiplier attains \(d^*\). Thus equality of primal and dual values, if separately established, would not by itself provide an exact existential dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite dual value may be approached only by an unbounded multiplier sequence, leaving no optimal dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonattainment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly exhibits a finite unattained infimum and fits the dual-nonattainment leaf, but it has no inspectable source. A source should also justify its use as a dual-feasible-region example in this robust-duality context.

children.title: Reformulation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundary conditions under which a dual counterpart is not exact.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)\) is a primal worst-case value and \(d(x)\) its weak-dual value.
A proposed lifted counterpart asserts existence of a dual feasible certificate with value at most \(-\alpha(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact projection requires \(p(x)=d(x)\) and attainment of the required dual bound; otherwise the lifted system can be conservative or omit boundary points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact dual lifting and conservative or nonclosed projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose weak duality gives \(p(x)\le d(x)\). The primal robust condition is \(\alpha(x)+p(x)\le0\), whereas substitution of the dual value gives \(\alpha(x)+d(x)\le0\). If \(p(x)<d(x)\), the substituted counterpart is strictly conservative for any \(x\) with \(-d(x)<\alpha(x)\le-p(x)\). If \(p(x)=d(x)\) but the dual infimum is not attained, an existential lifted formulation requiring a feasible dual certificate can omit points satisfying \(\alpha(x)+p(x)=0\). Exact reformulation therefore requires zero gap plus the relevant certificate attainment or an explicit closure operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual robust counterpart ceases to be exact when a positive gap makes it conservative or nonattainment removes feasible boundary points from its projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-gap and boundary-nonattainment distinctions are mathematically plausible and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but the exact projection/closure claim is unsupported by any source and should be checked against an authoritative duality or robust-reformulation result.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Counterpart Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral lift of one affine robust inequality by linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(F\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and suppose \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Fu\le g\}\ne\varnothing\). Let \(\alpha:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(q:X\to\mathbb R^k\), and suppose \(\sigma_U(q(x))<+\infty\) for every \(x\in X\). Linear-programming duality gives \(\sigma_U(q(x))=\min\{g^\top\lambda:\lambda\in\mathbb R^\ell_+,\ F^\top\lambda=q(x)\}\). Therefore \(\alpha(x)+\sigma_U(q(x))\le0\) holds exactly when there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^\ell_+\) satisfying \(F^\top\lambda=q(x)\) and \(\alpha(x)+g^\top\lambda\le0\). Thus the robust feasible set is the projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates of this lifted set in \((x,\lambda)\)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral robust constraint is the projection of a finite lifted system containing the decision and a nonnegative dual multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set, \(F\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(U:=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Fu\le g\}\ne\varnothing\).
\(\alpha:X\to\mathbb R\), \(q:X\to\mathbb R^k\), and \(\sigma_U(q(x))<+\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in X:\alpha(x)+\sigma_U(q(x))\le0\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,\lambda)\in X\times\mathbb R^\ell_+:F^\top\lambda=q(x),\ \alpha(x)+g^\top\lambda\le0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constraintwise Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-duality construction for separately imposed robust affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), \(P_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times p_i}\), \(q_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}\), \(F_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i\times p_i}\), \(g_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\), and \(U_i=\{u\in\mathbb R^{p_i}:F_i u\le g_i\}\). If \(U_i\) is nonempty and bounded, then \((a_i+P_i u)^\top x\le b_i+q_i^\top u\) for every \(u\in U_i\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}_+\) satisfying \[F_i^\top\lambda_i=P_i^\top x-q_i,\qquad a_i^\top x+g_i^\top\lambda_i\le b_i.\] Thus separately imposed robust rows have row-specific dual certificates coupled only through \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each separately imposed robust affine row has its own nonnegative LP-dual multiplier; the resulting certificates interact only through the shared decision vector.
assumptions_latex: \(U_i\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
Each uncertain row depends affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\), the robust row is equivalent to the displayed linear constraints in \((x,\lambda_i)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust Counterpart of an Uncertain Linear Optimization Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the worst-case objective, robust feasibility, robust optimal solutions, and robust optimal value for uncertain linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\) be an uncertainty set of linear-optimization data \((c,d,A,b)\). Define
\[
\widehat c(x):=\sup_{(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U}(c^Tx+d).
\]
The robust counterpart is
\[
\min_x\left\{\widehat c(x):Ax\le b\quad\forall(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U\right\}.
\]
Any optimal solution of this problem is called a robust optimal solution, and its optimal value is called the robust optimal value of the uncertain linear-optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust counterpart minimizes the worst-case linear objective over decisions that satisfy the linear constraints for every data realization in the uncertainty set. Its optimal solutions and optimal value are called robust optimal solutions and the robust optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U\text{ is an uncertainty set of compatible linear-optimization data }(c,d,A,b).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{minimize}_{x}\ \sup_{(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U}(c^Tx+d)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\le b\ \text{for every }(c,d,A,b)\in\mathcal U.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust linear-program counterpart and support-function form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rowwise robust feasibility, establishes convexity for arbitrary uncertainty sets, and states the worst-case support-function representation with its attainment boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sets \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), the robust counterpart of a linear program with uncertain row vectors is
\[
\min_x c^\top x
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad
 a^\top x\le b_i\quad\forall a\in U_i,
\quad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
For every \(U_i\),
\[
X_i=\bigcap_{a\in U_i}\{x:a^\top x\le b_i\}
\]
is convex. Furthermore,
\[
a^\top x\le b\quad\forall a\in U
\iff
\sup_{a\in U}a^\top x\le b.
\]
The supremum may be written as a maximum only when it is attained. Explicit tractability depends on whether this worst-case value can be evaluated or represented tractably.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust LP requires every uncertain row constraint to hold for all coefficient vectors in its uncertainty set. The robust feasible set remains convex because it is an intersection of half-spaces. Each row is governed by the uncertainty set's support function; writing a maximum instead of a supremum additionally requires attainment.
assumptions_latex: U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
b_i\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_i=\bigcap_{a\in U_i}\{x:a^\top x\le b_i\}\text{ is convex},\qquad a^\top x\le b\ \forall a\in U\iff\sup_{a\in U}a^\top x\le b
