knowledge_statements.title: Rowwise Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP counterpart when every uncertain row has its own polyhedral set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), \(P_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times p_i}\), \(F_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i\times p_i}\), \(g_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}\), and \(U_i=\{u_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}:F_i u_i\le g_i\}\). If each \(U_i\) is nonempty and bounded, then the system \((a_i+P_i u_i)^\top x\le b_i\) for every \(u_i\in U_i\) and every \(i\) holds if and only if, for every \(i\), there exists \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R^{r_i}_+\) such that \[F_i^\top\lambda_i=P_i^\top x,\qquad a_i^\top x+g_i^\top\lambda_i\le b_i.\] Hence the rowwise-polyhedral robust system has an exact LP extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust linear system with a separate nonempty bounded polyhedral uncertainty set for each row has an exact LP formulation with one nonnegative dual vector per row.
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\), \(U_i\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
Each uncertain row depends affinely on its row-specific vector \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust feasible set is the projection onto \(x\) of the displayed linear system in \((x,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\).

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for the inequalities defining the rowwise uncertainty set

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact row certificates for coefficients generated by one common polyhedral uncertainty vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:Fu\le g\}\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{r\times p}\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^r\), and suppose \(U\) is nonempty and bounded. For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and \(P_i\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Then \((a_i+P_i u)^\top x\le b_i\) for every \(u\in U\) and every \(i\) is equivalent to the existence, for every \(i\), of \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R^r_+\) satisfying \[F^\top\lambda_i=P_i^\top x,\qquad a_i^\top x+g^\top\lambda_i\le b_i.\] The common uncertainty set therefore admits distinct exact dual certificates for its universally quantified rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even when one polyhedral uncertainty vector affects every row, exact LP reformulation uses a distinct nonnegative dual certificate for each universally quantified row.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
The same vector \(u\) affects all rows affinely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled robust feasible set is the projection onto \(x\) of the displayed LP system.

notation.meaning: row-specific dual certificate over the common uncertainty set

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP counterpart when the uncertainty set is given as a polyhedral projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), \(q\in\mathbb R^p\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{r\times p}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{r\times s}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\exists v\in\mathbb R^s,\ Fu+Gv\le h\}\). Suppose the extended polyhedron is nonempty and the support of \(U\) in direction \(c(x)=P^\top x-q\) is finite. Then \((a+Pu)^\top x\le b+q^\top u\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r_+\) such that \[F^\top\lambda=c(x),\qquad G^\top\lambda=0,\qquad a^\top x+h^\top\lambda\le b.\] Thus direct dualization of the lifted uncertainty-set description gives an exact extended LP counterpart without explicit projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected polyhedral uncertainty set can be dualized in its lifted variables, producing an exact extended LP counterpart without explicitly eliminating those variables.
assumptions_latex: The polyhedron \(\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R^s:Fu+Gv\le h\}\) is nonempty.
The support value in direction \(P^\top x-q\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust inequality is equivalent to the displayed lifted linear certificate in \((x,\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary variable in the uncertainty-set formulation
support-function direction P-transpose x minus q
nonnegative multiplier for the extended inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Ellipsoid Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOCP reformulation for one affine row over one Euclidean ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Then \((\bar a+Pz)^\top x\le b\) for every \(z\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfying \(\|z\|_2\le\rho\) holds if and only if \[\bar a^\top x+\rho\|P^\top x\|_2\le b.\] Consequently, replacing every row of this form by its displayed inequality gives an exact second-order-cone formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing an affine row over one Euclidean ellipsoid produces a Euclidean-norm term, yielding an exact SOCP counterpart.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(\rho\ge0\).
The uncertain coefficient vector is affine in \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to \(\bar a^\top x+\rho\|P^\top x\|_2\le b\).

notation.meaning: radius of the Euclidean uncertainty ball
matrix mapping uncertainty into the row coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Intersecting-Ellipsoid Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the single-ellipsoid norm formula for an intersection of ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(E_1=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:u_1^2/4+u_2^2\le1\}\), \(E_2=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:u_1^2+u_2^2/4\le1\}\), and \(c=(1,1)\), one has \[\sigma_{E_1}(c)=\sigma_{E_2}(c)=\sqrt5,\qquad \sigma_{E_1\cap E_2}(c)=\frac4{\sqrt5}<\sqrt5.\] Thus replacing the support of an ellipsoid intersection by the minimum of the individual supports is generally conservative, not exact. The one-ellipsoid SOCP formula therefore does not extend by simply selecting the tightest constituent ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support of intersecting ellipsoids can be strictly smaller than every individual support, so the single-ellipsoid norm formula cannot be reused directly.
assumptions_latex: Support functions are defined by \(\sigma_S(c)=\sup_{u\in S}c^\top u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, \(\sigma_{\cap_k E_k}(c)<\min_k\sigma_{E_k}(c)\) can occur.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically consistent and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no citation supports the exact values or the claimed limitation of the constituent-ellipsoid approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Ellipsoidal Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe outer-ellipsoid and optimistic inner-ellipsoid bounds for robust affine rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty, and let nonempty ellipsoids satisfy \(E_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq U\subseteq E_{\mathrm{out}}\). For a nonempty set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), define \(\sigma_S(c)=\sup_{u\in S}c^\top u\). Then, for every \(c\in\mathbb R^p\), \[\sigma_{E_{\mathrm{in}}}(c)\le\sigma_U(c)\le\sigma_{E_{\mathrm{out}}}(c).\] Let \(x,a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R\). Enforcing \(a^\top x+\sigma_{E_{\mathrm{out}}}(P^\top x)\le b\) is sufficient for \((a+Pu)^\top x\le b\) for every \(u\in U\), whereas using \(E_{\mathrm{in}}\) gives only a relaxation. The two ellipsoidal bounds are second-order-cone representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer ellipsoid gives a safe SOCP restriction of a robust affine row, while an inner ellipsoid gives a relaxation that may admit nonrobust decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq U\subseteq E_{\mathrm{out}}\), and all three sets are nonempty.
The uncertain row depends affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outer ellipsoidal containment yields a sufficient robust constraint, while inner ellipsoidal containment yields a necessary constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted-Uncertainty Linear Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Bertsimas–Sim linear counterpart for one budgeted uncertain row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_\Gamma=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:|z_j|\le1,\ \sum_{j=1}^n|z_j|\le\Gamma\}\), where \(0\le\Gamma\le n\). The robust row \(\bar a^\top x+\sum_j d_jx_jz_j\le b\) for every \(z\in U_\Gamma\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\theta\ge0\) and \(p_j\ge0\) such that \[\bar a^\top x+\Gamma\theta+\sum_jp_j\le b,\qquad \theta+p_j\ge d_jx_j,\qquad \theta+p_j\ge-d_jx_j\quad(j=1,dots,n).\] Thus the budgeted robust counterpart is a linear formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality-budget uncertainty set yields an exact LP counterpart with one threshold variable and one nonnegative excess variable per coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\Gamma\le n\) and \(d_j\ge0\).
Coefficient perturbations are \(d_jz_j\) with \(z\in U_\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust row is equivalent to the displayed finite linear system.

notation.meaning: dual variables of the budgeted support problem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated Bertsimas–Sim counterpart is standard, but the named theorem has no source. In addition, the index text uses the invalid expression \(j=1,dots,n\) instead of \(j=1,\ldots,n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonaffine Perturbations of Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonaffine uncertainty can turn robust separation into a hard nonconvex maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model may be linear in \(x\) while its uncertain coefficient map is nonaffine. For example, let \(U=\{-1,1\}^n\) and require \(x+u^\top Q u\le b\) for every \(u\in U\), with symmetric \(Q\). Its exact counterpart is \[x+\max_{u\in\{-1,1\}^n}u^\top Q u\le b.\] For suitable \(Q\), evaluating this maximum contains the weighted Max-Cut problem. Consequently, the LP and SOCP recipes based on affine support functions do not generally extend to nonaffine perturbations without additional structure or relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonaffine coefficient dependence can make robust separation NP-hard even when the decision appears linearly, so affine counterpart formulas need not survive.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a given symmetric rational matrix.
Computational complexity is measured in the binary encoding of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact robust separation for the displayed family is NP-hard in general.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and content kind fit the leaf, but the NP-hardness conclusion and claimed Max-Cut embedding require a specific complexity reference or reduction locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust feasibility and robust counterpart of an uncertain conic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines robust feasibility over a perturbation set and the epigraph formulation minimizing the guaranteed worst-case objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an uncertain conic program and a perturbation set \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is robust feasible if and only if \(A_i(\zeta)x-b_i(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q_i\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and every \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z\). Its robust counterpart is \[\min_{x,t}\left\{t:c(\zeta)^Tx+d(\zeta)-t\in\mathbb R_-,\ A_i(\zeta)x-b_i(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q_i\ \forall i=1,\ldots,m,\ \forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision is robust feasible when it satisfies every conic constraint for every perturbation in the prescribed set. The robust counterpart minimizes an epigraph bound on the objective under the same universal perturbation requirement, thereby minimizing the guaranteed worst-case objective value.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^d
x\in\mathbb R^n
c(\zeta),d(\zeta),A_i(\zeta),b_i(\zeta)\text{ are the uncertain conic-program data}
\mathbf Q_i\text{ are the fixed constraint sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is robust feasible}\iff A_i(\zeta)x-b_i(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q_i\quad\forall i=1,\ldots,m,\ \forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z;\qquad \operatorname{RC}=\min_{x,t}\{t:c(\zeta)^Tx+d(\zeta)\le t,\ A_i(\zeta)x-b_i(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q_i\ \forall i,\forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactly Representable Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite SOCP counterpart for scalar interval uncertainty in a conic-quadratic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(y_0,y_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\) be affine maps, and let \(t:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be affine. Then \[\|y_0(x)+u y_1(x)\|_2\le t(x)\quad\text{for every }u\in[-1,1]\] is equivalent to \[\|y_0(x)+y_1(x)\|_2\le t(x),\qquad \|y_0(x)-y_1(x)\|_2\le t(x).\] Thus scalar interval uncertainty in this affine norm expression has an exact finite second-order-cone counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar interval uncertainty in an affine norm expression is represented exactly by enforcing its two endpoint second-order-cone constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(y_0,y_1:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^r\) and \(t:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are affine.
The scalar uncertainty set is \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semi-infinite robust SOC constraint is equivalent to the intersection of the two displayed SOC constraints.

notation.meaning: nominal and uncertain affine vector terms

knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Uncertainty Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment-based bounds for robust conic-quadratic feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq U\subseteq U_{\mathrm{out}}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(A:U_{\mathrm{out}}\to\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(b:U_{\mathrm{out}}\to\mathbb R^r\), \(c:U_{\mathrm{out}}\to\mathbb R^n\), and \(d:U_{\mathrm{out}}\to\mathbb R\). Define \(\phi_x(u)=\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2-c(u)^\top x-d(u)\). Then \[\sup_{u\in U_{\mathrm{in}}}\phi_x(u)\le\sup_{u\in U}\phi_x(u)\le\sup_{u\in U_{\mathrm{out}}}\phi_x(u).\] For \(S\subseteq U_{\mathrm{out}}\), define \(X(S)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\phi_x(u)\le0\text{ for every }u\in S\}\). It follows that \[X(U_{\mathrm{out}})\subseteq X(U)\subseteq X(U_{\mathrm{in}}).\] Thus the outer uncertainty set gives a safe inner approximation of the robust feasible set, while the inner uncertainty set gives an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing uncertainty by a tractable outer set is safely conservative, while replacing it by an inner set relaxes the robust conic-quadratic model.
assumptions_latex: \(U_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq U\subseteq U_{\mathrm{out}}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\).
The displayed suprema are well-defined in the extended real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible sets satisfy \(X(U_{\mathrm{out}})\subseteq X(U)\subseteq X(U_{\mathrm{in}})\).

notation.meaning: conic-quadratic violation at decision x and uncertainty u
decisions feasible for every uncertainty realization in S

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-of-Ellipsoids Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-constraint S-procedure certificate for a quadratic robust implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u:q_k(u)\ge0,\ k=1,\ldots,K\}\), where every \(q_k\) is quadratic and describes an ellipsoid, and suppose robust feasibility reduces to \(q_0(u;x)\ge0\) for all \(u\in U\). A verifiable sufficient certificate is the existence of multipliers \(\lambda_k\ge0\) such that \[q_0(u;x)-\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k q_k(u)\ge0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^p.\] Global nonnegativity of the resulting quadratic is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of its augmented coefficient matrix. For multiple ellipsoids this certificate is generally sufficient but not necessary, hence it defines a conservative semidefinite approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative S-procedure multipliers yield a checkable SDP certificate for robustness over intersecting ellipsoids, but the certificate can be conservative when several ellipsoids are present.
assumptions_latex: Each \(q_k\) and \(q_0(\cdot;x)\) is quadratic in \(u\).
The inequalities \(q_k(u)\ge0\) describe the constituent ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed multiplier condition certifies \(q_0(u;x)\ge0\) on \(U\), without guaranteeing necessity for \(K>1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and sufficiency direction are appropriate, but the multi-constraint S-procedure, PSD representation, and general non-necessity claim require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured LMI Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine uncertain LMIs whose symmetric perturbation directions have no prescribed block or invariant-subspace structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^L\), and let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_L:X\to\mathbb S^m\) be affine. The robust LMI is
\[F(x,u):=F_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^L u_\ell F_\ell(x)\succeq0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\]
The uncertainty is unstructured when the perturbation directions \(F_1(x),\ldots,F_L(x)\) are allowed to be arbitrary symmetric matrices, without a prescribed simultaneous block decomposition, sparsity pattern, or cone-preserving action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstructured robust LMI must remain positive semidefinite for every uncertainty realization, while its symmetric perturbation directions obey no additional structural restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^L\)
\(F_0,\ldots,F_L:X\to\mathbb S^m\) are affine
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is robustly feasible}\iff F_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^L u_\ell F_\ell(x)\succeq0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\)

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order m

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact LMI reformulation under unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust-counterpart reformulation for an uncertain LMI whose nonzero factor R is independent of the decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an uncertain LMI of the unstructured norm-bounded form \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)+L(y)^T\zeta R+R^T\zeta^T L(y)\succeq0\), where \(L(\cdot)\) is affine, \(R\ne0\) is independent of \(y\), and \(\rho\ge0\). Then \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)+L(y)^T\zeta R+R^T\zeta^T L(y)\succeq0\) for every \(\zeta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) with \(\|\zeta\|_{2,2}\le\rho\) if and only if there exists a scalar \(\lambda\) such that \(\begin{bmatrix}\lambda I_p&\rho L(y)\\ \rho L(y)^T&\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)-\lambda R^TR\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unstructured norm-bounded uncertain LMI with a nonzero constant factor R, robust positive semidefiniteness over every perturbation of operator norm at most rho is equivalent to feasibility of the stated finite block LMI in y and an auxiliary scalar lambda.
assumptions_latex: \rho\ge0
\zeta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}
L(\cdot)\text{ is affine}
R\ne0
R\text{ is independent of }y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall\zeta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q},\ \|\zeta\|_{2,2}\le\rho\Rightarrow\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)+L(y)^T\zeta R+R^T\zeta^TL(y)\succeq0\right]\iff\left[\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R:\begin{bmatrix}\lambda I_p&\rho L(y)\\ \rho L(y)^T&\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)-\lambda R^TR\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right].

knowledge_statements.title: Structured LMI Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine uncertain LMIs whose perturbation directions are restricted to a specified matrix subspace or block pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^L\), let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S^m\) be a prescribed linear subspace, and let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_L:X\to\mathbb S^m\) be affine. The robust LMI
\[F(x,u):=F_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^L u_\ell F_\ell(x)\succeq0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\]
has uncertainty structured by \(\mathcal S\) when
\[F_\ell(x)\in\mathcal S\quad\text{for every }x\in X\text{ and }\ell=1,\ldots,L.\]
Consequently, \(F(x,u)-F_0(x)\in\mathcal S\) for every \((x,u)\in X\times\mathcal U\). Typical choices of \(\mathcal S\) impose block-diagonal, sparsity, or repeated-block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured LMI uncertainty requires every uncertain matrix direction to lie in a prescribed subspace, which consequently confines every realized perturbation to that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^L\)
\(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb S^m\) is a prescribed linear subspace
\(F_0,\ldots,F_L:X\to\mathbb S^m\) are affine
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\ell(x)\in\mathcal S\ \forall x\in X,\ \ell=1,\ldots,L\Longrightarrow F(x,u)-F_0(x)\in\mathcal S\ \forall(x,u)\in X\times\mathcal U\)

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order m

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Semidefinite Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner semidefinite-representable approximations of robust LMI feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x,u)\in\mathbb S^m\), define the robust feasible set \(R:=\{x:F(x,u)\succeq0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\}\). A semidefinite-representable set
\[S:=\{x:\exists y\in\mathbb R^r,\ G_0+\mathcal G_x(x)+\mathcal G_y(y)\succeq0\}\]
is a safe semidefinite approximation when every feasible lifted certificate implies the uncertain LMI, namely
\[G_0+\mathcal G_x(x)+\mathcal G_y(y)\succeq0\ \Longrightarrow\ F(x,u)\succeq0\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U.\]
Consequently \(S\subseteq R\), so feasibility in the approximation certifies robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe SDP approximation is an efficiently representable inner approximation: every point it accepts satisfies the original uncertain LMI for all scenarios.
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb S^m\) is given
\(G_0+\mathcal G_x(x)+\mathcal G_y(y)\) is affine in \((x,y)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq R\)

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Preserving Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative uncertainty acting through endomorphisms of the ordering cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone and let \(T_u:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear for each \(u\in\mathcal U\). The uncertainty is cone-preserving when
\[T_u(K)\subseteq K\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U.\]
Hence \(y(x)\in K\) implies \(T_u y(x)\in K\) for every scenario. If some \(u_0\in\mathcal U\) satisfies \(T_{u_0}=I\), then
\[T_u y(x)\in K\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y(x)\in K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone-preserving uncertainty maps every cone element back into the cone. If the identity scenario is included, the corresponding robust conic constraint equals the nominal one.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone
\(T_u\) is linear for every \(u\in\mathcal U\)
\(T_{u_0}=I\) for some \(u_0\in\mathcal U\) for the equivalence
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_u(K)\subseteq K\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\), and with an identity scenario, \(T_u y(x)\in K\ \forall u\iff y(x)\in K\)

knowledge_statements.title: Tractable Conic Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional conic representations of semi-infinite robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a tractable closed convex cone and define
\[R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A(u)x+b(u)\in K\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\}.\]
An exact conic lift of \(R\) consists of a tractable closed convex cone \(Q\), an auxiliary variable \(y\in\mathbb R^r\), and an affine map \(L:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^r\to\operatorname{span}(Q)\) such that
\[x\in R\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists y\in\mathbb R^r:\ L(x,y)\in Q.\]
Relative to a specified input encoding, the lift is polynomial-size when its dimensions and encoding length are bounded polynomially in the input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact tractable conic lift replaces a universally quantified robust conic constraint by an equivalent existential constraint over a tractable cone. Polynomial size is an additional encoding-dependent property of the lift.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a tractable closed convex cone
\(\varnothing\ne\mathcal U\) has a specified finite encoding
\(A(u)x+b(u)\) is affine in \(x\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^r,\ L(x,y)\in Q\}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Intractable Robust-Conic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact tractability when robust conic separation contains a hard global optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the robust constraint \(g(x,u):=A(u)x+b(u)\in K\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\), define
\[v(x):=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\operatorname{dist}(g(x,u),K).\]
Robust feasibility is equivalent to \(v(x)=0\). If computing whether \(v(x)>0\) is NP-hard for a chosen representation class of \(A,b,\mathcal U,K\), then exact robust-feasibility separation for that class is NP-hard. Thus ordinary tractability of membership in \(K\) does not ensure tractability once uncertainty makes the adversarial maximization nonconvex or combinatorial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tractable cone can yield an intractable robust problem when detecting the worst violating scenario requires NP-hard global or combinatorial optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is closed and convex
\(\mathcal U\) is compact
\(g(x,u)=A(u)x+b(u)\) is continuously evaluable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x)=0\iff g(x,u)\in K\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\); hardness of deciding \(v(x)>0\) implies hardness of exact robust separation

notation.meaning: distance from z to K in a fixed norm

knowledge_statements.title: Convex–Concave Robust Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust inequalities convex in decisions and concave in adversarial variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty convex sets, with \(\mathcal U\) compact. Suppose \(f:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R\) is convex in \(x\) for each fixed \(u\), and concave and upper semicontinuous in \(u\) for each fixed \(x\). Then
\[\phi(x):=\max_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\]
is convex on \(X\), and
\[f(x,u)\le0\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\phi(x)\le0.\]
For fixed \(x\), computing \(\phi(x)\) is the maximization of a concave function over a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex decision domain, maximizing a decision-convex and uncertainty-concave constraint over a compact convex uncertainty set produces a convex worst-case function and an equivalent robust inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex
\(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty, compact, and convex
\(f(\cdot,u)\) is convex on \(X\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\)
\(f(x,\cdot)\) is concave and upper semicontinuous on \(\mathcal U\) for every \(x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\text{ is convex on }X,\text{ and }\phi(x)\le0\iff f(x,u)\le0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\)

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Robust Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sum-of-squares certificates for polynomial inequalities over compact basic semialgebraic uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:g_j(u)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\), and assume its quadratic module is Archimedean. For fixed \(x\), strict robust positivity \(p(x,u)>0\) on \(\mathcal U\) admits a certificate
\[p(x,u)=\sigma_0(u)+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_j(u)g_j(u),\]
where every \(\sigma_j\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial. Bounding the degrees of the \(\sigma_jg_j\) gives a semidefinite-representable sufficient condition for \(p(x,u)\ge0\) on \(\mathcal U\); increasing the bound yields a nested hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict polynomial positivity on an Archimedean semialgebraic uncertainty set has an SOS certificate; degree bounds produce nested safe semidefinite approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(p(x,\cdot),g_1,\ldots,g_s\in\mathbb R[u]\)
\(\mathcal U=\{u:g_j(u)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\) is nonempty
\(M(g)\) is Archimedean and \(p(x,u)>0\) on \(\mathcal U\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(x,u)=\sigma_0(u)+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_j(u)g_j(u)\) for sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_j\)

notation.meaning: quadratic module generated by the defining polynomials

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Uncertainty Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A box-uncertain quadratic family exhibiting combinatorial worst-case separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\) be the Laplacian of a weighted undirected graph and let \(\mathcal U=[-1,1]^p\). The robust polynomial inequality
\[t-u^\mathsf TLu\ge0\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U\]
is equivalent to
\[t\ge\max_{u\in[-1,1]^p}u^\mathsf TLu=4\,\operatorname{MaxCut}(L).\]
Because the quadratic is convex, a maximizer over the box exists at a vertex \(u\in\{-1,1\}^p\). Hence allowing nonconcave dependence on uncertainty can make exact robust separation NP-hard, even though the uncertainty set is a simple polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic maximized over box uncertainty encodes maximum cut, showing that nonconcave uncertainty dependence can make robust separation NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is the weighted Laplacian of an undirected graph with nonnegative edge weights
\(\mathcal U=[-1,1]^p\)
\(\operatorname{MaxCut}(L)\) denotes maximum total cut weight
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{u\in[-1,1]^p}u^\mathsf TLu=4\operatorname{MaxCut}(L)\), so deciding robust feasibility is NP-hard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the standard weighted-Laplacian convention, the factor-four Max-Cut identity and vertex maximization argument are correct, but the reduction and NP-hardness conclusion require an inspectable complexity source.

knowledge_statements.title: Min–Max Combinatorial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust combinatorial optimization with worst-case scenario cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be a nonempty family of feasible incidence vectors and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact cost-uncertainty set. The min–max robust combinatorial problem is
\[\min_{x\in X}\ \max_{c\in\mathcal C}c^\mathsf T x.\]
A feasible solution \(x^\star\in X\) is min–max optimal when its worst-case cost satisfies
\[\max_{c\in\mathcal C}c^\mathsf T x^\star\le\max_{c\in\mathcal C}c^\mathsf T x\quad\forall x\in X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a feasible combinatorial object minimizing its largest cost across all scenarios in the cost-uncertainty set.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\)
\(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is compact
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\max_{c\in\mathcal C}c^\mathsf T x\)

knowledge_statements.title: Min–Max-Regret Combinatorial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial optimization minimizing worst-case additive regret relative to each scenario optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be nonempty and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact. For scenario \(c\), define its perfect-information optimum by
\[z(c):=\min_{y\in X}c^\mathsf T y.\]
The additive regret of \(x\in X\) under \(c\) is \(r(x,c):=c^\mathsf T x-z(c)\). The min–max-regret problem is
\[\min_{x\in X}\ \max_{c\in\mathcal C}\bigl(c^\mathsf T x-z(c)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a combinatorial solution minimizing its greatest cost shortfall relative to the solution that would be optimal after observing each scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\)
\(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is compact
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\max_{c\in\mathcal C}\left[c^\mathsf T x-\min_{y\in X}c^\mathsf T y\right]\)

notation.meaning: additive regret of x in scenario c

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Robust Integer Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here-and-now integer decisions followed by scenario-adaptive integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), let \(\mathcal U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set, and define
\[Y(x,u):=\{y\in\mathbb Z^q:W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x\}.\]
With the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), a two-stage robust integer problem is
\[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{c^\mathsf T x+\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\inf_{y\in Y(x,u)}q(u)^\mathsf T y\right\}.\]
The first-stage decision \(x\) is chosen before \(u\) is observed, whereas the recourse decision may depend on \(u\). A first-stage decision is robustly feasible when
\[Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\]
Finiteness of the objective additionally requires the relevant recourse values and their worst-case supremum to be finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer first-stage decision is fixed before uncertainty is observed, after which a scenario-dependent integer recourse decision is selected. Robust feasibility requires feasible recourse in every scenario, while finite objective value requires additional boundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\)
\(\varnothing\ne\mathcal U\)
\(W,T,h,q\) are scenario data of compatible finite dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is robustly feasible}\iff Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\)

notation.meaning: integer recourse feasible set after scenario u

knowledge_statements.title: Recoverable Robust Combinatorial Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage discrete robustness with scenario-dependent, neighborhood-restricted recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the first-stage feasible set, let \(U\) be a scenario set, and let \(F(u)\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the feasible solutions under \(u\in U\). Given a recovery neighborhood \(N(x)\) and costs \(c\) and \(d(u)\), a recoverable robust problem is
\[
\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\sup_{u\in U}\inf_{y\in F(u)\cap N(x)}d(u)^\top y\right\}.
\]
A first-stage solution is recoverably robust when \(F(u)\cap N(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a discrete solution that can be repaired within a prescribed neighborhood after every uncertainty scenario, minimizing first-stage cost plus worst-case optimal recovery cost.
assumptions_latex: \(X,F(u),N(x)\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(U\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is recoverably robust exactly when \(F(u)\cap N(x)\neq\varnothing\) for all \(u\in U\).

notation.meaning: allowed recovery neighborhood of the first-stage solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and optimization model are mathematically coherent and fit the terminal topic, but the cited sections concern general discrete, stochastic, or robust optimization and do not specifically support recoverable robustness, recovery neighborhoods, or the displayed min-sup-inf formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe and Computationally Tractable Convex Approximation of a Scalar Chance Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safety through feasible-set projection and tractability through efficient computability of the constituent convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the scalar chance constraint specified by the prescribed data, and let \(\mathcal S\) be a system of convex constraints in \(x\) and auxiliary variables \(v\). knowledge_statements.title: Basic Robust Counterpart Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe scalar chance approximation obtained from a high-probability uncertainty region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\) have probability law \(P\), let \(g(x,\xi)\) be a scalar constraint function, and fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\). Choose a deterministic uncertainty set \(U_\epsilon\) satisfying \(P(\xi\in U_\epsilon)\ge 1-\epsilon\). The robust-counterpart condition
\[
\sup_{u\in U_\epsilon}g(x,u)\le 0
\]
is a safe approximation of the chance constraint \(P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\epsilon\). Its conservatism depends on the geometry and probability coverage of \(U_\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enforcing a constraint throughout any uncertainty set carrying at least probability one minus epsilon safely implies the corresponding scalar chance constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\).
\(P(\xi\in U_\epsilon)\ge1-\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in U_\epsilon}g(x,u)\le0\Rightarrow P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\epsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation invariance, homogeneity, monotonicity, and subadditivity of the bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of the approximation functional on scalar convex piecewise-linear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed z and f,g\in\mathcal{CL}, the value \Phi[f,z] is independent of the chosen representation of f as a maximum of affine functions. Moreover, for \lambda\geq0, \Phi[\lambda f,z]=\lambda\Phi[f,z]; if f\leq g pointwise, then \Phi[f,z]\leq\Phi[g,z]; and \Phi[f+g,z]\leq\Phi[f,z]+\Phi[g,z].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Budgeted-uncertainty robust counterpart with a probability guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A basic scalar chance-constraint approximation for the uncertain linear-constraint model referenced by (3.1)–(2.16).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $$\mathcal Z=\left\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^L:-1\le\zeta_\ell\le1\ (\ell=1,\ldots,L),\ \sum_{\ell=1}^L|\zeta_\ell|\le\gamma\right\}.$$ For the uncertain linear constraint (3.1)–(2.16), its robust counterpart under $\mathcal Z$ is represented by the existence of $z,w\in\mathbb R^L$ satisfying $$\sum_{\ell=1}^L|z_\ell|+\gamma\max_{1\le\ell\le L}|w_\ell|+(a^0)^Tx\le b^0,$$ $$z_\ell+w_\ell=b^\ell-(a^\ell)^Tx\quad(\ell=1,\ldots,L).$$ Under the random-perturbation assumptions (3.4), the $x$-component of every feasible solution satisfies (3.1) with probability at least $1-\exp(-\gamma^2/(2L))$. In this guarantee, $\gamma/\sqrt L$ plays the same role as $\Omega$ in Proposition 3.2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For componentwise bounded uncertainty with an l1 budget gamma, the robust counterpart has an auxiliary formulation involving the l1 norm of z and gamma times the infinity norm of w. Under the referenced random model, feasibility guarantees probability at least one minus exp(−gamma squared divided by 2L), and gamma divided by square root of L plays the same confidence-parameter role as Omega.

\text{For the probability guarantee, the random perturbations satisfy (3.4).}

knowledge_statements.title: Bernstein Approximation Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chernoff–Bernstein safe condition for a scalar affine chance constraint with independent disturbances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g(x,\xi)=a_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m a_i(x)\xi_i\), where the \(\xi_i\) are independent and \(\Lambda_i(s)=\log\mathbb E[\exp(s\xi_i)]\) is finite at the required arguments. For \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\), the Bernstein condition
\[
\inf_{t>0}\left\{a_0(x)+t\log(1/\epsilon)+t\sum_{i=1}^m\Lambda_i\!\left(a_i(x)/t\right)\right\}\le0
\]
is sufficient for \(P(g(x,\xi)\le0)\ge1-\epsilon\). Using tractable upper bounds on the cumulant-generating functions yields conservative members of the same family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chernoff bound converts an affine scalar chance constraint into a deterministic minimization involving the disturbances’ cumulant-generating functions.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m\) are independent.
\(\Lambda_i(a_i(x)/t)<\infty\) for the candidate \(t>0\).
\(\epsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Bernstein condition implies \(P(g(x,\xi)>0)\le\epsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint-product representation of the Bernstein approximation functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the source-defined functional using sign-dependent two-point marginal distributions and records an efficiently computable specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the source-defined family \(\mathcal P\) and every \(\gamma\) satisfying (5.18),
\[
\Psi_{\mathcal P}(z)=\mathbf E_{\zeta\sim P^z}\!\left[\gamma\!\left(z_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell z_\ell\right)\right],
\qquad P^z=P_1^{z_1}\times\cdots\times P_L^{z_L},
\]
where \(P_\ell^s\) is supported on \(\{-1,1\}\) and
\[
P_\ell^s\{1\}=1-P_\ell^s\{-1\}=\begin{cases}
(1+\mu_\ell^+)/2,&s\geq0,\\
(1+\mu_\ell^-)/2,&s<0.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular, when \(\gamma=\gamma_{d,T}\), the function \(\Psi_{\mathcal P}(z)\) is efficiently computable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the source-defined family, the functional equals an expectation under a product distribution whose coordinates lie at minus one and one, with endpoint probabilities chosen according to the signs of the corresponding components of z. With the generating function gamma d,T, the functional is efficiently computable.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\text{ is the source-defined family}
\gamma\text{ satisfies condition (5.18)}
P^z=P_1^{z_1}\times\cdots\times P_L^{z_L}
P_\ell^s\text{ has the stated two-point distribution on }\{-1,1\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi_{\mathcal P}(z)=\mathbf E_{\zeta\sim P^z}\!\left[\gamma\!\left(z_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell z_\ell\right)\right],\qquad \gamma=\gamma_{d,T}\Longrightarrow\Psi_{\mathcal P}(z)\text{ is efficiently computable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust-Counterpart Representation of the Bernstein Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty-set interpretation of the Bernstein safe approximation for a scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\epsilon<1\). Assume \(\log\mathbb{E}[\exp(w^T\zeta)]\leq\Phi(w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^L\), where \(\Phi\) is convex, finite everywhere, and satisfies \(\Phi(0)=0\), and suppose \[\Phi(w)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^M}\{w^T(Au+a)-\phi(u)\},\] where \(\phi\) is convex and lower semicontinuous and every real sublevel set of \(\phi\) is bounded. Define \[\mathcal U_\epsilon=\{u:\phi(u)\leq\log(1/\epsilon)\},\qquad \mathcal Z_\epsilon=A\mathcal U_\epsilon+a.\] Then \(\mathcal U_\epsilon\) is nonempty, convex, and compact, and \[ (z_0,w)\in Z_\epsilon\iff z_0+\xi^Tw\leq0\quad\forall\xi\in\mathcal Z_\epsilon. \] Thus the Bernstein condition is robust feasibility of the uncertain linear inequality over \(\mathcal Z_\epsilon\), and it is sufficient for the associated chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the two Bernstein assumptions, the relevant sublevel set of phi is nonempty, convex, and compact. Its affine image is an uncertainty set over which robust feasibility is equivalent to membership in the Bernstein approximation set and therefore safely implies the chance constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\epsilon<1\).
\(\log\mathbb{E}[\exp(w^T\zeta)]\leq\Phi(w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^L\), with \(\Phi\) convex, finite everywhere, and \(\Phi(0)=0\).
\(\Phi(w)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^M}\{w^T(Au+a)-\phi(u)\}\).
\(\phi\) is convex and lower semicontinuous, and each real sublevel set \(\{u:\phi(u)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_\epsilon\) is nonempty, convex, and compact, and \((z_0,w)\in Z_\epsilon\iff z_0+\xi^Tw\leq0\) for every \(\xi\in A\mathcal U_\epsilon+a\); this robust-feasibility condition is sufficient for the associated chance constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diffuseness Majorization Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the distributional order used by majorization-based scalar chance-constraint approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p,q\in\mathcal P\), define \(q\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm m}p\) by \[q\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm m}p\iff \forall a\geq0:\ \int_a^\infty p(s)\,ds\leq\int_a^\infty q(s)\,ds.\] For \(\xi,\eta\in\Pi\), define \(\eta\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm m}\xi\) when their corresponding densities satisfy the same relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The density q is more diffuse than p when every upper-tail integral beginning at a nonnegative threshold is at least as large for q as for p. Random variables in Pi inherit this order from their densities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral Characterization of Diffuseness Majorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes diffuseness majorization using integrals of even functions that are nondecreasing on the nonnegative axis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_b\) be the family of bounded, continuously differentiable, even functions on \(\mathbb R\) that are nondecreasing on \(\mathbb R_+\). For \(p,q\in\mathcal P\), \[q\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm m}p\iff \forall f\in\mathcal M_b:\ \int f(s)q(s)\,ds\geq\int f(s)p(s)\,ds.\] Moreover, whenever this condition holds, the same inequality holds for every even function on \(\mathbb R\) that is nondecreasing on \(\mathbb R_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density q is more diffuse than p exactly when q gives at least as large an integral for every bounded, continuously differentiable, even function that increases on the nonnegative axis. Under this condition, the inequality extends to every even function increasing there.
assumptions_latex: p,q\in\mathcal P
\mathcal M_b=\{f:f\text{ is bounded, continuously differentiable, even, and nondecreasing on }\mathbb R_+\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm m}p\iff\left(\forall f\in\mathcal M_b:\int f(s)q(s)\,ds\geq\int f(s)p(s)\,ds\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic-dual safe approximation of an ambiguous scalar chance constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient explicit convex constraints for a scalar distributionally ambiguous chance constraint when the associated uncertainty set has a strictly feasible conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z_\xi=\{\xi:\exists u,\ P\xi+Qu+p\in\mathbf K\}\) admit a strictly feasible conic representation; if \(\mathbf K\) is polyhedral, feasibility suffices. Let \(\mathcal Z_\eta^\epsilon\) be computationally tractable, convex, and compact, with \(f(z)=\max_{\eta\in\mathcal Z_\eta^\epsilon}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell z_\ell\), and assume \(z_0+f(z)\le0\) implies \(\Pr_{\eta\sim\mathbb P}\{z_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell z_\ell\le0\}\ge1-\epsilon\) for every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal P\). If \(x\) extends to \(y,t\) satisfying \(p^Ty+(a^0)^Tx-b^0\le t\), \(Q^Ty=0\), \((P^Ty)_\ell+(a^\ell)^Tx=b^\ell\) for \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\), \(y\in\mathbf K_*:=\{y:y^Tv\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathbf K\}\), and \(t+f((a^1)^Tx-b^1,\ldots,(a^L)^Tx-b^L)\le0\), then \(x\) satisfies the associated ambiguous scalar chance constraint for every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Suppose the associated uncertainty set has a strictly feasible conic representation, with feasibility sufficient for a polyhedral cone, and a tractable compact convex set supplies a robust inequality that safely implies the required probability bound for every distribution in the ambiguity family. Then feasibility of the displayed conic-dual convex system is sufficient for the decision x to satisfy the associated ambiguous scalar chance constraint under every distribution in that family.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Z_\xi=\{\xi:\exists u,\ P\xi+Qu+p\in\mathbf K\}\) has a strictly feasible conic representation; feasibility suffices if \(\mathbf K\) is polyhedral.
\(\mathcal Z_\eta^\epsilon\) is computationally tractable, convex, and compact, and \(f(z)=\max_{\eta\in\mathcal Z_\eta^\epsilon}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell z_\ell\).
\(\forall(z_0,z),\ z_0+f(z)\le0\Rightarrow\forall\mathbb P\in\mathcal P,\ \Pr_{\eta\sim\mathbb P}\{z_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell z_\ell\le0\}\ge1-\epsilon\).

There exist \(y,t\) such that \(p^Ty+(a^0)^Tx-b^0\le t\), \(Q^Ty=0\), \((P^Ty)_\ell+(a^\ell)^Tx=b^\ell\) for every \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\), \(y\in\mathbf K_*\), and \(t+f((a^1)^Tx-b^1,\ldots,(a^L)^Tx-b^L)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\mathbb P\in\mathcal P,\quad \Pr_{\eta\sim\mathbb P}\!\left\{\left[a^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell a^\ell\right]^Tx\le b^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\eta_\ell b^\ell\right\}\ge1-\epsilon.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Quadratic Chance Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order-cone representation of a scalar Gaussian affine chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)\), let \(a(x)\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). The scalar Gaussian chance constraint
\[
P\bigl(a(x)^\top\xi\le b(x)\bigr)\ge1-\epsilon
\]
is equivalent to the conic-quadratic constraint
\[
\mu^\top a(x)+\Phi^{-1}(1-\epsilon)\left\|\Sigma^{1/2}a(x)\right\|_2\le b(x).
\]
For non-Gaussian laws, replacing the Gaussian quantile by a valid distributional tail factor gives a safe, generally conservative second-order-cone approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian affine chance constraint equals a second-order-cone inequality involving its mean, standard deviation, and the normal quantile.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)\) with \(\Sigma\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chance constraint is equivalent to the displayed second-order-cone constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Gaussian Tail Bound for an Affine Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An extraction-grounded Gaussian exceedance bound supporting safe conic-quadratic chance-constraint approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G,\rho\ge 0\) and define
\[
\Omega=\frac{\tau_*^2}{\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)\left[\max_{s\in\mathcal S}s^T(GA-I)^T(GA-I)s+\rho^2\operatorname{Tr}(G^TG)\right]}.
\]
If \(\Omega\ge1\), then for every \(s\in\mathcal S\),
\[
\Pr_{\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,I)}\!\left(\left\|(GA-I)s+\rho G\zeta\right\|_2>\tau_*\right)
\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{\Omega-1-\ln\Omega}{2}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If G and rho satisfy the stated nonnegativity condition and the normalized threshold parameter Omega is at least one, then, for every s in S, the probability that the Euclidean norm of (GA−I)s+rho G zeta exceeds tau_* is at most exp(−(Omega−1−ln Omega)/2).
assumptions_latex: G,\rho\ge 0
\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,I)
\Omega=\frac{\tau_*^2}{\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)\left[\max_{s\in\mathcal S}s^T(GA-I)^T(GA-I)s+\rho^2\operatorname{Tr}(G^TG)\right]}
\Omega\ge1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall s\in\mathcal S:\quad \Pr_{\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,I)}\left\{\left\|(GA-I)s+\rho G\zeta\right\|_2>\tau_*\right\}\le \exp\left(-\frac{\Omega-1-\ln\Omega}{2}\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Chance-Constrained LMI Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian Bernstein safe approximation for a quadratic chance constraint using SOC and LMI constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)\), let \(A=A^\top\), and fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\). The existence of \(s,t\ge0\) satisfying
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A)+\sqrt{2\log(1/\epsilon)}s+\log(1/\epsilon)t+c\le0,
\]
\[
\sqrt{\|A\|_F^2+2\|b\|_2^2}\le s,\qquad tI_m-A\succeq0
\]
is a tractable sufficient condition for
\[
P\bigl(z^\top Az+2b^\top z+c\le0\bigr)\ge1-\epsilon.
\]
The last inequality is a linear matrix inequality controlling the positive spectral part of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian quadratic chance constraint admits a safe Bernstein approximation combining a norm bound, a trace inequality, and a linear matrix inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(z\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)\).
\(\epsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility of the displayed SOC–LMI system implies the quadratic chance constraint.

notation.meaning: Frobenius norm of the quadratic coefficient matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed SOC-LMI system matches a standard Gaussian quadratic Bernstein safe condition, and condition fits the terminal container. However, the generic chance-constraint section does not presently establish the exact trace, Frobenius-norm, spectral, and logarithmic constants; because those constants determine validity, an authoritative exact formula locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distributional representation of averaged pointwise worst-case loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a samplewise robust objective as a worst-case expectation over probability measures satisfying finite union-mass constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given f:\mathbb R^{m+1}\to\mathbb R and Borel sets \mathfrak Z_1,\ldots,\mathfrak Z_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+1}, define
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{\mu\in\mathcal P:\mu\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in S}\mathfrak Z_i\right)\ge \frac{|S|}{n}\quad\forall S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sup_{(\mathbf x_i,y_i)\in\mathfrak Z_i}f(\mathbf x_i,y_i)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal P_n}\int_{\mathbb R^{m+1}}f(\mathbf x,y)\,d\mu(\mathbf x,y).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The average of the pointwise worst values over the uncertainty sets equals the worst expected value over probability measures that assign at least |S|/n mass to every selected union of sets.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^{m+1}\to\mathbb R
\mathfrak Z_1,\ldots,\mathfrak Z_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+1}\text{ are Borel sets}
\mathcal P_n=\left\{\mu\in\mathcal P:\mu(\bigcup_{i\in S}\mathfrak Z_i)\ge |S|/n\ \forall S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\right\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sup_{z\in\mathfrak Z_i}f(z)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal P_n}\int f\,d\mu.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Expectation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static distributionally robust objective over an ambiguity set of probability laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty set of probability measures on a measurable uncertainty space, and let \(\ell(x,\xi)\) be integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\). A worst-case expectation model has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)].
\]
The inner supremum evaluates a fixed decision against the most adverse distribution admitted by \(\mathcal P\); infinite values are allowed unless uniform integrability or growth restrictions exclude them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a decision minimizing expected loss under the most adverse probability distribution contained in a prescribed ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\neq\varnothing\).
\(\ell(x,\cdot)\) is measurable for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust objective is \(x\mapsto\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical definition of a static distributionally robust worst-case expectation model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The static worst-case expectation formulation is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriately classified as a definition, but it has no source reference. Standard-field rationale alone cannot satisfy the requested citation review.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Constraint Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation constraints required to hold uniformly over an ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a decision set, \(\mathcal P\) a nonempty ambiguity set of probability laws, and \(g_j:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) measurable for \(j=1,\ldots,J\). A distributionally robust expectation-constrained model imposes
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[g_j(x,\xi)]\le0,\qquad j=1,\ldots,J,
\]
together with \(x\in X\). Thus every admissible distribution satisfies each expected constraint. The formulation is well-defined in the extended-real sense; tractable models normally impose moment, support, or growth conditions ensuring finite worst-case expectations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributionally robust constraint requires each expected constraint to hold under every probability law in the ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\neq\varnothing\).
\(g_j(x,\cdot)\) is measurable for every \(x\in X\) and \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires \(\mathbb E_P[g_j(x,\xi)]\le0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\) and every \(j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical distributionally robust expectation-constraint definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform worst-case expectation constraints correctly define the stated subclass of distributionally robust constraint models, and definition fits the leaf. No inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Chance Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chance feasibility required uniformly over every distribution in an ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a nonempty ambiguity set, let \(g:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be measurable in uncertainty, and let \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\). A distributionally robust chance constraint is
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}P\bigl(g(x,\xi)\le0\bigr)\ge1-\epsilon.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P\bigl(g(x,\xi)>0\bigr)\le\epsilon.
\]
Hence a feasible decision controls the violation probability at level \(\epsilon\) simultaneously for all probability laws admitted by \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The probability of constraint violation must not exceed epsilon under any distribution belonging to the ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\neq\varnothing\).
\(g(x,\cdot)\) is measurable for every \(x\in X\).
\(\epsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}P(g(x,\xi)>0)\le\epsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two displayed probability conditions are equivalent and correctly define a distributionally robust chance constraint. The cited source locator concerns ordinary chance constraints, however, and does not establish the ambiguity-set infimum or worst-case violation formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Distributionally Robust Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipative multistage optimization against ambiguous conditional probability kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(h_t=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t)\) be the observed history and let \(x_t(h_t)\) be a nonanticipative policy. Given a rectangular family \(\mathfrak P\) of joint laws generated by conditional kernels \(P_t(\cdot\mid h_{t-1})\in\mathcal P_t(h_{t-1})\), a multistage distributionally robust model is
\[
\inf_{x\in\Pi}\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P}\mathbb E_P\left[\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(x_t(h_t),\xi_t)\right],
\]
subject to history-wise feasibility. Rectangularity permits the adversary to select admissible conditional kernels consistently at every history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonanticipative policy minimizes total expected cost against adverse conditional distributions selected from stagewise ambiguity sets along every history.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
\(x_t\) is measurable with respect to information available at stage \(t\).
\(\mathfrak P\) is generated by the specified conditional ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model optimizes over nonanticipative policies against the worst joint law in \(\mathfrak P\).

notation.meaning: multistage ambiguity set of joint laws

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical-Centered Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity sets defined as probability-law balls around the empirical distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(\widehat\xi_1,\ldots,\widehat\xi_N\in\Xi\), define the empirical law \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}\). For a distance or divergence \(D\) on probability measures and radius \(\rho\ge0\), an empirical-centered neighborhood is
\[
\mathcal P_{N,\rho}=\{P\in\mathcal M(\Xi):D(P,\widehat P_N)\le\rho\}.
\]
Choices such as Wasserstein distance, total variation, or statistical divergence produce different ambiguity models. At \(\rho=0\), the set reduces to the empirical law whenever \(D(P,Q)=0\) implies \(P=Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empirical-centered ambiguity set contains all probability laws within a chosen distance or divergence radius of the empirical distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is defined on the relevant probability measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{N,\rho}=\{P:D(P,\widehat P_N)\le\rho\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity over probabilities assigned to fixed observed sample locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For observations \(\widehat\xi_1,\ldots,\widehat\xi_N\in\Xi\), let
\[
\Delta_N=\left\{w\in\mathbb R_+^N:\sum_{i=1}^N w_i=1\right\},
\]
and let \(W\subseteq\Delta_N\) be a nonempty admissible set of weights. The corresponding sample-weight ambiguity set is
\[
\mathcal P_W=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N w_i\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}:w\in W\right\}.
\]
Thus the support locations remain fixed at the observations while their probability masses vary over \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample-weight ambiguity fixes the observed support points but allows their probability weights to vary within a prescribed nonempty subset of the probability simplex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observations \(\widehat\xi_1,\ldots,\widehat\xi_N\in S\), define the support-augmented empirical ambiguity set by \[\mathcal P_{N,S}(\varepsilon):=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P(S)=1,\ D(P,\widehat P_N)\le\varepsilon\right\},\qquad \widehat P_N:=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}.\] Thus every admissible distribution is concentrated on \(S\) and lies within discrepancy radius \(\varepsilon\) of the empirical law. The definition is meaningful for any specified discrepancy \(D\); its statistical and computational properties depend on that choice.

children.top_down_role: Ambiguity-set structure based on information about distributional means.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is Borel measurable and every considered distribution has a finite first moment.
\(M\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a prescribed nonempty set of admissible means.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_M=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\int_\Xi \xi\,P(d\xi)\in M\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Mean of the random vector under distribution P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact means arise by taking \(M\) to be a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a probability measure \(P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\) with finite first moment, its mean information is the constraint \[\mu(P):=\int_\Xi \xi\,P(d\xi)\in M.\] The corresponding mean-based ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_M:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\int_\Xi \xi\,P(d\xi)\in M\right\}.\] In particular, exact mean information \(\mu(P)=\mu_0\) is represented by \(M=\{\mu_0\}\), while a non-singleton \(M\) represents uncertain or estimated mean information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean information restricts an admissible distribution by requiring its expected random vector to lie in a specified set.
knowledge_statements.title: Mean Information

children.title: Covariance Information
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity-set structure based on information about covariance.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central second-moment information with exact or set-valued covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\) with finite second moment, define \[\Sigma(P):=\int_\Xi (\xi-\mu(P))(\xi-\mu(P))^\top P(d\xi).\] Covariance information requires \(\Sigma(P)\in\mathcal C\), giving the ambiguity set \[\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\Sigma(P)\in\mathcal C\right\}.\] Exact covariance information is obtained by taking \(\mathcal C=\{\Sigma_0\}\) for a prescribed matrix \(\Sigma_0\in\mathbb S_+^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance information restricts the centered second-moment matrix of each admissible distribution to a prescribed positive-semidefinite matrix set.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a probability measure on a Borel set \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) with finite second moment.
\(\mu(P)=\int_\Xi\xi\,P(d\xi)\), and \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb S_+^d\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_{\mathcal C}=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\Sigma(P)\in\mathcal C\}.\]

notation.meaning: Cone of symmetric positive-semidefinite d-by-d matrices

children.title: Mean–Covariance Coupling
children.top_down_role: Joint restrictions linking first-moment and second-moment information.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a probability measure on \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) with finite second moment.
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_+^d\) is a prescribed nonempty joint uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_K=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):(\mu(P),\Sigma(P))\in K\}.\]

notation.meaning: Joint admissible set for mean and covariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint, rather than independent, restrictions on the first two moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu(P):=\int_\Xi\xi\,P(d\xi)\) and \(\Sigma(P):=\int_\Xi(\xi-\mu(P))(\xi-\mu(P))^\top P(d\xi)\). Mean-covariance coupling is imposed through a joint set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_+^d\): \[\mathcal P_K:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):(\mu(P),\Sigma(P))\in K\right\}.\] When \(K=M\times\mathcal C\), the restrictions are uncoupled. A nonproduct \(K\) encodes admissibility of each covariance conditional on the associated mean and cannot generally be replaced by separate marginal restrictions without enlarging the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean-covariance coupling requires the mean and covariance induced by a distribution to belong jointly to one admissible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Mean–Covariance Coupling

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal B)\) is measurable, and \(g_j:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) are measurable and integrable under every considered distribution.
\(l_j,u_j\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(l_j\le u_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_g=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):l_j\le\int_\Xi g_j(\xi)\,P(d\xi)\le u_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite families of equality or inequality constraints on expectations of measurable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given measurable functions \(g_1,\ldots,g_m:\Xi\to\mathbb R\), generalized moment information defines \[\mathcal P_g:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):l_j\le\int_\Xi g_j(\xi)\,P(d\xi)\le u_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\] Equality information \(\int_\Xi g_j(\xi)P(d\xi)=b_j\) is the special case \(l_j=u_j=b_j\). Ordinary raw moments result from polynomial \(g_j\), while indicators, piecewise-linear functions, or other integrable functions encode probabilities and generalized features.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized moment information bounds or fixes expectations of specified measurable functions under every admissible distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Moment Information

children.title: Support Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on the admissible support of probability distributions.

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal B)\) is a measurable space and \(S\in\mathcal B\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_S=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P(S)=1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional support is interpreted as concentration on a prescribed measurable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hard support restriction associated with a measurable set \(S\subseteq\Xi\) is \[P(S)=1.\] It defines the class \[\mathcal P_S:=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P(S)=1\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(P(\Xi\setminus S)=0\). This condition asserts concentration on \(S\); it does not require every point of \(S\) to belong to the topological support of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support restriction requires every admissible distribution to assign probability one to a prescribed measurable region.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Restrictions

children.title: Moment Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on admissible distributional moments.

assumptions_latex: \(g_j:\Xi\to\mathbb R\) are measurable and integrable under every considered probability measure.
\(B\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a prescribed nonempty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\left(\int g_1\,dP,\ldots,\int g_m\,dP\right)\in B\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Vector of generalized moments under P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-valued generalized-moment predicate used in support-moment ambiguity sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the generalized-moment map \[G(P):=\left(\int_\Xi g_1(\xi)\,P(d\xi),\ldots,\int_\Xi g_m(\xi)\,P(d\xi)\right).\] A moment restriction is the predicate \(G(P)\in B\), and the induced class is \[\mathcal P_B:=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):G(P)\in B\}.\] Componentwise lower and upper bounds correspond to a box \(B\), whereas affine equalities and inequalities correspond to a polyhedral \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment restrictions require the vector of specified expectations to lie in an admissible set such as a box or polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment Restrictions

children.title: Support–Moment Intersection Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometry induced by imposing support restrictions together with moment restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\Xi\) is measurable, \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are integrable on the relevant measures, and \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal P_{S,B}=\mathcal P_S\cap\mathcal P_B=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P(S)=1,\ G(P)\in B\}.\]

notation.meaning: Probability measures satisfying the moment restrictions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection representation and its immediate nonemptiness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(P):=(\int g_1\,dP,\ldots,\int g_m\,dP)\). The joint support-moment ambiguity set has the intersection representation \[\mathcal P_{S,B}:=\mathcal P_S\cap\mathcal P_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P(S)=1,\ G(P)\in B\right\}.\] If \(\mathcal M(S):=\{G(P):P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi),\ P(S)=1\}\) denotes the support-attainable moment region, then \[\mathcal P_{S,B}\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B\cap\mathcal M(S)\ne\varnothing.\] Thus feasibility is governed by the intersection of prescribed and support-attainable moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined ambiguity set is the intersection of support-feasible and moment-feasible distributions; it is nonempty exactly when their attainable moment regions intersect.
knowledge_statements.title: Support–Moment Intersection Geometry

assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,d)\) is Polish, \(p\in[1,\infty)\), and the center \(P_0\) has finite \(p\)-th moment.
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal B_{W_p}(P_0,\varepsilon)=\{P\in\mathcal P_p(\Xi):W_p(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\}.\]

notation.meaning: Probability measures with finite p-th moment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static \(p\)-Wasserstein ball on a Polish metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P,Q\in\mathcal P_p(\Xi)\), define \[W_p(P,Q):=\left(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}d(\xi,\zeta)^p\,\pi(d\xi,d\zeta)\right)^{1/p}.\] The Wasserstein ambiguity set of radius \(\varepsilon\) centered at \(P_0\) is \[\mathcal B_{W_p}(P_0,\varepsilon):=\left\{P\in\mathcal P_p(\Xi):W_p(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\right\}.\] When \(P_0\) is empirical, this set permits probability mass to move away from observed samples while charging transportation distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wasserstein ambiguity set contains all finite-moment distributions whose optimal transportation distance from a reference distribution does not exceed a radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The static p-Wasserstein definition is standard and precise, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\) is Polish and \(c:\Xi\times\Xi\to[0,\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous.
\(P_0\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and at least one finite-cost coupling exists for each admitted distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal B_c(P_0,\varepsilon)=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\mathsf T_c(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\}.\]

notation.meaning: Optimal transport value with ground cost c
Set of couplings of P and Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static ambiguity sets induced by a general lower-semicontinuous transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For probability measures \(P,Q\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\), the optimal-transport cost generated by \(c\) is \[\mathsf T_c(P,Q):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}c(\xi,\zeta)\,\pi(d\xi,d\zeta).\] The associated ambiguity set centered at \(P_0\) is \[\mathcal B_c(P_0,\varepsilon):=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\mathsf T_c(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\right\}.\] Unlike a Wasserstein distance, \(\mathsf T_c\) need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality unless the ground cost has additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general transport-cost ambiguity set bounds the minimum expected ground cost needed to couple an admissible distribution with a reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: General Optimal-Transport Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general transport-cost construction is plausible and fits the leaf, but no source verifies the formulation or the selected assumptions on the extended-valued cost.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi=\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_T\) with each \(\Xi_t\) Polish, and \(P,Q\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\).
\(c_t:\Xi_{1:t}\times\Xi_{1:t}\to[0,\infty]\) are measurable stage costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nest}}(P_0,\varepsilon)=\{P:\mathsf T_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\}.\]

notation.meaning: Set of bicausal couplings of two process laws

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multistage process-law ambiguity using bicausal transport couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,Q)\) be the couplings of \(P\) and \(Q\) that are causal in both directions with respect to the canonical filtrations. Define \[\mathsf T_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,Q):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(\xi_{1:t},\zeta_{1:t})\,\pi(d\xi,d\zeta).\] A nested transport ambiguity set is \[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nest}}(P_0,\varepsilon):=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):\mathsf T_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,P_0)\le\varepsilon\right\}.\] The bicausality restriction preserves the temporal information structure when comparing process laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested transport ambiguity bounds transport cost between process laws while restricting couplings to respect information revealed through time.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Transport Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bicausal formulation is a plausible interpretation of nested transport ambiguity, but the title does not uniquely determine this version and no source supports its coupling or stage-cost formulation.

assumptions_latex: \(P,Q\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi)\), with \(P\ll Q\).
\(\phi:[0,\infty)\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and satisfies \(\phi(1)=0\); \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal B_\phi(Q,\rho)=\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P\ll Q,\ D_\phi(P\|Q)\le\rho\}.\]

notation.meaning: Radon-Nikodym density of P relative to Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolutely continuous probability measures; extended divergences with singular mass are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\ll Q\), define the \(\phi\)-divergence \[D_\phi(P\|Q):=\int_\Xi \phi\!\left(\frac{dP}{dQ}\right)dQ.\] The radius-\(\rho\) divergence ambiguity set centered at \(Q\) is \[\mathcal B_\phi(Q,\rho):=\left\{P\in\mathcal M_1(\Xi):P\ll Q,\ D_\phi(P\|Q)\le\rho\right\}.\] Convexity of \(\phi\) and \(\phi(1)=0\) imply \(D_\phi(P\|Q)\ge0\) by Jensen's inequality, and \(Q\in\mathcal B_\phi(Q,\rho)\) for every \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phi-divergence ball contains distributions absolutely continuous with respect to a reference law whose convex density-ratio divergence is at most a radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Phi-Divergence Balls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolutely continuous phi-divergence ball is mathematically coherent and properly scoped, but it has no citation or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Entropy Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kullback–Leibler ball centered at a nominal probability law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, let \(P_0\) be a probability measure, and let \(\rho\ge 0\). The relative-entropy ambiguity set centered at \(P_0\) is \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0,\rho)=\left\{Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi):Q\ll P_0,\ D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\Vert P_0)\le\rho\right\},\] where \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\Vert P_0)=\int_\Xi \log\!\left(\frac{dQ}{dP_0}\right)dQ.\] Equivalently, if \(q=dQ/dP_0\), then the constraint is \(\int_\Xi q\log q\,dP_0\le\rho\), with \(0\log 0=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ambiguity set contains probability laws absolutely continuous with respect to the nominal law whose Kullback–Leibler divergence from it does not exceed the radius.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
\(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) and \(\rho\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0,\rho)=\{Q\ll P_0:D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q\Vert P_0)\le\rho\}\).

notation.meaning: Kullback–Leibler divergence of Q from P0
