knowledge_statements.title: Chi-Square Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pearson chi-square divergence ball about a nominal law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, \(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\), and \(\rho\ge0\). The Pearson chi-square ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_{\chi^2}(P_0,\rho)=\left\{Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi):Q\ll P_0,\ \chi^2(Q\Vert P_0)\le\rho\right\},\] where \[\chi^2(Q\Vert P_0)=\int_\Xi\left(\frac{dQ}{dP_0}-1\right)^2dP_0.\] Thus, writing \(q=dQ/dP_0\), feasible likelihood ratios satisfy \(q\ge0\), \(\int_\Xi q\,dP_0=1\), and \(\int_\Xi(q-1)^2dP_0\le\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This ambiguity set bounds the nominal mean squared deviation of a candidate law’s likelihood ratio from one.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
\(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) and \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\chi^2}(P_0,\rho)=\{Q\ll P_0:\chi^2(Q\Vert P_0)\le\rho\}\).

notation.meaning: candidate likelihood ratio relative to the nominal law

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Variation Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-variation ball using the supremum-over-events convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, let \(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\), and let \(\rho\in[0,1]\). Define \[d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,P_0)=\sup_{A\in\mathcal F}|Q(A)-P_0(A)|.\] The total-variation ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0,\rho)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi):d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,P_0)\le\rho\}.\] If \(Q\) and \(P_0\) admit densities \(q\) and \(p_0\) with respect to a common dominating measure \(\mu\), then \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,P_0)=\tfrac12\int_\Xi|q-p_0|\,d\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The set contains all probability laws whose probabilities differ from the nominal law by at most the radius on every measurable event.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
\(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) and \(\rho\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0,\rho)=\{Q:d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,P_0)\le\rho\}\).

notation.meaning: total-variation distance under the supremum-over-events convention

knowledge_statements.title: Kolmogorov-Type Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate Kolmogorov-distance ball around a nominal distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be a probability law on \(\mathbb R\), with cumulative distribution function \(F_0(t)=P_0(({-\infty},t])\), and let \(\rho\in[0,1]\). For any probability law \(Q\) on \(\mathbb R\), write \(F_Q(t)=Q(({-\infty},t])\). The Kolmogorov-type ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_K(P_0,\rho)=\left\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R):\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F_Q(t)-F_0(t)|\le\rho\right\}.\] Equivalently, every feasible cumulative distribution function lies pointwise between \(\max\{0,F_0-\rho\}\) and \(\min\{1,F_0+\rho\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate univariate laws are admitted when their cumulative distribution functions remain uniformly within the specified radius of the nominal CDF.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_K(P_0,\rho)=\{Q:\|F_Q-F_0\|_\infty\le\rho\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Mean-Embedding Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-mean-discrepancy ball induced by a reproducing kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k:\Xi\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be a measurable positive-definite kernel with reproducing kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_k\). For every probability law \(Q\) satisfying \(\int_\Xi\sqrt{k(x,x)}\,dQ(x)<\infty\), define its kernel mean embedding by \(\mu_Q=\int_\Xi k(x,\cdot)\,dQ(x)\in\mathcal H_k\). Given a nominal law \(P_0\) with an existing embedding and \(\rho\ge0\), the kernel mean-embedding ambiguity set is \[\mathcal P_k(P_0,\rho)=\{Q:\|\mu_Q-\mu_{P_0}\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le\rho\}.\] The displayed norm is the maximum mean discrepancy between \(Q\) and \(P_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ambiguity set contains laws whose RKHS mean embeddings lie within a prescribed norm radius of the nominal embedding.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a measurable positive-definite kernel with RKHS \(\mathcal H_k\).
The kernel mean embeddings of \(Q\) and \(P_0\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_k(P_0,\rho)=\{Q:\operatorname{MMD}_k(Q,P_0)\le\rho\}\).

children.title: Contamination Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Distribution families allowing a bounded contamination component.

knowledge_statements.title: Contamination Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Huber contamination neighborhood of a fixed nominal distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space, let \(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\), and choose \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\). The \(\varepsilon\)-contamination neighborhood of \(P_0\) is \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_0,\varepsilon)=\left\{(1-\varepsilon)P_0+\varepsilon H:H\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\right\}.\] Thus each candidate law retains a fixed mass \(1-\varepsilon\) from the nominal distribution, while the remaining mass may follow an arbitrary contaminating law \(H\). For \(\varepsilon=0\), the neighborhood is the singleton \(\{P_0\}\); for \(\varepsilon=1\), it is \(\mathcal P(\Xi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contamination neighborhood mixes a fixed nominal law with an arbitrary contaminating law using a prescribed contamination fraction.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
\(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) and \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_0,\varepsilon)=\{(1-\varepsilon)P_0+\varepsilon H:H\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Mixture Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity generated by finitely many component-law families and admissible weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Xi,\mathcal F)\) be a measurable space. For \(j=1,\ldots,m\), let \(\mathcal Q_j\subseteq\mathcal P(\Xi)\) be a nonempty family of component laws, and let \(W\subseteq\Delta_m\) be a nonempty set of admissible mixture weights, where \(\Delta_m=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^m:\sum_{j=1}^m w_j=1\}\). The associated finite-mixture ambiguity family is \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{mix}}(W;\mathcal Q_1,\ldots,\mathcal Q_m)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^m w_jQ_j:w\in W,\ Q_j\in\mathcal Q_j\right\}.\] If every \(\mathcal Q_j\) is a singleton, only the mixing weights are ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-mixture family consists of convex combinations of finitely many admissible component distributions with weights drawn from a specified subset of the simplex.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and each \(\mathcal Q_j\subseteq\mathcal P(\Xi)\) is nonempty.
\(W\subseteq\Delta_m\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{mix}}=\{\sum_{j=1}^m w_jQ_j:w\in W,\ Q_j\in\mathcal Q_j\}\).

children.title: Contamination–Mixture Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between contamination neighborhoods and mixture representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Contamination–Mixture Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contamination neighborhoods as constrained two-component mixture families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\) and \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\). The contamination neighborhood is exactly the two-component finite-mixture family \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_0,\varepsilon)=\left\{w_1Q_1+w_2Q_2:(w_1,w_2)=(1-\varepsilon,\varepsilon),\ Q_1=P_0,\ Q_2\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\right\}.\] If \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), a probability law \(Q\) belongs to this family if and only if \(Q(A)\ge(1-\varepsilon)P_0(A)\) for every \(A\in\mathcal F\). In that case the contaminating law is uniquely recovered as \(H=(Q-(1-\varepsilon)P_0)/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contamination neighborhood is a two-component mixture with fixed weights and nominal first component; membership is equivalently certified by measure domination.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0,Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\).
\(0<\varepsilon\le1\) for the domination equivalence and recovery formula.

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Distribution Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-law ambiguity specified through exact or set-valued coordinate marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi=\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_d\) be a product measurable space, and let \(\pi_i:\Xi\to\Xi_i\) be the coordinate projection. For prescribed nonempty marginal families \(\mathcal M_i\subseteq\mathcal P(\Xi_i)\), the joint-law family consistent with the marginal information is \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{marg}}(\mathcal M_1,\ldots,\mathcal M_d)=\left\{Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi):Q\circ\pi_i^{-1}\in\mathcal M_i\ \text{for every }i=1,\ldots,d\right\}.\] Exact marginal information is the special case \(\mathcal M_i=\{P_i\}\). This constraint alone generally leaves the dependence among coordinates unspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal information restricts each coordinate distribution of a joint law, either exactly or to an admissible family, without generally fixing dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Structure Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence restrictions represented by an admissible class of copulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a probability law on \(\mathbb R^d\) with joint cumulative distribution function \(F_Q\) and continuous marginal distribution functions \(F_{Q,1},\ldots,F_{Q,d}\). Its dependence structure is represented by the unique copula \(C_Q:[0,1]^d\to[0,1]\) satisfying \[F_Q(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=C_Q\bigl(F_{Q,1}(x_1),\ldots,F_{Q,d}(x_d)\bigr).\] Given an admissible copula class \(\mathcal C\), dependence information imposes the constraint \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{dep}}(\mathcal C)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d):C_Q\in\mathcal C\}.\] Such information restricts cross-coordinate dependence separately from the marginal distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuous marginals, dependence is uniquely encoded by a copula; admissible dependence information restricts that copula to a specified class.

Every marginal distribution function of \(Q\) is continuous.
\(\mathcal C\) is a class of d-dimensional copulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Copula-Constrained Families

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\mathcal M_i\) be a family of univariate cumulative distribution functions, and let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of \(d\)-dimensional copulas. The copula-constrained family comprises the joint laws whose cumulative distribution functions have the form \[F(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=C\bigl(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d)\bigr),\qquad C\in\mathcal C,\quad F_i\in\mathcal M_i.\] Equivalently, it is the collection of distributions generated by pairing an admissible marginal tuple with an admissible copula. Every displayed composition is a valid joint cumulative distribution function with marginals \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal–Dependence Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for marginal laws and a prescribed copula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\) be univariate cumulative distribution functions and let \(C:[0,1]^d\to[0,1]\). The marginal tuple and dependence specification are compatible precisely when \(C\) is a \(d\)-dimensional copula; then \[F(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=C\bigl(F_1(x_1),\ldots,F_d(x_d)\bigr)\] is a joint cumulative distribution function with marginals \(F_1,\ldots,F_d\). Conversely, every joint distribution with these marginals admits such a copula representation. The representing copula is unique on \(\operatorname{Ran}(F_1)\times\cdots\times\operatorname{Ran}(F_d)\), and it is unique on all of \([0,1]^d\) when every \(F_i\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any valid copula is compatible with any tuple of univariate marginals; the resulting joint law has those marginals, with full copula uniqueness for continuous marginals.

\(C\) is a d-dimensional copula.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is Borel measurable.
Prescribed moment and support constraints define a nonempty family of probability measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{lc}}\) is a shape-constrained distributional ambiguity set.

notation.meaning: Lebesgue density of a probability measure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the common log-concave subclass of shape-constrained distribution ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A log-concave shape-constrained ambiguity set on \(\Xi\) is
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{lc}}=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):P\ll\operatorname{Leb},\ \int_\Xi \phi_j(\xi)\,dP(\xi)\in C_j\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\ f_P(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\ge f_P(x)^\theta f_P(y)^{1-\theta}\right\},
\]
where the final inequality holds for all \(x,y\in\Xi\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), with \(0^0=1\). Equivalently, \(\log f_P\) is concave on the convex support where \(f_P>0\). Additional support or moment restrictions are represented by the measurable functions \(\phi_j\) and sets \(C_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shape-constrained ambiguity set may consist of distributions whose densities are log-concave and that additionally satisfy specified support or moment restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Constrained Distributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and log-concave example fit the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The pointwise density inequality also requires a specified log-concave representative and a convex ambient domain or an explicit extension of the density by zero; a Lebesgue density is otherwise defined only almost everywhere.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\{p\ge0:Ap=b\}\) is nonempty and \(\sup\{\ell^\top p:Ap=b,p\ge0\}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{p\ge0,\,Ap=b}\ell^\top p=\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge\ell\}\).

notation.meaning: Probability vector on the finite support.
Loss values at the support points.
Multiplier for the probability and moment equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support worst-case expectation with equality-defined probability ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the uncertainty support be \(\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\}\), let \(\ell_i=\ell(\xi_i)\), and let
\[
\mathcal P=\left\{p\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ap=b\right\},
\]
where a row of \(A\) may impose \(\sum_i p_i=1\). If \(\mathcal P\ne\varnothing\) and the primal value is finite, linear-programming strong duality gives
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\ell_i
=
\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{b^\top y:A^\top y\ge\ell\right\}.
\]
Both optima are attained. Thus the worst-case expectation over the finite-support ambiguity set equals a finite-dimensional dual linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible finite-support ambiguity polytope with finite value, the worst-case expected loss equals the optimum of its linear-programming dual.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Duality

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\) is compact Hausdorff and \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,h\in C(\Xi)\).
The prescribed moment vector lies in the relative interior of the attainable moment set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_b}\int h\,dP=\inf_{\lambda_0,\lambda}\{\lambda_0+\lambda^\top b:\lambda_0+\lambda^\top g(\xi)\ge h(\xi)\ \forall\xi\in\Xi\}\).

notation.meaning: Probability measures satisfying the prescribed moments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-support equality-moment version with a relative-interior regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\mathcal P_b=\left\{P\in\mathcal P(\Xi):\int_\Xi g_i(\xi)\,dP(\xi)=b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P_b\ne\varnothing\) and \(b\) lies in the relative interior of \(\{\int g\,dP:P\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\}\), then
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_b}\int_\Xi h(\xi)\,dP(\xi)
=
\inf_{\lambda_0\in\mathbb R,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}
\left\{\lambda_0+\lambda^\top b:\lambda_0+\lambda^\top g(\xi)\ge h(\xi)\ \text{for every }\xi\in\Xi\right\}.
\]
The primal supremum is attained, and the displayed semi-infinite problem is the generalized-moment dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness and a relative-interior moment condition, a worst-case expectation with equality moments equals a semi-infinite multiplier problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Moment Problem Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact equality-moment formulation is plausible and duality is the correct content kind, but the exact generalized-moment theorem, including the stated relative-interior condition and primal attainment, has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi\) is Polish and \(c:\Xi\times\Xi\to[0,\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous with \(c(\xi,\xi)=0\).
\(Q\in\mathcal P(\Xi)\), \(\rho\ge0\), and the upper-semicontinuous loss \(h\) has sufficient \(c\)-growth for finite expectations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P:W_c(P,Q)\le\rho}E_P[h]=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\{\lambda\rho+E_Q[\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}(h(\xi)-\lambda c(\xi,Z))]\}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal transport cost between probability measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong duality for a transport-cost ball around a nominal distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
W_c(P,Q)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(P,Q)}\int_{\Xi\times\Xi}c(\xi,z)\,d\pi(\xi,z),
\]
and ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_\rho=\{P:W_c(P,Q)\le\rho\}\), transport duality yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\rho}\int_\Xi h(\xi)\,dP(\xi)
=
\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\lambda\rho+
\int_\Xi\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\bigl(h(\xi)-\lambda c(\xi,z)\bigr)\,dQ(z)\right\}.
\]
The equality holds when the stated semicontinuity, measurability, and growth conditions ensure transport duality and integrability; if the common value is finite and standard compactness conditions hold, the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case expectation over a transport ball equals a scalar minimization involving the nominal expectation of a pointwise transport-penalized loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Transport Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Optimal-transport duality fits the leaf, but phrases such as “sufficient c-growth” and “standard compactness conditions” do not state a verifiable theorem hypothesis. An authoritative source is required to fix the precise measurability, integrability, growth, and attainment conditions.

assumptions_latex: \(\Xi=\mathbb N_0\), \(Q=\delta_0\), \(c(m,n)=|m-n|\), and the transport radius is \(1\).
The loss is \(h(n)=n^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{P:W_c(P,Q)\le1}E_P[h]=+\infty\), so no finite-valued transport-dual reformulation exists under merely linear transport control.

notation.meaning: A feasible distribution placing vanishing mass far from zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear loss under a linearly growing transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_N=(1-N^{-1})\delta_0+N^{-1}\delta_N\) for \(N\ge1\). Its transport cost from \(Q=\delta_0\) is
\[
W_c(P_N,Q)=N^{-1}c(N,0)=1,
\]
so \(P_N\) belongs to the radius-one transport ambiguity set. However,
\[
E_{P_N}[h]=N^{-1}N^2=N\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{P:W_c(P,Q)\le1}E_P[h]=+\infty.
\]
Thus transport-budget control alone does not produce a finite worst-case expectation when the loss grows faster than the transport cost; a compatible growth or integrability assumption is indispensable for finite-valued DRO duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-cost transport ball permits tiny masses arbitrarily far away, making a quadratic-loss worst-case expectation infinite unless a growth condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: DRO Duality Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct and failure_boundary is the exact mathematical role for this leaf. It nevertheless lacks the required cited source and locator for the claimed DRO failure context.

children.title: Linear Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional DRO representations expressible through linear optimization.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(D\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\mathcal P=\{p\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ap=b,\ Dp\le d\}\) is nonempty and \(\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\ell^\top p<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\ell^\top p=\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}\{b^\top y+d^\top z:A^\top y+D^\top z\ge\ell\}\).

notation.meaning: Multipliers for the equality and inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP reformulation for polyhedral finite-support ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(D\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\), and define
\[
\mathcal P=\{p\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ap=b,\ Dp\le d\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P\ne\varnothing\) and \(\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\ell^\top p<+\infty\), linear-programming strong duality gives
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\ell^\top p
=
\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in\mathbb R_+^r}
\left\{b^\top y+d^\top z:A^\top y+D^\top z\ge\ell\right\}.
\]
Consequently, replacing such a worst-case expectation by the displayed dual variables, inequalities, and objective yields an equivalent linear formulation when all remaining decision-dependent expressions and constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-support worst-case expectation over a nonempty polyhedral ambiguity set has an exact linear-programming reformulation when its value is finite; the surrounding DRO model remains linear when its other expressions are affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Reformulations

children.title: Conic Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional DRO representations expressible through conic optimization.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) are nonempty closed convex cones; \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\).
The primal value is finite, and there exists \(\bar p\in\operatorname{ri}C\) such that \(A\bar p=b\) and \(d-B\bar p\in\operatorname{ri}K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup\{\ell^\top p:Ap=b,\ d-Bp\in K,\ p\in C\}=\min\{b^\top y+d^\top z:z\in K^*,\ A^\top y+B^\top z-\ell\in C^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact finite-dimensional conic dual reformulation under an explicit relative-interior Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) be nonempty closed convex cones, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(d\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(\ell\in\mathbb R^n\), and consider
\[
\sup_{p\in C}\left\{\ell^\top p:Ap=b,\ d-Bp\in K\right\}.
\]
Assume that its value is finite and that there exists \(\bar p\in\operatorname{ri}C\) satisfying \(A\bar p=b\) and \(d-B\bar p\in\operatorname{ri}K\). Then conic strong duality gives
\[
\sup_{p\in C}\left\{\ell^\top p:Ap=b,\ d-Bp\in K\right\}
=
\min_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,z\in K^*}
\left\{b^\top y+d^\top z:A^\top y+B^\top z-\ell\in C^*\right\}.
\]
Thus a DRO constraint containing this worst-case value has an exact finite conic representation whenever its ambiguity restrictions and loss admit the stated finite-dimensional conic form and regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite conic worst-case problem has an exact attained conic-dual reformulation when its value is finite and an explicit relative-interior Slater condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Reformulations

children.title: Linear-to-Conic Representability
children.top_down_role: Relationships between linear representability and broader conic representability.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is described by finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every linear representation is a conic representation over products of nonnegative orthants and zero cones.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative orthant used for inequality slacks.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedding finite linear systems into conic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
S=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\right\},
\]
then introducing a slack vector \(s\) gives
\[
S=\left\{x:\exists s\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ Ax=b,\ Gx+s=h\right\}.
\]
Thus every finite linear formulation is a conic formulation using the product cone \(\mathbb R_+^m\) for inequality slacks and the zero cone for equalities. Consequently, any exact linear DRO reformulation is automatically conically representable. The converse holds only when the cones in a conic lift are polyhedral; nonpolyhedral cones generally express feasible sets unavailable to finite linear extended formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear systems are conic systems over nonnegative orthants; a conic formulation reduces to a finite linear formulation when all participating cones are polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-to-Conic Representability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear-to-conic embedding and the polyhedral-cone converse are standard and representation is the correct content kind. However, the record supplies neither a source reference nor a locator; standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy this statement-review citation requirement.

children.title: Representability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity-set or loss structures that resist exact linear or conic representation.

assumptions_latex: Extended formulations use finitely many real auxiliary variables and finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^n\) has no finite linear extended formulation.

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpolyhedral cones obstruct exact finite LP lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone
\[
\mathbb S_+^n=\left\{X\in\mathbb S^n:v^\top Xv\ge0\ \text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^n\right\}
\]
is nonpolyhedral for \(n\ge2\). Every projection of a set defined by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities is polyhedral. Therefore no finite linear extended formulation can project exactly onto \(\mathbb S_+^n\). In particular, a DRO reformulation whose feasible region contains an unrestricted positive-semidefinite constraint cannot generally be replaced by an exact finite LP lift. Exact linearization requires additional structure, such as a polyhedral restriction, while finite collections of linear cuts provide only approximations in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the positive-semidefinite cone is nonpolyhedral, an unrestricted semidefinite DRO reformulation cannot have an exact finite linear extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Representability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonpolyhedrality argument is mathematically correct, and failure_boundary correctly classifies the obstruction. An authoritative source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator is still required.

assumptions_latex: \(q_i(x)=x^\top Q_i x+2a_i^\top x+b_i\) for \(i=0,1\), with \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\).
There exists \(\bar x\) such that \(q_0(\bar x)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_0(x)\le0\Rightarrow q_1(x)\le t\) iff there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(\begin{bmatrix}-Q_1+\lambda Q_0&-a_1+\lambda a_0\\(-a_1+\lambda a_0)^\top&t-b_1+\lambda b_0\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-quadratic-constraint S-lemma reformulation used in moment-based DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the strict-feasibility assumption, the robust quadratic implication
\[
q_0(x)\le0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_1(x)\le t
\]
holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(t-q_1(x)+\lambda q_0(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Equivalently,
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
-Q_1+\lambda Q_0&-a_1+\lambda a_0\\
(-a_1+\lambda a_0)^\top&t-b_1+\lambda b_0
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
Thus a semi-infinite quadratic constraint arising after DRO moment dualization admits an exact finite semidefinite representation when it has one quadratic support constraint and satisfies the stated Slater condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one strictly feasible quadratic support constraint, the S-lemma converts a robust quadratic inequality exactly into one positive-semidefinite matrix constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated S-lemma sign convention and block matrix are consistent, and representation fits the semidefinite-reformulation leaf. The scalar t is not assigned a domain, and no exact S-lemma source with an inspectable locator is supplied; the precise theorem therefore remains source-dependent.

assumptions_latex: Scenarios \(i=1,\ldots,n\) have probabilities \(p\) ranging over a nonempty polytope \(\mathcal P\).
Constants \(M_i\) are valid upper bounds for the scenario violations \(g_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distributionally robust chance constraint is represented by binary violation indicators, valid big-M inequalities, and the LP dual of \(\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}p^\top z\).

notation.meaning: Binary indicator that scenario i may violate its constraint.
Polyhedral ambiguity set for scenario probabilities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario distributionally robust chance constraints with valid big-M bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite scenarios, introduce \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\) and impose
\[
g_i(x)\le M_i z_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
When each \(M_i\) is valid, \(z_i=0\) enforces scenario \(i\), while \(z_i=1\) permits its violation. The distributionally robust chance constraint is
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{i=1}^n p_i z_i\le\varepsilon.
\]
If \(\mathcal P\) is polyhedral, the supremum is replaced exactly by its linear-programming dual. Together with the binary restrictions and big-M inequalities, this yields a mixed-integer linear reformulation; conically representable \(\mathcal P\) analogously yields a mixed-integer conic formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-scenario robust chance constraints become mixed-integer programs by marking violated scenarios and dualizing the worst-case probability over a polyhedral ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed-integer construction is plausible and its content kind fits the leaf, but the cited generic discrete-optimization and finite-state sections do not specifically substantiate the distributionally robust chance-constraint equivalence. The admissible domain of x and validity domain for each big-M bound also need explicit support from an exact source.

assumptions_latex: \(R(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\).
A tractable function \(U\) satisfies \(U(x)\ge R(x)\) for every admissible decision \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:U(x)\le0\}\subseteq\{x:R(x)\le0\}\) and \(\inf_x U(x)\ge\inf_x R(x)\) on a common feasible domain.

notation.meaning: Tractable upper approximation of the worst-case loss.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety and objective ordering for upper approximations of DRO risks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
R(x)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]
\]
and let \(U(x)\) be a tractable upper bound satisfying \(R(x)\le U(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then
\[
\{x\in X:U(x)\le0\}\subseteq\{x\in X:R(x)\le0\},
\]
so replacing a DRO constraint by \(U(x)\le0\) is conservative and preserves robust feasibility. For minimization on the same domain,
\[
\inf_{x\in X}R(x)\le\inf_{x\in X}U(x).
\]
Equality is recovered whenever the approximation is pointwise exact at an optimizer; otherwise the difference between these two values quantifies objective conservatism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any tractable upper bound on worst-case loss yields a safe inner approximation of DRO constraints and an upper bound on the minimization value.
knowledge_statements.title: Conservative DRO Approximations

assumptions_latex: The loss random variable lies in \(L^\infty(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\).
The functional \(\rho:L^\infty\to\mathbb R\) is coherent, monotone, and has the Fatou property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\) is a worst-case expectation over a convex set of probability measures absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\).

notation.meaning: Coherent risk functional applied to loss
Dual ambiguity set of probability measures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of a Fatou-continuous coherent risk functional on \(L^\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,P)\) be a probability space. A functional \(\rho:L^\infty\to\mathbb R\) that is monotone, subadditive, positively homogeneous, cash invariant in the loss convention, and has the Fatou property admits a representation
\[
\rho(Z)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q}E_Q[Z],
\]
where \(\mathcal Q\) is a nonempty convex set of countably additive probability measures satisfying \(Q\ll P\). Conversely, any functional defined by this supremum is coherent and has the Fatou property when \(\mathcal Q\) is closed in the dual topology appropriate to \(L^\infty\). Thus minimizing coherent risk is equivalent to minimizing a distributionally robust worst-case expectation over its risk envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coherent loss risk with the Fatou property equals the worst expected loss over a convex ambiguity set, making coherent-risk minimization a distributionally robust problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Coherent-Risk Equivalences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content fits Coherent-Risk Equivalences, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative locator is required to verify the precise L-infinity Fatou-property representation, the countably additive risk envelope, the relevant dual topology and closure condition, and the stated converse.

assumptions_latex: Samples \(\widehat\xi_1,\ldots,\widehat\xi_n\in\mathbb R^d\) define the empirical distribution \(\widehat P_n\).
The loss is affine in uncertainty: \(\ell(x,\xi)=a(x)^\top\xi+b(x)\).
The transport cost is induced by a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Wasserstein distributional robustness adds the exact regularizer \(\varepsilon\|a(x)\|_*\) to empirical risk.

notation.meaning: Norm dual to the transport norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact affine-loss equivalence for a first-order Wasserstein ball on \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\) in a decision set \(X\), let \(\ell(x,\xi)=a(x)^\top\xi+b(x)\), and let \(W_1\) use ground cost \(\|\xi-\xi'\|\). If the ambiguity set contains all probability measures on \(\mathbb R^d\) within radius \(\varepsilon\) of \(\widehat P_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}\), then
\[
\sup_{Q:W_1(Q,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon}E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)]
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(x,\widehat\xi_i)+\varepsilon\|a(x)\|_*.
\]
Consequently, minimizing the distributionally robust objective over \(X\) is exactly empirical-risk minimization with the dual-norm regularizer \(\varepsilon\|a(x)\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For affine losses, worst-case expectation over a first-order Wasserstein ball equals empirical loss plus a dual-norm penalty on the uncertainty coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Equivalences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Regularization Equivalences and the affine-loss formula is standard under suitable first-moment and Wasserstein-domain conditions. No source is cited, so the exact equality and its required measure-class assumptions cannot be accepted as candidate-review knowledge.

assumptions_latex: The empirical law is \(\widehat P_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{(u_i,y_i)}\).
Transport may perturb each feature \(u_i\) within \(\|u-u_i\|\leq\varepsilon\) but cannot change its label \(y_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distributionally robust empirical objective equals the adversarial-training objective with radius \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Feature perturbation set around sample i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Label-preserving \(W_\infty\) ambiguity and independently perturbed training features.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_i(\varepsilon)=\{u:\|u-u_i\|\leq\varepsilon\}\). Define \(\mathcal P_\varepsilon\) as the distributions obtainable by coupling mass \(1/n\) at each \((u_i,y_i)\) to points \((u,y_i)\) with \(u\in B_i(\varepsilon)\). For any measurable loss \(L(\theta;u,y)\) whose displayed suprema are finite,
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_\varepsilon}E_Q[L(\theta;u,y)]
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sup_{u\in B_i(\varepsilon)}L(\theta;u,y_i).
\]
Thus minimizing this DRO objective is equivalent to adversarial training in which every training feature is replaced by its worst admissible perturbation while its label is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A label-preserving infinity-Wasserstein DRO objective is the average worst loss under independent bounded perturbations of each training feature, exactly matching adversarial training.
knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial-Training Connections

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is locally appropriate for Adversarial-Training Connections, but no source verifies the label-preserving W-infinity coupling model, the interchange leading to independently optimized samplewise losses, or the needed measurability conditions.

assumptions_latex: The decision \(x\) is fixed independently of the calibration sample.
The random ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfies \(P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\geq1-\delta\).
The loss \(\ell(x,\xi)\) is integrable under every distribution considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), the robust value upper-bounds the true risk of the fixed decision.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage-based upper certificate for one sample-independent decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\in X\) before observing the sample used to construct \(\mathcal P_n\), and define
\[
R_n^{\rm rob}(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_n}E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)].
\]
On the event \(\{P\in\mathcal P_n\}\), inclusion of the true distribution immediately gives \(E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(x)\). Hence the coverage condition implies
\[
P^n\!\left\{E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(x)\right\}\geq1-\delta.
\]
This is a pointwise guarantee: its probability statement applies to the prespecified \(x\), without asserting simultaneous validity over all decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a calibrated ambiguity set contains the true distribution with high probability, its worst-case value upper-bounds the true risk of any prespecified decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Out-of-Sample Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate correctly distinguishes a prespecified decision and fits Pointwise Out-of-Sample Guarantees. However, the record has no source with an inspectable locator supporting the ambiguity-set coverage formulation.

assumptions_latex: The random ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_n\) contains \(P\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
For every \(x\in X\), the loss is integrable under all distributions in \(\mathcal P_n\cup\{P\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One event of probability at least \(1-\delta\) certifies the robust upper bound simultaneously for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous guarantee induced by distribution-level coverage of a common ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(R_P(x)=E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) and \(R_n^{\rm rob}(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_n}E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)]\). If \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), then for every \(x\in X\),
\[
R_P(x)\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(x).
\]
Therefore
\[
P^n\!\left\{\sup_{x\in X}\bigl(R_P(x)-R_n^{\rm rob}(x)\bigr)\leq0\right\}\geq1-\delta.
\]
Unlike a collection of separately calibrated pointwise statements, this assertion holds on one common event and remains valid after selecting a data-dependent decision from \(X\), provided the same ambiguity set and loss class are used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distribution-level coverage yields one high-probability event on which robust risk upper-bounds true risk for every decision simultaneously, including a subsequently selected decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Generalization Guarantees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate fits Uniform Generalization Guarantees and correctly uses one distribution-level coverage event for all decisions. No cited source supports the simultaneous formulation or its application to a data-dependent selection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform VC-dimension generalization bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability uniform risk bound for binary hypothesis classes under the source's empirical-risk sampling setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $H$ be a family of functions taking values in $\{-1,+1\}$ with $\operatorname{VCdim}(H)=d$, and suppose $m\ge d\ge1$ and $0<\delta<1$. Under the sampling model defining $R$ and $\widehat R$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously for all $h\in H$, $$R(h)\le\widehat R(h)+\sqrt{\frac{2d\log(em/d)}{m}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{2m}}.$$ For fixed $\delta$ and asymptotically increasing $m/d$, the VC-complexity contribution has order $O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(m/d)}{m/d}}\right)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary hypothesis class of VC dimension d, the stated sampling setup gives, with probability at least one minus delta, a simultaneous upper bound on every hypothesis's true risk by its empirical risk plus VC-complexity and confidence terms.
assumptions_latex: H\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{\mathcal X}
\operatorname{VCdim}(H)=d
m\ge d\ge1
0<\delta<1
R\text{ and }\widehat R\text{ are defined under the source's sampling model}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left[\forall h\in H:\ R(h)\le\widehat R(h)+\sqrt{\frac{2d\log(em/d)}{m}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{2m}}\right]\ge1-\delta.

source_witnesses.locator: Rademacher Complexity and VC-Dimension / 3.3. VC-dimension / Corollary 3.4

directory_assessment.rationale: Uniform generalization is relevant to this A16 specialization, but a generic VC theorem should retain a statistical-learning primary home rather than be owned by the DRO hierarchy.

assumptions_latex: A decision rule \(\widehat x_n\) is measurable with respect to the calibration data.
A simultaneous event satisfies \(R_P(x)\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same event certifies \(R_P(\widehat x_n)\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(\widehat x_n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a simultaneous bound to a decision selected from the same data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat x_n\in X\) be any measurable function of the data, including an optimizer of \(R_n^{\rm rob}\). If an event \(G_n\) satisfies
\[
G_n\subseteq\left\{R_P(x)\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(x)\ \text{for every }x\in X\right\}
\quad\text{and}\quad P^n(G_n)\geq1-\delta,
\]
then substitution of \(x=\widehat x_n\) on \(G_n\) gives
\[
P^n\!\left\{R_P(\widehat x_n)\leq R_n^{\rm rob}(\widehat x_n)\right\}\geq1-\delta.
\]
Pointwise bounds proved only for each deterministic \(x\) do not by themselves justify this substitution because \(\widehat x_n\) depends on the same data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform risk bound remains valid for a decision chosen from the calibration data; separate pointwise bounds generally do not justify adaptive substitution.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Dependent Generalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits Decision-Dependent Generalization and accurately separates uniform control from deterministic pointwise statements. An authoritative citation with a specific locator is absent.

assumptions_latex: The observations are i.i.d. from the nonatomic uniform distribution on \([0,1]\).
The decision class contains every finite subset of \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise consistency does not imply consistency for an adaptively selected decision without uniform control.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive overfitting counterexample separating pointwise and uniform convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]\), let \(\mathcal A\) be the class of finite subsets of \([0,1]\), and define \(\ell_A(z)=\mathbf 1\{z\notin A\}\). For every fixed \(A\in\mathcal A\), the empirical mean converges almost surely to \(E[\ell_A(Z)]=1\). However, the data-dependent choice \(\widehat A_n=\{Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\}\) satisfies
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_{\widehat A_n}(Z_i)=0,
\qquad E[\ell_{\widehat A_n}(Z)]=1
\]
almost surely. Thus arbitrarily accurate pointwise laws provide no guarantee for adaptive optimization over a class lacking uniform complexity control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite subsets of a nonatomic space, every fixed loss generalizes, yet choosing the observed sample as the decision produces zero empirical loss and unit true loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalization Failure Boundaries

assumptions_latex: The decision set \(X\) is compact.
The true objective \(f(x)=E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) is finite and continuous on \(X\).
The robust objectives \(f_n\) converge uniformly to \(f\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust optimal values converge almost surely to the true optimal value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-decision uniform-convergence version of DRO value consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(n\), let
\[
f_n(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_n}E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)],\qquad
v_n=\inf_{x\in X}f_n(x),
\]
and let \(f(x)=E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) with \(v=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). If \(X\) is compact, \(f\) is finite and continuous, and
\[
\sup_{x\in X}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\longrightarrow0
\]
almost surely, then \(v_n\to v\) almost surely. Indeed, the deterministic bound \(|v_n-v|\leq\sup_{x\in X}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\) applies on every sample path where uniform convergence holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convergence of robust objectives to a continuous true objective on a compact decision set implies almost-sure convergence of their optimal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits Optimal-Value Consistency, and the uniform-convergence conclusion is precisely scoped. No source is provided for the stated consistency result, despite the record being marked as requiring one.

assumptions_latex: The decision set \(X\) is compact, and the true minimizer set \(X^*\) is nonempty.
The objectives \(f_n\) converge uniformly to the continuous objective \(f\) almost surely.
Each \(x_n\) is asymptotically optimal: \(f_n(x_n)\leq\inf_X f_n+\eta_n\), where \(\eta_n\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point of \((x_n)\) belongs to \(X^*\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(x_n,X^*)\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer consistency of approximate DRO minimizers under uniform objective convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\), and choose \(x_n\in X\) satisfying
\[
f_n(x_n)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f_n(x)+\eta_n,
\qquad \eta_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
If \(X\) is compact, \(f\) is continuous, \(X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_n(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely, then every accumulation point of \((x_n)\) lies in \(X^*\) almost surely. Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x_n,X^*)\longrightarrow0
\]
almost surely. Convergence to a single decision follows when \(X^*\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness and uniform objective convergence, every limit point of asymptotically optimal DRO decisions is truly optimal; uniqueness yields convergence to the unique optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits Solution Consistency and distinguishes set convergence from convergence under uniqueness. An authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is missing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-sure population-risk consistency of robust linear regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The conclusion concerns convergence of achieved population root-mean-square prediction risk, not convergence of coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let c_n\downarrow0 and suppose
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}n(c_n)^{m+1}=\infty.
\]
If there exists H<\infty such that \|\boldsymbol\beta(c_n,S_n)\|_2\le H for every n, then, almost surely,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt{\int (y-\mathbf x^\top\boldsymbol\beta(c_n,\mathcal S_n))^2\,d\mathbb P(y,\mathbf x)}
=
\sqrt{\int (y-\mathbf x^\top\boldsymbol\beta(\mathbb P))^2\,d\mathbb P(y,\mathbf x)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the robustness radius tends to zero slowly enough and the robust regression coefficients remain uniformly bounded, their population root-mean-square prediction loss converges almost surely to the population solution's loss.
assumptions_latex: c_n\downarrow0
\lim_{n\to\infty}n(c_n)^{m+1}=\infty
\exists H<\infty\ \forall n:\|\boldsymbol\beta(c_n,S_n)\|_2\le H
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sqrt{\int (y-\mathbf x^\top\boldsymbol\beta(c_n,\mathcal S_n))^2\,d\mathbb P}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathrm{a.s.}}\sqrt{\int (y-\mathbf x^\top\boldsymbol\beta(\mathbb P))^2\,d\mathbb P}.

assumptions_latex: The empirical distributions \(\widehat P_n\) converge to \(P\) in a metric \(d\) almost surely.
The radii satisfy \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\) and eventually \(d(P,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon_n\) almost surely.
Expected losses are uniformly continuous with respect to \(d\), uniformly over \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ambiguity sets retain the true law eventually while their robust objectives converge uniformly to the true objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic metric-ball regime balancing asymptotic shrinkage and eventual coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a probability metric \(d\), define
\[
\mathcal P_n=\{Q:d(Q,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon_n\}.
\]
A consistency-compatible shrinking regime requires \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) while \(d(P,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon_n\) eventually almost surely. If there exists a modulus \(\omega(t)\downarrow0\) as \(t\downarrow0\) such that
\[
\sup_{x\in X}|E_Q[\ell(x,\xi)]-E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]|
\leq\omega(d(Q,P)),
\]
then every \(Q\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfies \(d(Q,P)\leq\varepsilon_n+d(\widehat P_n,P)\), and consequently the robust objectives converge uniformly to the true objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid shrinking regime lets the radius vanish slowly enough to retain the true distribution and combines metric convergence with uniform continuity of expected losses.
knowledge_statements.title: Shrinking-Ambiguity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Shrinking-Ambiguity Regimes, but no source verifies the generic metric assumptions, triangle-inequality step, uniform expectation modulus, and eventual-coverage regime as stated.

assumptions_latex: A concentration inequality provides \(P^n\{d(P,\widehat P_n)>r\}\leq\psi_n(r)\).
The function \(\psi_n\) is nonincreasing in \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(\varepsilon_{n,\delta}=\inf\{r:\psi_n(r)\leq\delta\}\) gives ambiguity-set coverage at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inversion of a finite-sample concentration inequality into an ambiguity radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given sample size \(n\), confidence level \(\delta\in(0,1)\), empirical law \(\widehat P_n\), and a bound
\[
P^n\{d(P,\widehat P_n)>r\}\leq\psi_n(r),
\]
set
\[
\varepsilon_{n,\delta}=\inf\{r\geq0:\psi_n(r)\leq\delta\},
\qquad
\mathcal P_{n,\delta}=\{Q:d(Q,\widehat P_n)\leq\varepsilon_{n,\delta}\}.
\]
If the infimum is attained, or the radius is enlarged to a value satisfying \(\psi_n(\varepsilon_{n,\delta})\leq\delta\), output \(\mathcal P_{n,\delta}\). Then \(P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_{n,\delta}\}\geq1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invert a concentration tail bound at level delta and use the resulting quantile as the ambiguity radius; the resulting set covers the true law with probability at least one minus delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Concentration-Based Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role is suitable for Concentration-Based Calibration, and the statement handles possible nonattainment of the generalized inverse. No source with a specific concentration or calibration locator is supplied.

children.title: Statistical-Test Calibration
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity-set calibration based on statistical testing procedures.

assumptions_latex: For every candidate distribution \(Q\), a test of \(H_0:P=Q\) has rejection probability at most \(\alpha\) when \(Q=P\).
The test statistic and critical value are measurable functions of the data and candidate law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set of candidate distributions not rejected by the level-\(\alpha\) test has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Test statistic for candidate distribution Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample ambiguity-set calibration by inversion of point-null distributional tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that for every probability distribution \(Q\) in a model class \(\mathfrak P\), the test rejecting \(H_0:P=Q\) when \(T_n(Q)>c_{n,\alpha}(Q)\) satisfies
\[
Q^n\{T_n(Q)>c_{n,\alpha}(Q)\}\leq\alpha.
\]
Define the inverted acceptance region
\[
\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}=\{Q\in\mathfrak P:T_n(Q)\leq c_{n,\alpha}(Q)\}.
\]
When the data-generating law \(P\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P\), evaluating the test at \(Q=P\) yields
\[
P^n\{P\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the nonrejected distributions form a statistically calibrated DRO ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invert a valid level-alpha goodness-of-fit test: all nonrejected distributions form an ambiguity set containing the true model with probability at least one minus alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical-Test Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematics describes standard test inversion, but no source verifies the finite-sample testing and coverage formulation. In addition, the terminal container is Statistical-Test Calibration, for which algorithm or principle is a better mathematical role than certificate; the coverage statement is the output guarantee of the calibration method.

children.title: Profile-Based Calibration
children.top_down_role: Calibration based on profiled statistical criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Profile-Based Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Profile-discrepancy calibration of a parameter-induced DRO ambiguity region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a class of probability measures, let \(\widehat P_n\) be an empirical measure, let \(m:\mathcal P\to\Theta\) be a parameter map, and let \(d:\mathcal P\times\mathcal P\to[0,\infty]\) be a discrepancy. The empirical profile at \(\theta\in\Theta\) is \[R_n(\theta)=\inf\{d(Q,\widehat P_n):Q\in\mathcal P,\ m(Q)=\theta\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). For a calibrated critical value \(c_{n,\alpha}\), the profile region and induced ambiguity set are \[C_{n,\alpha}=\{\theta:R_n(\theta)\le c_{n,\alpha}\},\qquad \mathcal A_{n,\alpha}=\{Q\in\mathcal P:m(Q)\in C_{n,\alpha}\}.\] Calibration targets \(\Pr_{P_0}(m(P_0)\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge 1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A profile minimizes discrepancy subject to a fixed parameter value; thresholding it yields a confidence region and the corresponding DRO ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat P_n\) is constructed from data generated by an unknown \(P_0\in\mathcal P\).
\(c_{n,\alpha}\) is chosen for a specified level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal A_{n,\alpha}\) are the profile-calibrated parameter region and ambiguity set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Profile-Based Calibration and its notation is internally coherent, but no inspectable source is cited for this particular profile-discrepancy construction or its claimed coverage target. An authoritative locator is required to confirm the statistic, threshold convention, and induced DRO interpretation.

children.title: Test-Inversion Regions
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity regions obtained by inverting families of statistical tests.

knowledge_statements.title: Test-Inversion Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambiguity regions obtained by inverting pointwise distributional tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every candidate distribution \(Q\in\mathcal P\), let \(\varphi_n(Q)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate rejection of the null hypothesis \(H_Q:P_0=Q\). The inverted acceptance region is \[\mathcal A_{n,\alpha}=\{Q\in\mathcal P:\varphi_n(Q)=0\}.\] If the tests have uniform size at most \(\alpha\), meaning \[\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\Pr_Q\{\varphi_n(Q)=1\}\le\alpha,\] then the random region satisfies \[\inf_{P_0\in\mathcal P}\Pr_{P_0}\{P_0\in\mathcal A_{n,\alpha}\}\ge 1-\alpha.\] Thus the same set is both a confidence region for the data-generating distribution and a statistically calibrated DRO ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting all level-alpha tests produces an ambiguity set containing the true distribution with probability at least one minus alpha.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) contains the data-generating distribution.
Each null \(H_Q\) is tested using the same observed sample.
The test family has uniform size at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{P_0\in\mathcal P}\Pr_{P_0}(P_0\in\mathcal A_{n,\alpha})\ge 1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: rejection indicator for candidate distribution Q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The test-inversion construction and uniform-coverage implication match the node, but the record combines a representation with a theorem-level guarantee. No source is supplied to support either the uniform-size hypothesis or the resulting simultaneous statement. A source is also needed to determine whether the terminal container should hold the representation alone or the stated guarantee as a theorem or principle.

children.title: Coverage Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of finite-sample or asymptotic coverage behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-replication diagnostics for empirical coverage of a calibrated ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a distribution \(P_0\) and independently repeat the complete sampling-and-calibration experiment \(B\) times, producing ambiguity sets \(\mathcal A^{(1)},\ldots,\mathcal A^{(B)}\). Define \(I_b=\mathbf 1\{P_0\in\mathcal A^{(b)}\}\) and \(\widehat c_B=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B I_b\). If the repetitions are identically distributed, then \(B\widehat c_B\) is binomial with success probability \(c(P_0)=\Pr_{P_0}(P_0\in\mathcal A)\). Moreover, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[\Pr\left\{|\widehat c_B-c(P_0)|\le\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2B}}\right\}\ge1-\delta.\] Comparing this interval with the target \(1-\alpha\) diagnoses undercoverage at \(P_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated calibration experiments estimate true-set coverage by a binomial proportion, with a finite-sample Hoeffding confidence band.
assumptions_latex: The \(B\) experiments are independent and identically distributed under \(P_0\).
Membership \(P_0\in\mathcal A^{(b)}\) can be evaluated exactly.
\(B\ge1\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat c_B\) estimates \(c(P_0)\) with the displayed finite-replication deviation guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binomial model and Hoeffding band are mathematically appropriate under the stated independent and identically distributed replications, and the property fits Coverage Diagnostics. However, the record has no citation for the diagnostic protocol or finite-replication guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Validation-Based Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Split-sample quantile calibration of a discrepancy-ball ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition validation data into \(K\) exchangeable batches and form batch estimators \(\widehat P^{(1)},\ldots,\widehat P^{(K)}\), independently of a training-based center \(\widehat P^{\mathrm{tr}}\). Compute scores \(S_k=d(\widehat P^{(k)},\widehat P^{\mathrm{tr}})\), sort them as \(S_{(1)}\le\cdots\le S_{(K)}\), and set \(j=\lceil(K+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\) and \(r=S_{(j)}\). Output \[\mathcal A_r=\{Q:d(Q,\widehat P^{\mathrm{tr}})\le r\}.\] For an exchangeable future batch estimator \(\widehat P^{\mathrm{new}}\), rank symmetry gives \(\Pr\{d(\widehat P^{\mathrm{new}},\widehat P^{\mathrm{tr}})\le r\}\ge1-\alpha\), using randomized tie-breaking when necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a discrepancy radius as a validation-score order statistic; exchangeability then gives finite-sample coverage for a future batch estimator.
assumptions_latex: The \(K\) validation batches and future batch are exchangeable conditional on the training data.
Score ties are broken exchangeably or handled conservatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\widehat P^{\mathrm{new}}\in\mathcal A_r)\ge1-\alpha\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-statistic procedure is an algorithm and fits a validation-calibration topic, but its guarantee covers an exchangeable future batch estimator rather than the unknown data-generating distribution itself. Without a source, it is unclear whether this is the intended validation-based DRO calibration result or a conformal-style surrogate guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multistage ambiguity specified through admissible conditional distributions at each history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_T\) be standard Borel spaces and let \(h_t=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t)\) denote a history. For each \(t<T\) and history \(h_t\), prescribe a nonempty set \(\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\) of probability kernels on \(\Xi_{t+1}\), together with an initial-law set \(\mathcal K_1\). The stagewise ambiguity family is \[\mathfrak P=\left\{Q:Q_1\in\mathcal K_1,\ Q_{t+1}(\cdot\mid h_t)\in\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\ \text{for }Q\text{-almost every }h_t,\ t<T\right\}.\] Measurable kernel selections are required so that their iterated product defines a path measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise ambiguity constrains the initial law and every subsequent conditional distribution through history-dependent kernel sets.
assumptions_latex: All uncertainty spaces are standard Borel.
The kernel multifunctions admit measurable selections.
Regular conditional distributions are taken in fixed measurable versions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P\) is the family of path laws satisfying every stagewise conditional ambiguity constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct definitional role and local topic, but the objects denoted by the history-indexed sets require a sourced convention: at a fixed history they are normally sets of probability measures, whereas measurable selections across histories form kernels. A source is needed to validate the precise stagewise construction and null-history treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Transport Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-law ambiguity defined by a ball in nested, information-respecting transport distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be probability laws on \(\Xi_1\times\cdots\times\Xi_T\), and let \(c_t:\Xi_t\times\Xi_t\to[0,\infty)\) be measurable stage costs. A coupling \(\pi\) of \(P\) and \(Q\) is bicausal when, in both coordinate directions, the conditional distribution of each history through stage \(t\) given the entire opposite path depends only on the opposite history through \(t\). For \(p\ge1\), define \[d_{\mathrm{nest},p}(P,Q)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{bc}}(P,Q)}\left(\int\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(\xi_t,\zeta_t)^p\,d\pi(\xi,\zeta)\right)^{1/p}.\] The radius-\(\varepsilon\) nested-transport ambiguity set around \(\widehat P\) is \(\{Q:d_{\mathrm{nest},p}(Q,\widehat P)\le\varepsilon\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested-transport ambiguity consists of path laws close to a reference law under transport couplings that respect information in both temporal directions.
assumptions_latex: The path spaces are standard Borel.
The displayed transport integral is well defined.
At least one finite-cost bicausal coupling exists for relevant law pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{Q:d_{\mathrm{nest},p}(Q,\widehat P)\le\varepsilon\}\) is the nested-transport ambiguity ball.

notation.meaning: bicausal couplings of P and Q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A bicausal transport ball is an appropriate definition for Nested-Transport Ambiguity. The prose description of bicausality and the stage-cost convention are source-sensitive, however, and no citation is provided to establish that the displayed formula is the intended nested-distance variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Rectangularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangularity as closure under historywise selection and pasting of conditional laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak P\) be a family of path laws on a finite-horizon standard Borel space. For every stage and history, let \(\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\) be the collection of conditional kernels arising from laws in \(\mathfrak P\), and let \(\mathcal K_1\) be the corresponding collection of initial laws. The family is distributionally rectangular if \[\mathfrak P=\left\{Q_1\otimes q_2\otimes\cdots\otimes q_T:Q_1\in\mathcal K_1,\ q_{t+1}(\cdot\mid h_t)\in\mathcal K_{t+1}(h_t)\ \text{at every stage, up to null histories}\right\},\] where every admissible measurable historywise selection may be pasted independently of selections at other histories and stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distribution family is rectangular when admissible conditional laws can be selected and pasted independently across stages and histories.
assumptions_latex: Regular conditional kernels exist.
All selected kernels are measurable.
Equality is interpreted modulo conditional laws on null histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak P\) equals its historywise conditional-kernel pasting hull.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected content kind is correct and the pasting-hull idea matches Distributional Rectangularity. The construction of conditional-kernel sections from a family of laws, especially on null histories, depends on versions and on the exact rectangularity convention. The existing assumptions do not replace an authoritative source for that variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive robust expectations under a rectangular family of probability laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,P^*)\) be a finite filtered probability space, and let \(\mathfrak P\) be a nonempty family of laws dominated by \(P^*\) and stable under conditional pasting. For bounded \(Z\), define the conditional robust expectation \[\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathfrak P_t}E_Q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t],\] where \(\mathfrak P_t\) contains the admissible continuations after time \(t\). Then rectangularity yields the recursion \[\rho_t(Z)=\rho_t\bigl(\rho_{t+1}(Z)\bigr),\qquad t<T.\] Consequently, an action that is robustly optimal from time zero remains optimal for every reached continuation problem, subject to a measurable optimizer-selection condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangular ambiguity makes worst-case conditional expectation recursive, so robust plans remain optimal when continuation problems are reconsidered.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity family is nonempty, dominated, and stable under conditional pasting.
\(Z\) is bounded and \(\mathcal F_T\)-measurable.
Continuation optimizers admit measurable selections when policy optimality is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(Z)=\rho_t(\rho_{t+1}(Z))\) for every \(t<T\), implying distributional time consistency.

notation.meaning: admissible continuation-law family at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive robust-expectation result is theorem-level knowledge appropriate to the node, but the continuation families and the meaning of conditional expectations under changing laws are not defined precisely enough to verify the recursion. The further claim that every time-zero robustly optimal action remains continuation-optimal requires a fully specified dynamic decision problem, not only measurable optimizer selection. A source is necessary to select and state the correct dominated finite-horizon theorem.
