knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Revelation Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information patterns represented by nested observation maps or their generated sigma-fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi=(\xi_1,ldots,\xi_T)\) be the full uncertainty path. An uncertainty-revelation pattern is a sequence of measurable observation maps \(R_t\) with observed history \(Y_t=R_t(\xi)\) and information sigma-field \[\mathcal G_t=\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_t),\qquad \mathcal G_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal G_T.\] Two uncertainty paths are indistinguishable at stage \(t\) exactly when their observation histories coincide. A stage-\(t\) decision rule is compatible with this pattern only if it is constant on every such indistinguishability class, equivalently if it is \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation maps specify what uncertainty has been revealed; their nested sigma-fields determine which paths a decision rule may distinguish.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty and observation spaces are measurable spaces.
Every \(R_t\) is measurable.
Information is retained, so the generated sigma-fields are nested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_t=\sigma(Y_0,\ldots,Y_t)\) represents the information available for the stage-\(t\) decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The observation-map representation fits the terminal container, but the uncertainty path is written as \(\xi=(\xi_1,ldots,\xi_T)\), where `ldots` is malformed mathematical notation. More importantly, no source is supplied for the asserted equivalence between constancy on observation fibers and sigma-field measurability, whose factorization conditions depend on the measurable spaces involved.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative Policy Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy spaces restricted to decisions measurable with currently available information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal G_t)_{t=0}^T\) be the information filtration and let \(X_t\) be the measurable action space at stage \(t\). The nonanticipative policy space is \[\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}=\left\{\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_T):\pi_t:\Omega\to X_t\text{ is }\mathcal G_t\text{-measurable for every }t\right\}.\] If \(\mathcal G_t\) is generated by an observed history map \(H_t\), this is equivalent to requiring a measurable function \(f_t\) such that \(\pi_t=f_t\circ H_t\). Hence two scenarios with the same observed history through stage \(t\) must receive the same stage-\(t\) action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonanticipative policy chooses each action measurably from information already revealed and assigns equal actions to indistinguishable histories.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal G_t)\) is an increasing filtration.
Each action space \(X_t\) is measurable.
The history factorization statement uses standard Borel observation spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}\) exactly when every component \(\pi_t\) uses no information beyond \(\mathcal G_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of policies adapted to the available-information filtration fits Nonanticipative Policy Spaces. The claimed factorization \(\pi_t=f_t\circ H_t\) needs suitable measurable-space hypotheses on both the history representation and action space; specifying only a standard Borel observation space is not enough as written. No source is cited to resolve the required version.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite information filtration encoded by nodes and common scenario prefixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite scenario tree has node sets \(N_t\) at stages \(t=0,\ldots,T\), a unique parent for every nonroot node, and leaves representing complete scenarios. For a leaf \(\omega\), let \(n_t(\omega)\in N_t\) be its stage-\(t\) ancestor. The available information is the partition \[\mathcal P_t=\bigl\{\{\omega:n_t(\omega)=n\}:n\in N_t\bigr\},\] and \(\mathcal G_t=\sigma(\mathcal P_t)\). Because every stage-\(t+1\) node has a stage-\(t\) parent, \(\mathcal G_t\subseteq\mathcal G_{t+1}\). A policy is nonanticipative precisely when \(x_t(\omega)=x_t(\omega')\) whenever \(n_t(\omega)=n_t(\omega')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario tree groups scenarios sharing the same history; nodewise-constant decisions are exactly the nonanticipative decisions.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and rooted.
Each leaf determines one complete uncertainty scenario.
Every node except the root has a unique parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G_t=\sigma(\mathcal P_t)\) is the scenario-tree information filtration, and feasible decisions are nodewise constant.

knowledge_statements.title: Filtration-Based Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract nonanticipative information modeled by a filtration on the uncertainty space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a measurable uncertainty space \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\), a filtration is an increasing family of sub-sigma-fields \[\mathcal G_0\subseteq\mathcal G_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal G_T\subseteq\mathcal F.\] The sigma-field \(\mathcal G_t\) contains exactly the events whose occurrence is observable when the stage-\(t\) action is selected. A random state or observation \(Y_t\) is available at stage \(t\) when it is \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable, while an action process \((x_t)_{t=0}^T\) is adapted when every \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable. Adaptedness is the filtration-based nonanticipativity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filtration records accumulated observable events; states and actions available at a stage must be measurable with respect to its sigma-field.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F)\) is a measurable space.
The horizon \(T\) is finite.
Action and observation spaces carry specified sigma-fields.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_t)\) is nonanticipative exactly when it is adapted to \((\mathcal G_t)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The filtration and adaptedness definitions are standard, internally consistent, and well matched to Filtration-Based Information. Nevertheless, the record contains no citation or explicit standard-field rationale, so it does not satisfy the evidence requirement for candidate-review knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous second-stage decisions in a two-stage robust optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal U\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) contain no integrality restrictions. A two-stage model has continuous recourse when, after observing \(u\in\mathcal U\), its second-stage decision may be any \(y(u)\in Y\) satisfying \[W(u)y(u)\ge h(u)-T(u)x.\] For a first-stage decision \(x\in X\), the recourse value is \[Q(x,u)=\inf\{q(u)^\top y:y\in Y,\ W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x\},\] with \(Q(x,u)=+\infty\) when the displayed feasible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recourse is continuous when every post-observation decision ranges over a nonintegral subset of Euclidean space and satisfies the scenario-specific second-stage constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\).
\(u\in\mathcal U\) is observed before choosing \(y(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x,u)\) is the optimal continuous second-stage value, or \(+\infty\) if recourse is infeasible.

notation.meaning: continuous recourse decision after observing uncertainty

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure or mixed-integer second-stage decisions in two-stage robust optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal U\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_c}\times\mathbb Z^{m_i}\) with \(m_i\ge1\). A two-stage model has integer recourse when, after observing \(u\in\mathcal U\), the decision \(y(u)\in Y\) must satisfy \[W(u)y(u)\ge h(u)-T(u)x.\] Its recourse value is \[Q_I(x,u)=\inf\{q(u)^\top y:y\in Y,\ W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x\},\] where \(Q_I(x,u)=+\infty\) if no admissible mixed-integer recourse decision exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer recourse requires at least one post-observation decision component to be integral while satisfying the scenario-specific second-stage constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_c}\times\mathbb Z^{m_i}\) with \(m_i\ge1\).
\(u\in\mathcal U\) is observed before choosing \(y(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_I(x,u)\) is the optimal mixed-integer recourse value, or \(+\infty\) when infeasible.

notation.meaning: numbers of continuous and integer recourse components

children.title: Fixed-Recourse Matrices
children.top_down_role: Recourse structures whose corrective-action coefficients remain uncertainty independent.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Recourse Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage robust models whose recourse technology is uncertainty independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider second-stage constraints \[Wy(u)\ge h(u)-T(u)x\] for \(x\in X\), \(u\in\mathcal U\), and \(y(u)\in Y\). The model has fixed recourse when a single matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\) multiplies every recourse decision for every uncertainty realization. The right-hand side \(h(u)-T(u)x\), the objective coefficient \(q(u)\), and the selected decision \(y(u)\) may depend on \(u\); fixed recourse requires only that the recourse matrix itself satisfy \(W(u)=W\) throughout \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed recourse uses the same second-stage technology matrix in every uncertainty realization, although costs, right-hand sides, and recourse decisions may vary.
assumptions_latex: \(W(u)\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\) is defined for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(u)=W\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\).

children.title: Variable-Recourse Matrices
children.top_down_role: Recourse structures whose corrective-action coefficients vary with uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Recourse Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage robust models with uncertainty-dependent recourse technology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider second-stage constraints \[W(u)y(u)\ge h(u)-T(u)x\] for \(x\in X\), \(u\in\mathcal U\), and \(y(u)\in Y\). The model has variable recourse when the matrix multiplying the recourse decision is itself uncertainty dependent: there exist \(u_1,u_2\in\mathcal U\) such that \(W(u_1)\ne W(u_2)\). Thus the feasible adjustment technology, rather than only its right-hand side or cost, changes with the realized uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable recourse occurs when uncertainty changes the matrix multiplying the post-observation decision, so the feasible adjustment technology varies across realizations.
assumptions_latex: \(W:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^{p\times m}\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(\cdot)\) is nonconstant on \(\mathcal U\).

children.title: Recourse-Structure Consequences
children.top_down_role: Tractability and feasibility consequences of fixed versus variable recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Structure Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible-set consequence for continuous linear fixed versus variable recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y=\mathbb R_+^m\), recourse is continuous and linear, and \[Q(x,u)=\inf\{q^\top y:Wy\ge h(u)-T(u)x,\ y\ge0\}.\] Whenever linear-programming strong duality applies, \[Q(x,u)=\sup_{\pi\ge0}\{\pi^\top(h(u)-T(u)x):W^\top\pi\le q\}.\] Hence fixed \(W\) and \(q\) give one uncertainty-independent dual feasible set. If \(W=W(u)\), the dual restriction becomes \(W(u)^\top\pi\le q(u)\), so its feasible set generally varies with \(u\), obstructing direct reuse of fixed-recourse dual reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed continuous linear recourse yields a common dual feasible region; variable recourse generally makes that region scenario dependent and complicates robust reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=\mathbb R_+^m\) and the recourse problem is linear.
For each evaluated \((x,u)\), primal-dual strong duality applies.
In the fixed-recourse case, \(W\) and \(q\) are uncertainty independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed recourse yields \(\{\pi\ge0:W^\top\pi\le q\}\) independent of \(u\); variable recourse generally does not.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed LP dual and common-dual-region consequence are mathematically standard, but the cited recourse-problems locator does not specifically support the strong-duality formulation or the claimed obstruction to fixed-recourse reformulations. A duality or robust-reformulation section/theorem locator is required.

children.title: Complete Robust Recourse
children.top_down_role: Recourse availability across the full relevant right-hand-side regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Robust Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform ability of each recourse technology to generate every possible right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), let \(\mathcal U\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(W(u)\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\). The model has complete robust recourse when \[\forall u\in\mathcal U\;\forall r\in\mathbb R^p\;\exists y\in Y:\quad W(u)y\ge r.\] Equivalently, for every uncertainty realization, the upper image \(W(u)Y-\mathbb R_+^p\) equals \(\mathbb R^p\). This condition is independent of a particular first-stage decision or realized model right-hand side and therefore implies feasibility of recourse for every pair \((x,u)\) whenever the right-hand side is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete robust recourse means that every scenario’s recourse technology can satisfy every finite right-hand side, independently of the first-stage decision.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\).
\(W(u)\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(u)Y-\mathbb R_+^p=\mathbb R^p\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: image of admissible recourse decisions under scenario technology

children.title: Relatively Complete Robust Recourse
children.top_down_role: Recourse availability conditional on admissible first-stage decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relatively Complete Robust Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recourse feasibility restricted to admissible first-stage decisions and modeled uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the set of decisions satisfying all first-stage constraints. A two-stage robust model has relatively complete robust recourse when \[\forall x\in X_0\;\forall u\in\mathcal U\;\exists y\in Y:\quad W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x.\] Unlike complete robust recourse, this condition requires feasibility only for right-hand sides generated by admissible \(x\) and modeled \(u\). Consequently, the worst-case recourse value is never \(+\infty\) because of second-stage infeasibility for any \(x\in X_0\), provided every feasible recourse problem has a finite objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relatively complete robust recourse requires a feasible adjustment for every admissible first-stage decision and every uncertainty realization, but not for arbitrary right-hand sides.
assumptions_latex: \(X_0\) is the first-stage feasible set.
\(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is the recourse decision set.
\(W(u),h(u),T(u)\) are defined for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall(x,u)\in X_0\times\mathcal U,\ \{y\in Y:W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x\}\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: first-stage feasible set before robust recourse requirements

children.title: Conditional Feasibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary separating complete recourse from first-stage-dependent recourse feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Feasibility Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating first-stage decisions with and without robustly feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the recourse-feasible correspondence \[R(x,u)=\{y\in Y:W(u)y\ge h(u)-T(u)x\},\] define the robustly extendable first-stage set by \[X_R=\{x\in X_0:R(x,u)\ne\varnothing\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\}.\] The conditional feasibility boundary is the relative boundary \(\operatorname{rbd}_{X_0}(X_R)\) taken in the affine hull of \(X_0\). Decisions in \(X_R\) admit feasible recourse for every modeled realization; decisions in \(X_0\setminus X_R\) fail for at least one realization. Relative complete robust recourse holds exactly when \(X_R=X_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional feasibility boundary separates admissible first-stage decisions that possess recourse in every scenario from those that fail in at least one scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(X_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(R(x,u)\) is defined for every \((x,u)\in X_0\times\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rbd}_{X_0}(X_R)\) is the robust-recourse feasibility boundary, and \(X_R=X_0\) exactly under relative complete robust recourse.

notation.meaning: first-stage decisions extendable under every scenario
relative boundary within the affine hull of the first-stage domain

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the named conditional-feasibility boundary or the selected relative-boundary convention. A source must establish the terminology and whether the leaf should contain a definition rather than a condition before the mathematical formulation can be approved.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Induced Robust Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario certificate that a first-stage decision lacks feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X_0\), recourse-induced robust infeasibility occurs when \[\exists \bar u\in\mathcal U:\quad \{y\in Y:W(\bar u)y\ge h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x\}=\varnothing.\] Thus one uncertainty realization \(\bar u\) with an empty recourse-feasible set certifies that \(x\) is not robustly extendable. In continuous linear recourse with \(Y=\mathbb R_+^m\), a verifiable alternative certificate is a vector \(\pi\ge0\) satisfying \[W(\bar u)^\top\pi\le0,\qquad \pi^\top(h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x)>0,\] under the standard finite-dimensional theorem of alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-stage decision is robustly infeasible when one modeled scenario admits no recourse; in linear continuous models, a separating multiplier can certify this failure.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in X_0\) and \(\bar u\in\mathcal U\).
For the multiplier certificate, \(Y=\mathbb R_+^m\) and all data are finite dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The witness \(\bar u\), optionally with \(\pi\), certifies \(x\notin X_R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario witness and multiplier inequalities are mathematically plausible, but the cited recourse locator does not specifically support the theorem-of-alternatives certificate. The leaf title describes a failure phenomenon, so the certificate content kind also requires reconsideration once a precise source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Causal worst-case feasibility and performance over finitely many stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a horizon \(T<\infty\), uncertainty histories \(u_{1:t}=(u_1,\ldots,u_t)\), and causal policies \(\pi=(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_T)\) with \(x_t=\pi_t(u_{1:t})\). A policy is finite-horizon robustly feasible when every constraint \[g_t(x_{1:t},u_{1:t})\le0\] holds for every \(t=1,\ldots,T\) and every admissible history \(u_{1:T}\in\mathcal U_{1:T}\). Its robust value is \[V_T=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_T}\sup_{u_{1:T}\in\mathcal U_{1:T}}\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(x_{1:t},u_{1:t}),\] where infeasible policies have value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon robustness requires a causal policy to satisfy every stage constraint for every admissible uncertainty history through a fixed terminal stage.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
Each \(\pi_t\) is nonanticipative and uses only \(u_{1:t}\).
\(\mathcal U_{1:T}\) is the set of admissible histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_T\) is the worst-case finite-horizon value over causally robust-feasible policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Horizon Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discounted causal worst-case feasibility and performance over infinitely many stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta\in(0,1)\), let \(u_{1:\infty}\in\mathcal U_\infty\), and let \(x_t=\pi_t(u_{1:t})\) be a causal policy. The policy is infinite-horizon robustly feasible when \(g_t(x_{1:t},u_{1:t})\le0\) for every \(t\ge1\) and every admissible infinite history. If stage costs are uniformly bounded, its discounted robust value is \[V_\infty=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_\infty}\sup_{u_{1:\infty}\in\mathcal U_\infty}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\beta^{t-1}c_t(x_{1:t},u_{1:t}).\] Uniform boundedness and \(\beta<1\) ensure convergence of every displayed cost series.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite-horizon robustness requires causal feasibility at every time for every admissible infinite history, with discounted bounded costs giving a well-defined worst-case value.
assumptions_latex: Each policy component \(\pi_t\) is nonanticipative.
There exists \(C<\infty\) with \(|c_t|\le C\) uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_\infty\) is finite whenever at least one robustly feasible policy exists and all stage costs are uniformly bounded.

children.title: Rectangular Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty structures permitting independent recombination across stages or histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Historywise uncertainty sets closed under independent admissible continuation choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(\mathcal U_t(u_{1:t-1})\) be the admissible set of stage-\(t\) uncertainties after history \(u_{1:t-1}\). The multistage uncertainty set is rectangular when \[\mathcal U_{1:T}=\{u_{1:T}:u_1\in\mathcal U_1,\ u_t\in\mathcal U_t(u_{1:t-1})\ \text{for }t=2,\ldots,T\}.\] Equivalently, any sequence obtained by selecting an admissible continuation at each reached history remains globally admissible; there is no additional cross-history or whole-path constraint coupling those selections. If every \(\mathcal U_t\) is history independent, this reduces to the Cartesian product \(\mathcal U_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal U_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangular uncertainty permits any sequence of locally admissible stagewise continuations, without an additional constraint coupling choices across the entire path.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
Each correspondence \(\mathcal U_t(u_{1:t-1})\) is nonempty on admissible histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global admissibility is exactly equivalent to stage-by-stage membership in the conditional uncertainty correspondences.

notation.meaning: set of admissible complete uncertainty paths
admissible next-stage uncertainty after a history

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general robust-optimization page does not specifically support this history-dependent notion of rectangularity. Because rectangularity can mean Cartesian stagewise independence, recursive/pasting stability, or rectangular ambiguity sets, a dedicated definition or theorem locator is needed to validate the stated equivalence and exclude a merely tautological conditional representation.

children.title: Stagewise Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty organized according to the stages at which parameters are realized.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon uncertainty revealed sequentially under a nonanticipative information pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a horizon \(T\) and disturbance spaces \(\mathcal W_t\). A stagewise uncertainty process is a vector \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_T)\in\mathcal U\subseteq\prod_{t=1}^T\mathcal W_t\) whose component \(w_t\) is revealed at stage \(t\). If the stage-\(t\) decision precedes that revelation, an admissible decision rule has the form \(x_t=\pi_t(w_{1:t-1})\). Thus two scenarios agreeing through stage \(t-1\) must induce the same \(x_t\). This definition imposes an information structure but does not require independence or rectangularity of \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncertainty is revealed one stage at a time, and each decision may use only previously revealed disturbances; the scenario set may still couple stages.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
Each \(\mathcal W_t\) is a specified measurable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t=\pi_t(w_{1:t-1})\) is nonanticipative for every \(t\).

notation.meaning: Disturbance history available before the stage-t decision.
Set of admissible complete disturbance scenarios.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Stagewise Uncertainty leaf and consistently states the decision-before-revelation information pattern, but no inspectable citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Interstage Coupling Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary where temporal dependence prevents rectangular stagewise decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Interstage Coupling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp product-set boundary between stagewise rectangular and interstage-coupled scenario sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\prod_{t=1}^T\mathcal W_t\) be nonempty and let \(P_t\mathcal U\) denote its stage-\(t\) projection. The uncertainty set is stagewise uncoupled precisely when \(\mathcal U=\prod_{t=1}^T P_t\mathcal U\). Interstage coupling occurs at the strict boundary \(\mathcal U\subsetneq\prod_{t=1}^T P_t\mathcal U\): then some vector assembled from individually admissible stage values is not an admissible scenario. Consequently, replacing \(\mathcal U\) by the product of its projections enlarges the adversary's scenario set and can strictly increase a minimization problem's robust value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling begins when admissible values from separate stages cannot be combined arbitrarily; replacing the set by its stagewise projections is then a conservative enlargement.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
The robust problem minimizes a worst-case objective over \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U\subsetneq\prod_tP_t\mathcal U\) implies that product rectangularization can be strictly conservative.

notation.meaning: Projection of the scenario set onto stage t.
Product rectangularization of the scenario set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary product-set characterization of interstage coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-of-projections boundary is mathematically coherent and failure_boundary is appropriate, but the characterization and robust-value consequence have no inspectable supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Dependent Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional uncertainty sets whose admissible continuation depends on the realized disturbance history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(T<\infty\). For every stage \(t\), let \(\mathcal U_t(h_{t-1})\subseteq\mathcal W_t\) be a nonempty conditional uncertainty set indexed by the preceding history \(h_{t-1}=w_{1:t-1}\). The induced scenario set is \[\mathcal U=\{w: w_1\in\mathcal U_1,\; w_t\in\mathcal U_t(w_{1:t-1})\text{ for }t=2,\ldots,T\}.\] The uncertainty is history-dependent when \(\mathcal U_t(h)\neq\mathcal U_t(h')\) for some stage \(t\) and feasible histories \(h,h'\). Decisions remain nonanticipative functions of the history observed before they are selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History-dependent uncertainty assigns different admissible next-stage disturbances to different past disturbance histories while retaining nonanticipative decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
Every conditional set \(\mathcal U_t(h_{t-1})\) is nonempty on feasible histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible continuation at stage \(t\) is determined by \(\mathcal U_t(w_{1:t-1})\).

notation.meaning: Observed disturbance history before stage t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conditional-set model for multistage uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-set definition matches history-dependent uncertainty and is internally consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports the selected convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affinely Adjustable Robust Counterpart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the affine-decision-rule restriction of an adjustable uncertain conic program under a prescribed information base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c_\zeta,d_\zeta,A_\zeta,b_\zeta\) be affine in \(\zeta\), let \(\mathbf K\) be a direct product of nonnegative rays, Lorentz cones, and semidefinite cones, and let \(\mathcal Z=\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^d:\exists u,\ \mathcal P(\zeta,u)\succeq0\}\) be convex and compact with a strictly feasible semidefinite representation. Given information matrices \(P_j\), restrict the decisions to \(x_j(\zeta)=p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta\). The affinely adjustable robust counterpart is
\[
\min_{t,\{p_j,q_j\}_{j=1}^n}\left\{t:\begin{array}{l}
\sum_{j=1}^n c_\zeta^j(p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta)+d_\zeta\le t,\\
\sum_{j=1}^n A_\zeta^j(p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta)+b_\zeta\in\mathbf K
\end{array}\quad\forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affinely perturbed uncertain conic problem with a prescribed information base, the affinely adjustable robust counterpart restricts each decision to an affine function of the information available to it and optimizes the affine coefficients subject to the objective and conic constraints holding for every uncertainty realization.
assumptions_latex: c_\zeta,d_\zeta,A_\zeta,b_\zeta\text{ are affine in }\zeta
\mathbf K\text{ is a direct product of nonnegative rays, Lorentz cones, and semidefinite cones}
\mathcal Z=\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^d:\exists u,\ \mathcal P(\zeta,u)\succeq0\}\text{ is convex and compact and has a strictly feasible SDP representation}
\{P_j\}_{j=1}^n\text{ is the prescribed information base}
x_j(\zeta)=p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta\quad(j=1,\ldots,n)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{AARC}=\min_{t,\{p_j,q_j\}}\left\{t:\sum_jc_\zeta^j(p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta)+d_\zeta\le t,\ \sum_jA_\zeta^j(p_j+q_j^TP_j\zeta)+b_\zeta\in\mathbf K\ \forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Disturbance-Affine Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Causal affine policies parameterized directly by previously observed disturbances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a horizon \(T\), a disturbance-affine decision rule is a nonanticipative policy whose stage-\(t\) action satisfies \[u_t(w_{1:t-1})=u_t^0+\sum_{s=1}^{t-1}K_{t,s}w_s,\qquad t=1,\ldots,T.\] Here \(u_t^0\) and \(K_{t,s}\) are decision variables of compatible dimensions. The absence of terms involving \(w_s\) with \(s\geq t\) enforces causality. If the current disturbance is observed before acting, the same convention replaces the upper summation index by \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each action is an affine function of disturbances observed before that action, with the coefficient pattern enforcing causality.
assumptions_latex: \(w_s\in\mathbb R^{q_s}\) and \(u_t\in\mathbb R^{m_t}\).
The stage-\(t\) action is chosen before observing \(w_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t\) depends only on \(w_{1:t-1}\) and is therefore nonanticipative.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical causal affine disturbance-feedback parameterization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The causal disturbance-affine representation matches the leaf and clearly fixes the observation timing, but it lacks an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Affine Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine feedback policies expressed in terms of the observed system state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a controlled system with an observed state \(x_t\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\) available when the stage-\(t\) action is selected. A state-affine rule has the form \[u_t=k_t+K_tx_t,\qquad t=1,\ldots,T,\] where \(k_t\in\mathbb R^{m_t}\) and \(K_t\in\mathbb R^{m_t\times n_t}\) are policy parameters. The rule is nonanticipative whenever \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the information available at stage \(t\). If the state is not fully observed, this representation requires an admissible state estimate in place of \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state-affine policy chooses each action as an affine function of the currently observed state, or of an admissible state estimate under partial observation.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is available before \(u_t\) is chosen.
\(u_t\in\mathbb R^{m_t}\) and \(x_t\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t=k_t+K_tx_t\) defines a causal affine state-feedback policy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state-affine representation and its measurability condition are appropriate for the leaf, but no authoritative source and locator are provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Purified-Output Affine Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine output-feedback policies using innovations that remove the policy-induced nominal response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_t\) be the measured output and let \(\widehat y_t\) be the output predicted by the same causal model after suppressing exogenous disturbances while retaining the realized past controls. Define the purified output \(v_t=y_t-\widehat y_t\). A purified-output affine rule is \[u_t=u_t^0+\sum_{s=1}^{t}L_{t,s}v_s,\] when \(y_t\) is observed before \(u_t\); otherwise the sum ends at \(t-1\). The triangular coefficient pattern makes the rule causal, and purification isolates the output component generated by uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy is affine in output innovations obtained by subtracting the disturbance-free prediction, with summation limits determined by the observation timing.
assumptions_latex: A causal model defines \(\widehat y_t\) from information available when \(y_t\) is received.
The observation timing relative to \(u_t\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triangular gains \(L_{t,s}\) define a nonanticipative affine purified-output policy.

notation.meaning: Purified output or output innovation at stage t.
Gain from purified output s to action t.

review_flags: exact purification convention requires authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but purified-output conventions depend on the underlying causal model and information pattern. The supplied definition has no source from which its exact suppression and prediction convention can be verified.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Partition Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-affine policies over history partitions chosen before optimization or execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage \(t\), let \(\{C_{t,1},\ldots,C_{t,J_t}\}\) be a finite, disjoint partition of the observable history space, fixed independently of the policy parameters and realized scenario. A fixed-partition piecewise-affine rule is \[u_t(h)=a_{t,j}+B_{t,j}h\quad\text{whenever }h\in C_{t,j}.\] Every feasible history belongs to exactly one cell, with a prescribed tie convention on cell boundaries. Because both cell membership and the selected affine piece depend only on the observed history, the resulting policy is nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predetermined partition divides observable histories into cells, and a separate affine action rule is used on each cell.
assumptions_latex: The cells \(C_{t,j}\) form a finite partition of the stage-\(t\) history space.
Cell membership is decidable from information available at stage \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t(h)=a_{t,j}+B_{t,j}h\) on \(C_{t,j}\) defines a nonanticipative piecewise-affine rule.

notation.meaning: Fixed history cell j at stage t.
Observable history at the decision stage.
Affine parameters assigned to a cell.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard fixed-partition piecewise-affine policy definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes a fixed history partition with cellwise affine rules, but no inspectable source supports this terminology and formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Partition Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-affine policies whose causal partition refinement responds to observed histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive-partition rule is represented by a finite policy tree. At stage \(t\), the node reached by history \(h_t\) may be split using predicates measurable with respect to \(h_t\); each resulting leaf \(\ell\) carries an affine rule \(u_t(h_t)=a_{t,\ell}+B_{t,\ell}h_t\). The split chosen along a scenario may depend on observations already revealed, but not on future disturbances. A deterministic boundary convention assigns every feasible history to one leaf. Hence the realized partition can vary across histories while the policy remains nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The history partition is refined along a causal policy tree, and each reached leaf applies its own affine rule.
assumptions_latex: Every branching predicate uses only the currently observed history.
The policy tree is finite and has a deterministic boundary convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each feasible history reaches one leaf \(\ell\), and \(u_t(h_t)=a_{t,\ell}+B_{t,\ell}h_t\) is nonanticipative.

notation.meaning: Information history available at stage t.
Leaf reached by the observed history.
Affine parameters attached to a leaf.

review_flags: adaptive-partition convention varies across robust-optimization formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy-tree formulation is plausible, but adaptive-partition rules have formulation-dependent meanings. An authoritative source is required to verify that this exact causal refinement convention matches the intended leaf.

children.title: Polynomial Decision Rules
children.top_down_role: Adaptive policies parameterized through polynomial dependence on observed uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Decision Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Causal policies polynomial in the disturbance history up to a prescribed degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_t=(w_1,\ldots,w_{t-1})\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\) be the disturbance history available before the stage-\(t\) action. A polynomial decision rule of total degree at most \(d\) is \[u_t(z_t)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^{n_t}:\,|\alpha|\leq d}c_{t,\alpha}z_t^\alpha,\] where \(z_t^\alpha=\prod_{i=1}^{n_t}(z_t)_i^{\alpha_i}\) and the coefficients \(c_{t,\alpha}\) are decision variables. Dependence only on \(z_t\) enforces nonanticipativity; degree \(d=1\) recovers disturbance-affine rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each action is a polynomial of bounded total degree in previously observed disturbances; affine disturbance feedback is the degree-one special case.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N_0\).
The history vector satisfies \(z_t\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed polynomial defines a causal decision rule, with the affine family obtained when \(d=1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard multivariate polynomial policy parameterization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-total-degree polynomial rule is precise, causal, and correctly contains disturbance-affine rules at degree one, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Lifted Decision Rules
children.top_down_role: Adaptive policies represented through auxiliary lifted variables or features.

assumptions_latex: \(z_t\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\) contains only information available at stage \(t\).
The feature map \(\phi_t\) is fixed independently of future uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t=a_t+B_t\phi_t(z_t)\) is affine in lifted coordinates and causal in the original history.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the lifted feature vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine policies in a prescribed nonlinear feature lift of observable history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage \(t\), choose a fixed feature map \(\phi_t:\mathbb R^{n_t}\to\mathbb R^{p_t}\) of the available history \(z_t\). A lifted decision rule has the representation \[u_t(z_t)=a_t+B_t\phi_t(z_t),\] where \(a_t\) and \(B_t\) are optimization variables while \(\phi_t\) is fixed before solving the robust problem. The rule is nonanticipative when every component of \(\phi_t(z_t)\) depends only on information available at stage \(t\). Nonlinear features permit policies nonlinear in the original history but affine in lifted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed feature map lifts the observed history, after which the action is affine in the lifted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Decision Rules

children.title: Polynomial-to-Lifted Representability
children.top_down_role: Connections between polynomial policy parameterizations and lifted representations.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\) and \(d\in\mathbb N_0\).
The lift contains every nonconstant monomial of total degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{a+B\phi_d(\cdot)\}\) equals the class of \(\mathbb R^m\)-valued polynomials of degree at most \(d\).

notation.meaning: Vector of nonconstant monomials through degree d.
Monomial indexed by the multi-index alpha.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact realization of bounded-degree polynomial policies by a monomial feature lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), and define the monomial lift \(\phi_d(z)=(z^\alpha)_{1\leq|\alpha|\leq d}\). Every vector-valued polynomial \(p:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) of total degree at most \(d\) admits coefficients \(a\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times N_d}\) such that \[p(z)=a+B\phi_d(z)\quad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb R^n,\] where \(N_d=\binom{n+d}{d}-1\). Conversely, every affine function of this monomial lift is a polynomial of total degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Including every monomial through degree d as a feature makes affine lifted rules exactly equivalent to polynomial rules of degree at most d.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-to-Lifted Representability

children.title: Expressiveness–Tractability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between policy flexibility and computational tractability.

knowledge_statements.title: Expressiveness–Tractability Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested policy expressiveness versus feature dimension and robust-constraint complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi_d\) be the causal polynomial policy class containing every monomial of history dimension \(n\) and total degree at most \(d\). Then \(\Pi_d\subseteq\Pi_{d+1}\), so for a minimization problem the optimal restricted robust values satisfy \(V_{d+1}\leq V_d\). However, each scalar action requires \(\binom{n+d}{d}\) coefficients. Substitution into uncertain constraints produces polynomial worst-case inequalities; exact finite-dimensional conic reformulation therefore requires additional structure on the uncertainty set or a valid nonnegativity certificate. Increased degree expands the policy class while increasing representation size and typically complicating robust feasibility enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-degree policies cannot worsen the restricted minimization value, but their coefficient count grows combinatorially and their robust constraints require additional tractability structure.
assumptions_latex: All classes use the same information pattern and feasible uncertainty model.
\(V_d\) is the infimum over policies in \(\Pi_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_d\subseteq\Pi_{d+1}\), \(V_{d+1}\leq V_d\), and the scalar coefficient count is \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).

notation.meaning: Causal polynomial policies of degree at most d.
Restricted robust minimization value over Pi-d.
Dimension of the available history vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested approximation classes and monomial counting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nesting, minimization-value monotonicity, and monomial count are coherent, and principle fits the tradeoff leaf. The broader tractability claim nevertheless requires an inspectable source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: K-Adaptability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-menu restriction of a two-stage robust problem with uncertainty observed before recourse selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), and a nonempty uncertainty set \(\mathcal U\) be given. Let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(G:X\times Y\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R^p\). For a menu \(y^1,\ldots,y^K\), define \(I_{x,y}(\xi)=\{k\in[K]:G(x,y^k,\xi)\leq0\}\), with the inequality interpreted componentwise. The \(K\)-adaptability value is
\[
v_K=\inf_{\substack{x\in X,\,y^1,\ldots,y^K\in Y\\ I_{x,y}(\xi)\neq\varnothing\ \forall\xi\in\mathcal U}}\left\{c^\top x+\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U}\min_{k\in I_{x,y}(\xi)}d(\xi)^\top y^k\right\}.
\]
Thus all \(K\) recourse actions are chosen before observing \(\xi\), while a feasible action's index may be selected afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: K-adaptability preselects K recourse actions and, after uncertainty is observed, uses the cheapest preselected action that is feasible for that realization.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) and \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
The infimum and extended-real worst-case objective are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_K\) is the optimal robust value attainable with at most \(K\) precomputed recourse actions.

notation.meaning: Indices of menu actions feasible under realization \(\xi\).

review_flags: A direct bibliographic source for this two-stage K-adaptability formulation is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Menu Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-wise selection representation for a fixed menu of robust recourse policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\in X\) and menu \(y^1,\ldots,y^K\in Y\), define
\[
I(\xi)=\{k\in[K]:G(x,y^k,\xi)\leq0\}.
\]
A feasible policy-menu selector is any mapping \(\kappa:\mathcal U\to[K]\) satisfying \(\kappa(\xi)\in I(\xi)\) for every \(\xi\). If ties are resolved by the smallest index, the cost-minimizing selector is
\[
\kappa(\xi)=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{k\in I(\xi)}d(\xi)^\top y^k,
\]
and its worst-case recourse cost equals \(\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U}\min_{k\in I(\xi)}d(\xi)^\top y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each realization, select a feasible menu member of minimum realized cost; this selector realizes the scenario-wise minimum appearing in K-adaptability.
assumptions_latex: \(I(\xi)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
The finite menu costs are extended-real comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U}d(\xi)^\top y^{\kappa(\xi)}=\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U}\min_{k\in I(\xi)}d(\xi)^\top y^k\).

notation.meaning: Indices of menu policies feasible under realization \(\xi\).

review_flags: A source treating measurable selection issues and the precise policy model is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-menu selector representation is mathematically consistent, but no citation supports the precise policy model or any applicable regularity convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Adaptability Approximation Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-scenario guarantee and monotonicity of the K-adaptability hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_{\mathrm{FA}}\) be the optimal value when an arbitrary recourse action \(y(\xi)\in Y\) may be selected after observing \(\xi\), and let \(v_K\) be the corresponding \(K\)-adaptability value. For a minimization problem,
\[
v_{\mathrm{FA}}\leq v_{K+1}\leq v_K.
\]
If \(\mathcal U=\{\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^N\}\) is finite and the fully adjustable problem attains an optimal recourse action for every scenario, then
\[
v_K=v_{\mathrm{FA}}\qquad\text{for every }K\geq N.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding policies cannot worsen K-adaptability. With N uncertainty scenarios, at most N policies reproduce any attained fully adjustable optimum exactly.
assumptions_latex: The compared models have identical first-stage decisions, objectives, and feasibility constraints.
\(\mathcal U\) is finite for the exactness conclusion.
An optimal fully adjustable solution and its scenario recourse actions exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{FA}}\leq v_{K+1}\leq v_K\), and \(v_K=v_{\mathrm{FA}}\) when \(K\geq|\mathcal U|\).
review_flags: The finite-scenario guarantee is standard but needs a direct robust-optimization source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity and finite-scenario exactness claims are plausible under the stated attainment assumptions, but the theorem has no direct robust-optimization source.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Uncertainty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-policy exactness obtained by interpolation over an uncertainty interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R\), with \(\ell<u\). Fix a first-stage decision \(x\), and suppose the feasible graph
\[
\mathcal F_x=\{(\xi,y)\in\mathcal U\times Y:G(x,y,\xi)\leq0\}
\]
is convex. If endpoint recourse actions \(y_\ell\) and \(y_u\) are feasible, then
\[
y(\xi)=\frac{u-\xi}{u-\ell}y_\ell+\frac{\xi-\ell}{u-\ell}y_u
\]
is affine and feasible for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\). Consequently, whenever an optimal adjustable solution is determined by feasible endpoint actions and a convex endpoint-monotone worst-case objective, an optimal affine decision rule exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, convex interpolation of feasible endpoint actions yields an affine feasible policy; under an endpoint-determined objective, affine recourse is exact.
assumptions_latex: The feasible graph in uncertainty and recourse is convex.
Feasible endpoint actions exist.
The adjustable objective is determined monotonically by endpoint costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an affine feasible policy interpolating the endpoint actions, and it is optimal under the stated endpoint-determined objective condition.

notation.meaning: Feasible graph for the fixed first-stage decision.
Recourse actions at the interval endpoints.

review_flags: Exactness depends on the objective condition; a canonical theorem and source must be selected.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Convex-graph interpolation is valid, but “endpoint-monotone” and “determined by endpoint actions” do not formally specify an objective class sufficient for the asserted optimality. A canonical sourced theorem is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Uncertainty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-policy exactness by barycentric interpolation on a simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{v^0,\ldots,v^d\}\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a simplex. Fix \(x\), assume the feasible graph \(\mathcal F_x=\{(\xi,y):G(x,y,\xi)\leq0\}\) is convex, and choose feasible vertex actions \(y^0,\ldots,y^d\). Every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\) has barycentric coordinates \(\lambda_i(\xi)\), and
\[
y(\xi)=\sum_{i=0}^d\lambda_i(\xi)y^i
\]
is affine and feasible throughout \(\mathcal U\). If the worst-case objective is convex in \((\xi,y)\), its value under this policy is bounded by the largest vertex cost; hence vertex-determined adjustable optima admit an exact affine rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a simplex, barycentric interpolation of feasible vertex actions is affine and feasible. Convex worst-case costs are controlled by vertex costs, yielding exactness when vertices determine the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set is a nondegenerate simplex.
The feasible graph is convex.
The realized objective is convex in uncertainty and recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y(\xi)=\sum_i\lambda_i(\xi)y^i\) is feasible, and its worst-case cost does not exceed the maximum vertex cost.
review_flags: A direct source for this precise convex-graph exactness formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Barycentric feasibility and the convex-cost vertex bound are sound, but the final exactness assertion relies on an undefined “vertex-determined” optimum and needs a precise sourced formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Structured Exactness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-recourse structure forcing the unique feasible recourse policy to be affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider equality recourse
\[
Wy(\xi)=h_0+H\xi-Tx\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]
where \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular and no additional constraints restrict \(y\). For every fixed \(x\), feasibility forces the unique policy
\[
y(\xi)=W^{-1}(h_0-Tx)+W^{-1}H\xi,
\]
which is affine in \(\xi\). Therefore any feasible fully adjustable solution already uses an affine recourse rule, and restricting the model to affine decision rules leaves both its feasible first-stage set and optimal value unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nonsingular fixed equality recourse and no other recourse restrictions, feasibility uniquely determines an affine policy, so affine-rule restriction is exact.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is square, fixed, and nonsingular.
The recourse equations are affine in \(x\) and \(\xi\).
There are no additional restrictions on \(y(\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fully adjustable and affine-rule robust problems have identical feasible first-stage decisions and identical optimal values.
review_flags: This sufficient exactness regime needs a direct fixed-recourse reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonsingular equality-recourse condition does force a unique affine policy and fits this exactness-regime container, but no direct source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case approximation ratio indexed by uncertainty dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a normalized class \(\mathfrak I_d\) of minimization instances with uncertainty contained in \(\mathbb R^d\), positive fully adjustable value \(v^*(I)\), and affine-rule value \(v_{\mathrm{aff}}(I)\), define
\[
\rho_d=\sup_{I\in\mathfrak I_d}\frac{v_{\mathrm{aff}}(I)}{v^*(I)}.
\]
A function \(g:\mathbb N\to[1,\infty]\) is a dimension-dependent affine-rule guarantee precisely when \(\rho_d\leq g(d)\) for every \(d\). If the classes are closed under embedding an instance as one independent of an added uncertainty coordinate, then \(\rho_d\leq\rho_{d+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dimension-dependent conservatism factor is the worst affine-to-adjustable value ratio among d-dimensional instances; nested instance classes make this factor nondecreasing with dimension.
assumptions_latex: Every instance is a minimization problem with \(0<v^*(I)<\infty\).
Affine policies form a restriction of fully adjustable policies.
The stated embedding closure holds for monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\leq\rho_d\leq g(d)\), and embedding closure implies \(\rho_d\leq\rho_{d+1}\).

notation.meaning: Normalized class of d-dimensional uncertainty instances.

review_flags: A specific model class and published dimension-dependent rate must be attached in a later pass.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This defines a generic ratio rather than providing a dimension-dependent bound for a specified robust model. The instance class, normalization, published rate, and appropriate bound-oriented content kind must be established from a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Dependent Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional transfer of affine-rule guarantees through geometric comparison of uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\subseteq\mathcal U\subseteq\gamma E\) for a centrally scaled reference set \(E\) and \(\gamma\geq1\). Suppose robust minimization values are monotone under set inclusion, affine recourse is exact on \(E\), and the affine value obeys the scaling stability inequality
\[
v_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathcal U)\leq v_{\mathrm{aff}}(\gamma E)\leq\gamma v_{\mathrm{aff}}(E).
\]
Then
\[
v^*(\mathcal U)\leq v_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathcal U)\leq\gamma v^*(\mathcal U).
\]
Thus the containment distortion \(\gamma\), rather than dimension alone, bounds affine-rule conservatism under these stability conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the uncertainty set lies between a reference set and its γ-dilation, exactness on the reference and scaling stability give a γ approximation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq\mathcal U\subseteq\gamma E\) with \(\gamma\geq1\).
Robust values are monotone under uncertainty-set inclusion.
Affine exactness on \(E\) and the displayed scaling stability inequality hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\leq v_{\mathrm{aff}}(\mathcal U)/v^*(\mathcal U)\leq\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Reference uncertainty set on which affine recourse is exact.

review_flags: Scaling stability is model-dependent; a sourced canonical geometry bound is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional inequality follows from the displayed assumptions, but scaling stability is model-dependent, the dilation convention is underspecified, and the ratio conclusion additionally requires a positive adjustable value. A canonical geometry bound is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse-Structure Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of affine approximation bounds across separable recourse blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose recourse decomposes into independent blocks \(i=1,\ldots,q\), with nonnegative fully adjustable costs \(v_i^*>0\) and affine-rule costs satisfying \(v_i^{\mathrm{aff}}\leq\alpha_i v_i^*\). If feasibility is blockwise separable and total cost is additive, then
\[
v^*=\sum_{i=1}^qv_i^*,\qquad v^{\mathrm{aff}}\leq\sum_{i=1}^qv_i^{\mathrm{aff}},
\]
and consequently
\[
\frac{v^{\mathrm{aff}}}{v^*}\leq
\frac{\sum_i\alpha_i v_i^*}{\sum_i v_i^*}
\leq\max_{i\in[q]}\alpha_i.
\]
Thus the worst block factor bounds the conservatism of the combined affine policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent additive recourse blocks, blockwise affine guarantees combine as a cost-weighted average and never exceed the worst block guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Recourse feasibility is separable across blocks.
The objective is the sum of nonnegative block costs.
Each block satisfies \(v_i^{\mathrm{aff}}\leq\alpha_i v_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{\mathrm{aff}}/v^*\leq(\sum_i\alpha_i v_i^*)/(\sum_i v_i^*)\leq\max_i\alpha_i\).

notation.meaning: Fully adjustable value of recourse block \(i\).

review_flags: A robust-optimization source for separable recourse composition bounds is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Additive objectives and blockwise feasibility alone do not ensure that the robust adjustable value equals the sum of block values. The uncertainty product structure and absence of shared decisions or constraints must be formalized and sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-Policy Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar robust feasibility problem separating nonlinear and affine recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=[-1,1]\) and require a scalar recourse policy to satisfy
\[
y(\xi)=\xi^2\qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal U.
\]
The nonlinear policy \(y(\xi)=\xi^2\) is feasible and has worst-case magnitude \(1\). No affine policy \(y(\xi)=a\xi+b\) is feasible: equality at \(\xi=-1,0,1\) would imply simultaneously \(-a+b=1\), \(b=0\), and \(a+b=1\), which is inconsistent. Hence restricting recourse to affine rules can turn a feasible adjustable robust problem into an infeasible one, producing an infinite feasibility or objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The requirement y(ξ)=ξ² is feasible with nonlinear recourse on an interval but impossible for every affine rule, demonstrating an unbounded affine-policy gap.
assumptions_latex: Policies must satisfy the displayed equality for every \(\xi\in[-1,1]\).
Affine policies have the form \(a\xi+b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adjustable model is feasible, whereas its affine-policy restriction is infeasible.
review_flags: Concrete construction is self-contained, but an external source or standard-field rationale is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed nonlinear-versus-affine feasibility separation is correct and its counterexample kind fits the failure-regime leaf, but it has neither an external citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Complexity Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential lower bound for constant-policy partitions on a binary uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U_d=\{-1,1\}^d\), and define the required scalar recourse action
\[
y(\xi)=\sum_{j=1}^d2^{j-1}\frac{\xi_j+1}{2}.
\]
This mapping takes \(2^d\) distinct values. Any piecewise-constant policy represented by a partition \(\mathcal U_d=P_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup P_K\) and constants \(y_k\) that satisfies the equality requirement for every \(\xi\) must therefore have
\[
K\geq2^d.
\]
The bound is attained by assigning one singleton cell to each uncertainty realization. Thus exact finite adaptability may require exponentially many regions or policies in the uncertainty dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encoding every binary uncertainty vector as a distinct required action forces any exact constant-policy partition to contain 2^d cells, and this bound is tight.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\).
Each partition cell uses one constant recourse action.
The displayed recourse equality must hold exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every exact piecewise-constant representation has \(K\geq2^d\), and a representation with \(K=2^d\) exists.
review_flags: The explicit lower-bound construction requires external sourcing or approved standard-field rationale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The injective binary encoding correctly forces and attains \(2^d\) constant-policy cells, but the complexity claim lacks external evidence or an explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Adaptability Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connected uncertainty example separating adaptive integer recourse from affine integer-valued rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U=[0,1]\), require \(y(\xi)\in\{0,1\}\), and impose
\[
|y(\xi)-\xi|\leq\tfrac12\qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal U.
\]
The adaptive integer policy \(y(\xi)=0\) for \(\xi\leq\tfrac12\) and \(y(\xi)=1\) for \(\xi>\tfrac12\) is feasible; equivalently, a two-policy menu \(\{0,1\}\) suffices. Every affine mapping from the connected interval \([0,1]\) into the discrete set \(\{0,1\}\) is constant. Neither constant policy is feasible, because \(y\equiv0\) fails at \(\xi=1\) and \(y\equiv1\) fails at \(\xi=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary adaptive recourse satisfies a half-unit tracking constraint, while every affine binary-valued policy is constant and infeasible; two-policy adaptability closes the gap.
assumptions_latex: The tracking inequality must hold for every realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptive integer recourse and \(K=2\) adaptability are feasible, but affine integer-valued recourse is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Binary recourse action selected after observing uncertainty.

review_flags: The example is self-contained but needs an external source or approved standard-field rationale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connected-domain argument correctly separates adaptive binary recourse from affine binary-valued recourse, but the counterexample lacks external evidence or an explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon state-action rectangularity for robust Markov decision processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transition ambiguity set is state-action rectangular if it has the Cartesian-product form \[\mathfrak P=\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\prod_{s}\prod_{a}\mathcal P_t(s,a).\] Thus an admissible kernel sequence \(P\in\mathfrak P\) is specified by choosing \(P_t(\cdot\mid s,a)\in\mathcal P_t(s,a)\) independently for every \((t,s,a)\). Membership imposes no coupling constraints between choices associated with different times, states, or actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition uncertainty is rectangular when every time-and-state-action conditional distribution can be selected independently from its local ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Transition Uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the terminal container, but no source is supplied for the specific finite-horizon state-action rectangular convention.

assumptions_latex: The state and action sets are finite, and the horizon is \(T<\infty\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product of the coordinate projections strictly enlarges \(\mathfrak P\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonrectangularity defined by coupling among conditional transition choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transition uncertainty is nonrectangular when the joint ambiguity set cannot be reconstructed from its coordinate projections: \[\mathfrak P\subsetneq\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\prod_s\prod_a\operatorname{proj}_{t,s,a}\mathfrak P.\] Equivalently, at least one collection of locally admissible conditionals cannot occur jointly. Such a restriction may encode shared parameters, trajectory-wide budgets, moment constraints coupling states, or temporal dependence, so nature's feasible choice at one coordinate can depend on choices made elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transition uncertainty is nonrectangular when locally admissible conditional distributions are coupled and therefore cannot be combined independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonrectangular Transition Uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection-based definition is coherent and distinguishes this node from its rectangular sibling, but the specific robust-MDP convention and examples of coupling have no cited support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon minimax Bellman recursion under state-action rectangular ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(V_T(s)=h(s)\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), define \[V_t(s)=\min_{a\in A_t(s)}\left\{c_t(s,a)+\max_{p\in\mathcal P_t(s,a)}\sum_{s'}p(s')V_{t+1}(s')\right\}.\] Then \(V_t(s)\) equals the minimax cost-to-go from \((t,s)\). Selecting at every \((t,s)\) an action attaining the displayed minimum yields a deterministic Markov policy that is optimal against all admissible rectangular transition selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under rectangular transition ambiguity, backward minimax Bellman recursion gives the robust value, and minimizing selectors form an optimal Markov policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Robust Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP counterpart for one affinely uncertain linear inequality over polyhedral uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The robust requirement \[(a_0+P\zeta)^\top x\le b_0+q^\top\zeta\quad\text{for every }\zeta\in\mathcal U\] is equivalent, by linear-programming duality, to the existence of \(\lambda\ge 0\) satisfying \[D^\top\lambda=P^\top x-q,\qquad d^\top\lambda\le b_0-a_0^\top x.\] For a system of uncertain rows, introducing a separate multiplier for each row produces an exact finite linear robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing worst-case affine uncertainty over a polyhedron converts each robust linear row into finitely many linear constraints.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain row is \((a_0+P\zeta)^\top x\le b_0+q^\top\zeta\).
The nonempty polyhedron \(\mathcal U=\{\zeta:D\zeta\le d\}\) has finite support in direction \(P^\top x-q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semi-infinite robust row is equivalent to linear constraints in \((x,\lambda)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Robust Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic-dual counterpart for affine uncertainty with a conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c=P^\top x-q\). The robust row is equivalent to \(a_0^\top x+\sigma_{\mathcal U}(c)\le b_0\), where \(\sigma_{\mathcal U}(c)=\sup_{\zeta\in\mathcal U}c^\top\zeta\). Under conic strong duality, this holds exactly when there exists \(y\in K^*\) such that \[H^\top y=c,\qquad h^\top y\le b_0-a_0^\top x.\] Hence a conic representation of the uncertainty set yields a finite robust counterpart over the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic duality replaces a worst-case affine constraint over conic-representable uncertainty by finite constraints involving the dual cone.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain row is \((a_0+P\zeta)^\top x\le b_0+q^\top\zeta\).
The uncertainty set is \(\mathcal U=\{\zeta:h-H\zeta\in K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
Conic strong duality holds for the support problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust row is equivalent to a finite constraint system over \(K^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear–Conic Counterpart Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural rule for selecting an exact LP or conic robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine robust row, introduce \(t\) and represent the exact conditions \[\sigma_{\mathcal U}(P^\top x-q)\le t,\qquad t\le b_0-a_0^\top x.\] If \(\mathcal U\) is polyhedral, linear-programming duality gives an LP counterpart. If an exact support-function representation uses a nonpolyhedral cone \(K\), conic duality gives a \(K^*\)-conic counterpart. A linear counterpart is exact when the resulting dual-cone constraints have an exact polyhedral representation; otherwise a linear replacement is an approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an LP counterpart for a polyhedral support representation and the matching dual-cone counterpart when the exact representation is genuinely nonpolyhedral.
assumptions_latex: Uncertainty enters each robust inequality affinely.
The support-function dual has no duality gap and attains its optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact counterpart is linear in the polyhedral case and otherwise uses the cone required by an exact dual support representation.

Because the unit ball has a strictly feasible point, the S-lemma gives \[q_x(\zeta)
e0\quad\text{for every }\zeta^\top\zeta
e1\] if and only if there exists \(\lambda
e0\) such that \[\begin{pmatrix}Q(x)-\lambda I&q(x)\\q(x)^\top&r(x)+\lambda\end{pmatrix}
preceq0.\] If \(Q(x)\), \(q(x)\), and \(r(x)\) depend affinely on \(x\), the displayed condition is a semidefinite-programming robust counterpart.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The robust constraints \[g_i(x,u)\le 0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\text{ and every }i\] are equivalent to the finite family \[g_i(x,u^k)\le 0\quad\text{for }i=1,\ldots,m,\quad k=1,\ldots,N.\] Retaining the original integrality restrictions on designated coordinates of \(x\) yields an exact mixed-integer linear counterpart. Its deterministic-equivalent size grows linearly with the number of explicitly listed scenarios, apart from constraints shared across scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite uncertainty, imposing every robust constraint for every scenario gives an exact mixed-integer counterpart while preserving decision integrality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate \(x\), compute for every robust row \[v_i(x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal U}g_i(x,u),\qquad u_i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in\mathcal U}g_i(x,u).\] If some \(v_i(x)>0\), return \((i,u_i^*)\); the deterministic constraint \(g_i(x,u_i^*)\le0\) separates \(x\) from the robust feasible set. If \(v_i(x)\le0\) for every \(i\), return \(x\) as robust feasible. Exactness requires globally solving each maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact oracle globally maximizes every constraint violation, returning a violating scenario or certifying that the candidate is robust feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Worst-Case Oracles
