children.title: Stabilized Cutting Planes
children.top_down_role: Regularized cutting-plane variants designed to limit unstable master iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Cutting Planes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of a convex robust-violation cutting-plane master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the robust problem be \(\min_{x\in X} c(x)\) subject to \(V(x):=\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\le 0\), where \(X\) is closed and convex and \(c\) and \(V\) are convex. Given a center \(z_k\in X\), cuts \(V(x_i)+s_i^{\mathsf T}(x-x_i)\le 0\) with \(s_i\in\partial V(x_i)\), and \(\lambda_k>0\), solve
\[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert x-z_k\rVert^2:V(x_i)+s_i^{\mathsf T}(x-x_i)\le0\ \text{for all retained }i\right\}.\]
Evaluate a separation oracle at \(x_{k+1}\); stop when \(V(x_{k+1})\le\varepsilon\), otherwise append its cut and update the center according to the prescribed serious-step rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each accumulated-cut master with a proximal term around a center, add a violated robust cut, and move the center only under the chosen serious-step test.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(c\) and \(V\) are proper convex functions.
The oracle returns \(V(x_i)\) and \(s_i\in\partial V(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point satisfies \(V(x_{k+1})\le\varepsilon\) under the stated stopping rule.

children.title: Bundle-Based Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cut management through retained subgradient bundles.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Based Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle model for a convex worst-case violation function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sampled points \(x_i\in X\), oracle values \(V(x_i)\), and subgradients \(s_i\in\partial V(x_i)\), form the bundle model
\[m_k(x):=\max_{i\in B_k}\left\{V(x_i)+s_i^{\mathsf T}(x-x_i)\right\}.\]
Convexity gives \(m_k(x)\le V(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). A bundle-cut master minimizes \(c(x)\) over \(X\) subject to \(m_k(x)\le0\), optionally with stabilization. After evaluating \(V\) at a trial point, insert the new affine minorant; cuts may be deleted or aggregated only if the retained model remains a valid global lower model of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a maximum of subgradient minorants of worst-case violation, solve the resulting master, and update the bundle without losing global lower-model validity.
assumptions_latex: \(V:X\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
Each stored \(s_i\) belongs to \(\partial V(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(x)\le V(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: indices retained in the current bundle

children.title: Stabilization–Bundle Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Regimes combining master stabilization with bundle retention.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, while \(c\) and \(V\) are convex.
\(m_k(x)\le V(x)\) holds on \(X\).
\(\lambda_k>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained master cut remains valid, and termination yields \(V(x_{k+1})\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle scheme combining retained robust cuts with serious-step center updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k\) be a valid bundle minorant of the convex violation function \(V\), and let \(z_k\in X\). Compute
\[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert x-z_k\rVert^2:m_k(x)\le0\right\}.\]
Evaluate \(V(x_{k+1})\) and add a supporting cut at \(x_{k+1}\). Apply a prescribed serious-step test with threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\): if the test is passed, set \(z_{k+1}=x_{k+1}\); otherwise set \(z_{k+1}=z_k\). Stop when the oracle certifies \(V(x_{k+1})\le\varepsilon\) and the selected objective-gap test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilized bundle hybrid solves a proximal bundle master, enriches its cut model, and moves the center only after the prescribed serious-step test is passed.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization–Bundle Hybrids

children.title: Stabilization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where stabilization overhead or weak bundle information limits progress.

assumptions_latex: The stabilization radius is fixed at \(0<\rho<2\).
The center remains \(z_k=0\) for every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_k|x_k-x^\star|\ge 2-\rho>0\), so convergence to the robust optimizer fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by stabilization regions that permanently exclude robust optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stabilization rule need not preserve global convergence if its accessible regions fail to expand toward an optimizer. Consider \(X=[0,2]\), \(c(x)=-x\), and \(g(x,u)=-1\) for the sole scenario \(u\in U\). The robust problem has the unique optimizer \(x^\star=2\). If every stabilized master is restricted to \(|x-z_k|\le\rho\), with \(z_k=0\), fixed \(0<\rho<2\), and a center rule that never accepts a move, then every trial point satisfies \(x_k\le\rho\). Thus all robust constraints are satisfied, yet no iterate approaches \(x^\star\). Global convergence therefore requires a mechanism preventing permanent exclusion of improving solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed stabilization region and immobile center can keep every iterate away from the robust optimum even when all generated points are feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Failure Boundaries

assumptions_latex: \(V:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
The oracle inequality holds globally on \(X\).
A certified upper estimate \(\overline V_k\) is available for termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated cut is valid, and \(\overline V_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(V(x_k)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: inexact oracle value used in the cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex robust cutting-plane method using certified approximate values and subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be convex. At a query point \(x_k\), suppose an inexact oracle returns \(\widehat V_k\), \(s_k\), and \(\epsilon_k\ge0\) satisfying
\[V(y)\ge \widehat V_k+s_k^{\mathsf T}(y-x_k)-\epsilon_k\quad\text{for every }y\in X.\]
Append the valid affine lower cut \(\widehat V_k+s_k^{\mathsf T}(x-x_k)-\epsilon_k\le0\) to the master, solve the updated master for the next query, and retain a certified upper estimate \(\overline V_k\ge V(x_k)\). Terminate only when \(\overline V_k\le\varepsilon\); a small lower estimate alone does not certify robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use an oracle-certified affine lower bound as the cut and stop only from an upper bound on true worst-case violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Cutting Planes

assumptions_latex: Every restricted master has an optimizer whenever it is invoked.
The separation maximum over \(U\) is attained and solved exactly.
The robust problem has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns \(x_k\) with \(\sup_{u\in U}g(x_k,u)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: most violated scenario at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exchange algorithm for scenario-indexed robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in X}c(x)\) subject to \(g(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\), initialize a finite set \(S_0\subseteq U\). At iteration \(k\), solve
\[x_k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{c(x):g(x,u)\le0\ \text{for every }u\in S_k\}.\]
Compute \(u_k\in\arg\max_{u\in U}g(x_k,u)\). If \(g(x_k,u_k)\le\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\); otherwise set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{u_k\}\) and repeat. With exact master and separation solutions, the master objective is a lower bound on the robust optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted scenario master, add its most violated uncertainty realization, and stop when the worst remaining violation is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Constraint Generation

assumptions_latex: Each generated scenario constraint is valid for the original robust model.
Separation is exact for every uncertainty set \(U_j\).
The solver invokes the callback for every candidate it could accept.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted incumbent \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\sup_{u\in U_j}g_j(\bar x,u)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: uncertainty set for robust constraint j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callback generation of robust constraints at candidate mixed-integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a robust mixed-integer model with deterministic domain \(X\) and constraints \(g_j(x,u)\le0\) for all \(u\in U_j\) and \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Solve a relaxation containing only generated scenarios. Whenever the solver produces an integer candidate \(\bar x\), compute \(u_j^\star\in\arg\max_{u\in U_j}g_j(\bar x,u)\). If some \(g_j(\bar x,u_j^\star)>\varepsilon\), reject \(\bar x\) and add \(g_j(x,u_j^\star)\le0\) as a globally valid lazy constraint. Accept termination only after every incumbent passes all separation tests and the underlying solver establishes its usual optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each integer candidate, separate every robust constraint; violated scenarios become globally valid lazy constraints before the candidate may be accepted.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Robust Constraints

assumptions_latex: The restricted master contains only constraints from the original robust problem.
Separation computes the displayed worst-case violation exactly.
The candidate \(x_k\) satisfies the deterministic domain restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(v_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-robust feasibility. If additionally \(v_k\le0\) and \(U_k-L_k\le\delta\), then \(0\le U_k-p^\star\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasibility and objective-gap certificate for robust constraint generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_k\) be the optimal value of the restricted master, let \(x_k\) be a candidate, and set \(U_k=c(x_k)\). Suppose exact separation gives
\[v_k:=\max_{1\le j\le m}\sup_{u\in U_j}g_j(x_k,u)\le\varepsilon.\]
Because the restricted master relaxes the robust problem, \(L_k\le p^\star\), where \(p^\star\) is the robust optimal value. Thus \(v_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-robust feasibility. If \(v_k\le0\), then \(x_k\) is exactly robust feasible, so \(U_k\ge p^\star\); consequently, \(U_k-L_k\le\delta\) certifies \(0\le U_k-p^\star\le\delta\). For merely \(\varepsilon\)-feasible \(x_k\), an objective-gap claim requires a separately defined tolerance-adjusted problem and a lower bound for that same problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case separation certifies approximate feasibility. The restricted-master lower bound and candidate objective certify an exact robust objective gap only when the candidate is exactly robust feasible, unless a separate tolerance-adjusted problem is defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Generation Certificates

assumptions_latex: \(U\) contains exactly \(N<\infty\) scenarios.
Restricted masters and separation problems are solved exactly.
Every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent violated scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after at most \(N-|S_0|\) additions with a robust optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact constraint generation when the uncertainty index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) and consider \(\min_{x\in X}c(x)\) subject to \(g(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\). Run exact scenario constraint generation, adding at every nonterminal iteration a scenario \(u_k\) with \(g(x_k,u_k)>0\) that is not already in the master. Then no scenario is added twice, so at most \(N-|S_0|\) additions occur. The terminal restricted-master optimizer is feasible for all scenarios and, because every restricted master is a relaxation of the full problem, is an optimizer of the full finite-scenario robust problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many scenarios and exact separation, each failed iteration adds a new scenario, so the method terminates after finitely many additions at a robust optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Scenario Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
For fixed \(x\), the mapping \(g(x,\cdot)\) is convex and continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)=\max_{u\in\operatorname{ext}(U)}g(x,u)\).

notation.meaning: set of extreme points of the uncertainty polytope

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which worst-case separation may be restricted to polytope extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^q\) be a nonempty compact polytope and fix \(x\in X\). If \(u\mapsto g(x,u)\) is convex and continuous on \(U\), then at least one maximizer is an extreme point of \(U\), and
\[\max_{u\in U}g(x,u)=\max_{u\in\operatorname{ext}(U)}g(x,u).\]
Consequently, exact separation may search only the finite extreme-point set. Convexity is essential for this reduction: for concave uncertainty dependence, a strict interior maximizer may exist. Compact polyhedrality is essential to the stated finite-enumeration conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous convex function of uncertainty attains its polytope maximum at an extreme scenario, enabling finite extreme-point separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Scenario Separation Conditions

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are compact, and \(g\) is continuous on \(X\times U\).
Separation is exact and every generated constraint is retained.
The iterate sequence has an accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\max_{u\in U}g(\bar x,u)\le0\), but finite termination is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: an accumulation point of master solutions
exact worst-case scenario at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic feasibility of exact exchange methods over compact nonpolyhedral uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(U\) be compact, let \(g\) be continuous on \(X\times U\), and let exact constraint generation produce \(x_k\) and maximizers \(u_k\in\arg\max_{u\in U}g(x_k,u)\). Suppose every later master enforces \(g(x,u_k)\le0\), and the sequence has an accumulation point \(\bar x\). Along any convergent subsequence \(x_{k_r}\to\bar x\), compactness gives a further subsequence \(u_{k_r}\to\bar u\). Continuity, exact separation, and retention of generated constraints imply \(\max_{u\in U}g(\bar x,u)\le0\). Nevertheless, when \(U\) has infinitely many relevant scenarios, no finite-termination bound follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, continuity, exact separation, and retained cuts, accumulation points are robust feasible, although infinitely many relevant scenarios can prevent finite termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Asymptotic Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(V(x)-\delta\le\widehat V(x)\le V(x)\) for every queried \(x\).
The algorithm stops when \(\widehat V(x)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sharp guarantee is \(V(x)\le\varepsilon+\delta\); for this bound to imply vanishing residual violation as \(\varepsilon\to0\), the certified error \(\delta\) must also vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual feasibility limit imposed by uniformly inaccurate separation oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(x)=\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\), and suppose an oracle reports \(\widehat V(x)\) with the one-sided guarantee \(V(x)-\delta\le\widehat V(x)\le V(x)\) for fixed \(\delta\ge0\). Then the stopping test \(\widehat V(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies only \(V(x)\le\varepsilon+\delta\). This boundary is sharp: for singleton decision and uncertainty sets, choose \(V(x)=\varepsilon+\delta\) and let the oracle report \(\widehat V(x)=\varepsilon\). Hence exact feasibility cannot be inferred from fixed positive error. For this stopping bound to yield vanishing residual violation as \(\varepsilon\to0\), the certified oracle error must also converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle underestimating violation by at most a fixed error can certify only feasibility within the stopping tolerance plus that error.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Oracle Convergence Boundaries
Feasibility-Cut Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificates for infeasible continuous-recourse subproblems at generated uncertainty scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\bar u\in\mathcal U\) and consider \(Wy\ge h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x\). For an incumbent \(\bar x\), this system is infeasible if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(W^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\) and \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}[h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)\bar x]>0\). Every robustly feasible first-stage decision must satisfy
\[
\lambda^{\mathsf T}[h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x]\le0.
\]
This cut excludes \(\bar x\) and is certified by the ray and fixed scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas ray from an infeasible scenario subproblem yields a linear cut that excludes the incumbent while remaining necessary for robust feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is the uncertainty set and \(\bar u\in\mathcal U\).
\(W\) is a finite-dimensional recourse matrix.
Recourse feasibility has the displayed inequality form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}[h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x]\le0\) is a valid robust-feasibility cut violated by \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Cut Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual optimality cuts for feasible linear continuous recourse at a generated scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q(x,u)=\min_y\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h(u)-T(u)x\}\), and suppose the subproblem at \((\bar x,\bar u)\) is feasible and finite-valued. Its dual feasible set is \(D=\{\pi\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}\pi=q\}\). Every \(\pi\in D\) gives the valid scenario cut
\[
\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}[h(\bar u)-T(\bar u)x].
\]
If \(\pi\) is dual-optimal at \((\bar x,\bar u)\), the right-hand side equals \(Q(\bar x,\bar u)\). A violation shows that the restricted master underestimates the recourse value for this scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible recourse solution defines a global lower bound on scenario cost; a dual optimum produces an exact supporting cut at the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The recourse problem is a feasible, finite-valued, finite-dimensional linear program at \((\bar x,\bar u)\).
Linear-programming strong duality and dual attainment hold.
\(\theta\) is the master epigraph variable for the restricted approximation of worst-case recourse cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is valid, and a dual optimizer makes it exact at \(\bar x\) for scenario \(\bar u\).

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Robust Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized robust Benders scheme using problem-specific logical inference instead of linear duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a first-stage set \(X\), initialize a relaxation with no scenario cuts. At iteration \(k\), solve it for \((\bar x^k,\bar\theta^k)\), then use an exact adversarial oracle to select \(u^k\in\arg\max_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(\bar x^k,u)\). If recourse is infeasible, add a logically valid constraint excluding decisions that share the certified infeasible structure. Otherwise construct \(L_k:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L_k(x)\le Q(x,u^k)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(L_k(\bar x^k)=Q(\bar x^k,u^k)\), and add \(\theta\ge L_k(x)\). If certified bounds have gap at most \(\varepsilon\), return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact adversarial oracle generates scenarios, while logical infeasibility explanations or global recourse underestimators strengthen the master; a valid bound gap certifies termination.
assumptions_latex: Every generated logical cut is valid for all robustly feasible decisions.
The adversarial and recourse oracles are solved globally.
Finite valid lower and upper bounds are maintained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever the certified upper-minus-lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\), the returned incumbent has robust optimality gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: possibly discrete or nonconvex recourse value

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Recourse CCG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-and-constraint generation for two-stage robust problems with continuous linear recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in X}c^{\mathsf T}x+\max_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x,u)\) with linear continuous recourse, initialize a finite scenario set \(S_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve
\[
\min_{x,\theta,\{y^s\}}c^{\mathsf T}x+\theta,
\qquad Wy^s\ge h(u^s)-T(u^s)x,
\qquad \theta\ge q^{\mathsf T}y^s
\]
for every \(u^s\in S_k\). Compute \(u^{k+1}\in\arg\max_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x^k,u)\). If the valid incumbent upper bound minus the master lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\), return \(x^k\); otherwise set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{u^{k+1}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master contains recourse columns for sampled scenarios; an exact worst-case oracle adds a scenario until valid global bounds certify a small robust objective gap.
assumptions_latex: Recourse is continuous and linear, with complete recourse or valid feasibility handling.
Every master and adversarial subproblem is solved globally.
Finite valid lower and upper objective bounds exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test holds, \(x^k\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal robust first-stage solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Recourse CCG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact CCG variant retaining integrality in every generated recourse block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x,u)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h(u)-T(u)x,\ y\in Y\cap\mathbb Z^p\}\). Starting from finite \(S_0\subseteq\mathcal U\), solve a master containing one integer vector \(y^s\) and the constraints \(Wy^s\ge h(u^s)-T(u^s)x\) and \(\theta\ge q^{\mathsf T}y^s\) for every \(u^s\in S_k\). Globally maximize \(Q(x^k,u)\) over \(u\in\mathcal U\). Add a maximizing scenario unless the valid upper-minus-lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal U\) is finite and duplicate scenarios are suppressed, at most \(|\mathcal U|\) distinct scenarios can be added.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer-recourse CCG preserves recourse integrality in each scenario block and uses a globally exact adversarial mixed-integer oracle; finite uncertainty permits only finitely many distinct additions.
assumptions_latex: All master and adversarial mixed-integer problems are solved globally.
Generated scenario blocks preserve the original recourse domain.
The finite-termination claim assumes finite \(\mathcal U\) and suppression of duplicate scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The valid gap test certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality; finite \(\mathcal U\) permits at most \(|\mathcal U|\) distinct scenario additions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested CCG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-level generation scheme for adversarial problems whose recourse-value oracle itself requires decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an outer scenario set \(S_k\) and solve its restricted robust master for \(x^k\) and a valid lower bound. To evaluate \(\max_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x^k,u)\), run an inner column-and-constraint loop that maintains valid bounds, generates a recourse response or valid infeasibility certificate, and stops with certified error at most \(\delta_k\). Let \(u^{k+1}\) be the resulting certified adversarial solution. Add it to \(S_k\) unless valid outer bounds, adjusted for \(\delta_k\), have gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer scenario-generation loop calls an inner decomposition loop for the adversarial-recourse oracle, with inner error incorporated into the outer certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every inner cut is valid for the adversarial-recourse problem.
The outer upper bound accounts conservatively for \(\delta_k\).
The restricted outer master is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the error-adjusted valid outer bound gap is at most \(\varepsilon\), the returned incumbent has robust optimality gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Extreme-Point Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination scope when worst-case scenarios are drawn from finitely many extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\mathcal U\) is a nonempty compact polytope with finite extreme-point set \(E=\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal U)\), and for every feasible \(x\), the function \(u\mapsto Q(x,u)\) is convex and finite on \(\mathcal U\). Then
\[
\max_{u\in\mathcal U}Q(x,u)=\max_{u\in E}Q(x,u).
\]
Consequently, an exact CCG method that adds a previously absent maximizing extreme point whenever its master gap is positive can make at most \(|E|\) distinct scenario additions. Exact finite termination follows when all masters and separation problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex finite-valued worst-case recourse over a compact polytope has an extreme-point maximizer, so an exact CCG oracle restricted to new extreme points has finitely many scenarios to add.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is a nonempty compact polytope with \(E=\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal U)\).
\(u\mapsto Q(x,u)\) is finite and convex for every feasible \(x\).
The exact CCG oracle returns a previously absent maximizing extreme point whenever the gap is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case search reduces to \(E\), and at most \(|E|\) distinct scenario additions are required.

notation.meaning: finite extreme-point set of the uncertainty polytope

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Uncertainty Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of finite CCG termination over uncertainty sets with infinitely many exposed scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\) be compact and have infinitely many extreme or exposed points. Continuity of \(Q(x,\cdot)\) and exact solution of every adversarial problem do not by themselves guarantee finite scenario-generation termination: successive incumbents can expose distinct maximizers \(u^1,u^2,\ldots\). Finite exact termination therefore requires an additional finite-support, finite-representability, or problem-specific identification property. At any iteration with valid global bounds \(L_k\le p^\star\le U_k\), however,
\[
U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon
\]
certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact continuous uncertainty may permit infinitely many distinct exposed scenarios, so finite termination needs extra structure; a valid global bound gap still certifies approximate optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is compact and may have infinitely many exposed points.
\(Q(x,\cdot)\) is continuous.
\(L_k\) and \(U_k\) are valid global lower and incumbent upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compact continuous uncertainty alone does not imply finite exact CCG termination, while \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Recourse Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A positive integrality gap showing why LP-dual CCG cuts do not exactly represent integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a singleton uncertainty set and
\[
Q=\min\{y:2y\ge1,\ y\in\{0,1\}\}=1.
\]
Its linear relaxation is \(\min\{y:2y\ge1,\ y\ge0\}\), whose dual is
\[
\max\{\pi:2\pi\le1,\ \pi\ge0\}=\tfrac12.
\]
Thus the LP-dual value underestimates the integer-recourse value by \(\tfrac12\). A decomposition master that treats this relaxation dual as an exact representation of integer recourse can underestimate the robust objective. Exact integer-recourse methods require a globally valid representation or oracle for the integer value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable binary recourse problem has value one, whereas its LP relaxation and LP dual have value one half; continuous-duality cuts therefore do not exactly represent the integer recourse value.
assumptions_latex: The recourse variable satisfies \(y\in\{0,1\}\).
The proposed decomposition dualizes the continuous relaxation rather than the integer value function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuous LP-dual cuts do not exactly represent this integer-recourse value and cannot alone certify the robust optimum.

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for the relaxed covering constraint

children.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition organized through relaxation of complicating couplings.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable representation obtained by relaxing a coupling constraint with multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(x_s\in X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\), let \(A_s\in\mathbb R^{r\times n_s}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^r\). Consider
\[
p^\star=\inf\left\{\sum_{s=1}^m f_s(x_s):x_s\in X_s,\ \sum_{s=1}^m A_sx_s=b\right\}.
\]
For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\), relaxing the coupling equality gives
\[
g(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{s=1}^m\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_sx_s\bigr).
\]
Hence evaluating \(g(\lambda)\) decomposes into \(m\) independent subproblems, and \(g(\lambda)\le p^\star\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing the sole coupling equality separates the Lagrangian dual function into independent block subproblems and supplies a lower bound for minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(m,r,n_1,\ldots,n_m\) are positive integers and each \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s}\) is nonempty.
The sole cross-block constraint is \(\sum_{s=1}^mA_sx_s=b\).
The displayed infima are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian value separates blockwise and satisfies \(g(\lambda)\le p^\star\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\).

children.title: Dual Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition organized through separable dual subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier iteration for maximizing a separable Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb R^r\) and step sizes \(\alpha_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), solve in parallel
\[
x_s^k\in\arg\min_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(f_s(x_s)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}A_sx_s\bigr),
\]
compute \(d^k=\sum_sA_sx_s^k-b\), and update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_kd^k\). Track the best dual value \(g(\lambda^k)\) and any recovered coupling-feasible primal point. A certified primal-dual gap permits termination; without feasible primal recovery, only the dual bound and residual are certified. Under existence of a dual optimizer, uniformly bounded supergradients, and \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), the standard subgradient value-convergence guarantee applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block minimizations produce a coupling residual used as a dual supergradient; iterations track valid dual bounds and, when available, recovered feasible primal points.
assumptions_latex: Every block subproblem attains a minimizer.
A dual optimizer exists and the dual optimal value is finite when asymptotic convergence is asserted.
The generated supergradients are uniformly bounded when the stated diminishing-step convergence result is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update performs supergradient ascent on the concave function \(g\), and every recorded \(g(\lambda^k)\) is a valid primal lower bound.

children.title: Lagrangian–Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural overlap between relaxation-based and dual-coordination viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between coupling-constraint Lagrangian relaxation and the decomposed dual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the separable convex problem with coupling equality \(\sum_sA_sx_s=b\), define \(F_s=f_s+\delta_{X_s}\). Its Lagrangian dual is
\[
d^\star=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}g(\lambda)=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}\left[-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_s\inf_{x_s\in X_s}\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_sx_s\bigr)\right].
\]
Thus Lagrangian decomposition evaluates the concave objective maximized by dual decomposition, and always \(d^\star\le p^\star\). If every \(F_s\) is proper, closed, and convex and there exist \(x_s\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}F_s)\) satisfying \(\sum_sA_sx_s=b\), then strong duality gives \(d^\star=p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian decomposition evaluates the same concave function maximized by dual decomposition; a relative-interior convex regularity condition yields equality of primal and dual values.
assumptions_latex: For each block, \(F_s=f_s+\delta_{X_s}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The coupling constraint \(\sum_sA_sx_s=b\) is affine.
There exist \(x_s\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}F_s)\) satisfying the coupling equality when strong duality is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lagrangian and dual decomposition act on the same function \(g\); under the stated regularity, \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}g(\lambda)=p^\star\).

notation.meaning: convex indicator of the block set

children.title: Decomposition Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Coupling structures, duality regimes, or subproblem features limiting these decompositions.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\prod_{s=1}^S X_s\) with each \(X_s\) nonempty and convex.
\(f(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S f_s(x_s)\), while coupling is represented by \(\sum_{s=1}^S A_sx_s=b\).
Each scenario subproblem and the resulting multiplier master problem are solved to the accuracy required by the decomposition scheme.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(x,\lambda)\) separates by scenario exactly under the stated additive and linear-coupling structure; otherwise the advertised independent subproblems are not obtained.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian multiplier for the coupling constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for exact scenario decomposition through linear coupling dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_S)\), the partial Lagrangian is \[L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{s=1}^S\bigl(f_s(x_s)+\langle\lambda,A_sx_s\rangle\bigr)-\langle\lambda,b\rangle.\] Hence \(\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\) decomposes into \(S\) independent infima. Exact decomposition fails if an undualized constraint couples distinct blocks, if the objective contains a nonseparable term, or if the uncertainty set imposes nonseparable cross-scenario restrictions. Even when separation holds, equality of the decomposed dual value and the primal robust value additionally requires an appropriate strong-duality condition; otherwise decomposition supplies only a dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual decomposition is exact only when dualization removes every coupling and the remaining objective and feasible set separate; recovering the primal value also requires strong duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Applicability Boundaries

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
\(K\) is linear and a saddle point of \(g(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-f^*(y)\) exists.
\(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates implement a primal-dual splitting for \(\min_x g(x)+f(Kx)\), and a residual-based termination returns an approximate saddle pair.

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of a convex function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual hybrid gradient form for a convex robust saddle formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0\), \(y^0\), and \(\bar x^0=x^0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma f^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau g}(x^k-\tau K^*y^{k+1}),\] and \[\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Stop when a specified primal-dual residual is at most \(\varepsilon\), and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\); alternatively, after a fixed budget return weighted ergodic averages. In robust optimization, \(y\) represents the adversarial or uncertainty-side variable after a convex-concave reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate a dual proximal step, a primal proximal step, and primal extrapolation; terminate using a primal-dual residual or return ergodic averages after a fixed budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and displayed primal–dual updates fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the stated step-size/extrapolation variant, residual-based termination, or ergodic-output alternative. The residual must also be defined before its tolerance can certify an approximate saddle pair.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
\(F:Z\to Z^*\) is monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz.
A solution of \(\langle F(z^*),z-z^*\rangle\ge 0\) for every \(z\in Z\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(0<\gamma<1/L\), the two-projection update is an extragradient method for the stated monotone variational inequality.

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean extragradient method for monotone robust saddle operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(z^0\in Z\) and \(0<\gamma<1/L\). At iteration \(k\), form the prediction and correction \[w^k=P_Z\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(z^k)\bigr),\qquad z^{k+1}=P_Z\bigl(z^k-\gamma F(w^k)\bigr).\] The second evaluation is taken at the predicted point but corrects from \(z^k\). Stop when a prescribed variational-inequality residual at \(w^k\) is at most \(\varepsilon\), returning \(w^k\); with a fixed iteration budget, return an ergodic average of the prediction points. For convex-concave robust saddle problems, \(F\) combines the primal gradient and the negative adversarial gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extragradient evaluates the monotone operator at a projected prediction and uses that evaluation for a second projected step from the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Extragradient Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-projection update is a standard Euclidean extragradient algorithm and fits the container. An exact source is required for the step-size condition, the unspecified residual termination rule, and the asserted ergodic-output option.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is compact and convex, and \(F:Z\to Z^*\) is monotone and Lipschitz relative to a chosen norm.
\(\omega\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(Z\).
The Bregman proximal subproblems admit solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two Bregman-proximal evaluations constitute Mirror-Prox and accommodate non-Euclidean geometry of the robust saddle domain.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the distance function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Euclidean extragradient scheme for compact convex saddle domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[P_z(g)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in Z}\{\langle g,u\rangle+D_\omega(u,z)\}.\] Initialize \(z^1\in Z\). For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), choose \(\gamma_k>0\) and compute \[w^k=P_{z^k}(\gamma_kF(z^k)),\qquad z^{k+1}=P_{z^k}(\gamma_kF(w^k)).\] Return \(\bar w_N=(\sum_{k=1}^N\gamma_kw^k)/(\sum_{k=1}^N\gamma_k)\), or stop earlier when its computable gap residual is at most \(\varepsilon\). The distance generator may be selected separately for primal decisions and adversarial distributions, such as entropy on a probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mirror-Prox replaces Euclidean projections in extragradient with Bregman proximal steps and returns a step-size-weighted average of prediction points.
knowledge_statements.title: Mirror-Prox Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and Bregman two-step form fit Mirror-Prox, but arbitrary positive step sizes do not by themselves support a convergence or gap certificate. A source must specify the admissible step-size rule and the computable gap residual.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and has diameter at most \(D\).
\(F:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and every selected \(g^k\in\partial F(x^k)\) satisfies \(\lVert g^k\rVert\le G\).
A minimizer \(x^*\in X\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted output satisfies \(F(\bar x_N)-F(x^*)\le (D^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2)/(2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected subgradient minimization of a finite convex robust objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0\in X\) and positive step sizes \(\alpha_k\). For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), obtain \(g^k\in\partial F(x^k)\) and set \[x^{k+1}=P_X(x^k-\alpha_kg^k).\] Return \[\bar x_N=\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_kx^k}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k}.\] Stop at the first \(N\) for which the displayed a priori upper bound is at most \(\varepsilon\), or at a prescribed budget. For \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\), a maximizing scenario \(u^k\) yields a valid subgradient of \(F\) from a subgradient of \(f(\cdot,u^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each subgradient step onto the decision set and return a step-size-weighted average; worst-case scenarios can generate subgradients of the robust objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected subgradient algorithm and weighted-average bound are mathematically consistent under the stated diameter and bounded-subgradient assumptions, and the kind fits the leaf. The exact bound and worst-case-scenario subgradient claim need a specifically located authoritative source.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Pflug, Optimization of Stochastic Models
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Pflug, Optimization of Stochastic Models

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
At every queried point \(x^i\), an oracle supplies \(F(x^i)\) and \(g^i\in\partial F(x^i)\).
The proximal parameter \(t_k\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bundle model is a global lower model of \(F\), and serious/null steps respectively move the center or enrich the model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal cutting-plane bundle method for nonsmooth convex robust objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a bundle \(B_k\), form \[m_k(x)=\max_{i\in B_k}\{F(x^i)+\langle g^i,x-x^i\rangle\}\] and compute \[y^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert x-c^k\rVert^2\}.\] Evaluate \(F(y^k)\) and a subgradient there. If the actual decrease \(F(c^k)-F(y^k)\) is at least a fixed fraction of the predicted decrease \(F(c^k)-m_k(y^k)\), set \(c^{k+1}=y^k\); otherwise set \(c^{k+1}=c^k\). Add the new cut, optionally aggregate or delete inactive cuts, and stop when the predicted decrease is at most \(\varepsilon\), returning \(c^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle method minimizes a proximal cutting-plane model, accepts sufficiently productive trial points as serious steps, and otherwise retains the center while adding information.
knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Methods

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and has Euclidean diameter at most \(D\).
At round \(t\), the adversary selects a convex loss \(\ell_t:X\to\mathbb R\) with \(\lVert g_t\rVert\le G\) for \(g_t\in\partial\ell_t(x_t)\).
The decision \(x_t\) is chosen before \(\ell_t\) is revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\eta=D/(G\sqrt T)\), projected online subgradient descent has regret at most \(DG\sqrt T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static-regret guarantee for projected online subgradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x_1\in X\), update \(x_{t+1}=P_X(x_t-\eta g_t)\) after observing \(g_t\in\partial\ell_t(x_t)\). Define \[R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(x_t)-\min_{x\in X}\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(x).\] For every, possibly adaptive, loss sequence satisfying the assumptions, \[R_T\le \frac{D^2}{2\eta}+\frac{\eta G^2T}{2}.\] Thus \(\eta=D/(G\sqrt T)\) gives \(R_T\le DG\sqrt T\), so the average excess loss is at most \(DG/\sqrt T\). The resource counted is one subgradient and one projection per round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected online subgradient descent guarantees at most square-root cumulative regret against the best fixed robust decision, using one subgradient and projection per round.
knowledge_statements.title: Online Adversarial Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role is suitable for this leaf, and the projected online subgradient regret formula is standard and internally consistent. A specifically located authoritative source is required for the adaptive-adversary scope and exact constants.

children.title: First-Order Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Optimality-gap evidence produced by first-order robust optimization methods.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
\(\Phi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\).
The two optimization terms defining the gap can be evaluated or rigorously bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(G(\bar x,\bar y)\le\varepsilon\), then \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-saddle pair and \(\bar x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for \(\min_x\max_y\Phi(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute saddle-gap certificate for compact convex-concave formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\), define \[G(\bar x,\bar y)=\sup_{y\in Y}\Phi(\bar x,y)-\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x,\bar y).\] The quantity is nonnegative and directly checkable whenever the two one-sided optimization problems have certified values. If \(G(\bar x,\bar y)\le\varepsilon\), then for all \(x\in X\) and \(y\in Y\), \[\Phi(\bar x,y)-\Phi(x,\bar y)\le\varepsilon.\] In particular, with \(p^*=\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y)\), one has \(0\le\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(\bar x,y)-p^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate pair is certified when its worst primal value minus its best dual value is at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Gap Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and gap inequality fit the leaf, but the assumptions need the regularity required for minimax equality and existence of the stated primal value, such as appropriate semicontinuity/continuity conditions. No source is supplied to resolve the required hypotheses.

children.title: First-Order Feasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence of robust constraint satisfaction from first-order computations.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust-feasibility certificate using rigorous worst-case oracle bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[V(\bar x)=\max_{1\le j\le m}[U_j(\bar x)]_+.\] The finite data \((\bar x,U_1(\bar x),\ldots,U_m(\bar x))\), together with verifiable oracle upper-bound guarantees, constitute an \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility certificate when \(V(\bar x)\le\varepsilon\). Indeed, each uncertainty realization then satisfies \(g_j(\bar x,u)\le U_j(\bar x)\le\varepsilon\). If a separating oracle instead produces some \(u_j\) with \(g_j(\bar x,u_j)>\varepsilon\), that scenario is a verifiable certificate that \(\bar x\) is not \(\varepsilon\)-robust-feasible. First-order cuts may be used internally to establish the upper bounds, but sampled lower bounds alone do not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified upper bounds on every worst constraint value prove approximate robust feasibility; a scenario exceeding tolerance certifies that the candidate is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set and the robust constraints are \(g_j(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U_j\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
For the candidate \(\bar x\), an oracle returns certified upper bounds \(U_j(\bar x)\ge\sup_{u\in U_j}g_j(\bar x,u)\).
The feasibility tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\max_j[U_j(\bar x)]_+\le\varepsilon\), then \(g_j(\bar x,u)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(j\) and every \(u\in U_j\).

notation.meaning: Certified upper bound on worst constraint value

children.title: Certificate Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where gap quality, feasibility quality, or computational effort dominate.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Tradeoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized tradeoff between certified optimality and robust feasibility errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because both certificate components are nonnegative, \[\alpha G\le\alpha G+(1-\alpha)V\le\varepsilon,\qquad (1-\alpha)V\le\alpha G+(1-\alpha)V\le\varepsilon.\] Consequently, \[G\le\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha},\qquad V\le\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\alpha}.\] Thus weights near \(1\) favor a tight gap guarantee but permit a weak feasibility guarantee, while weights near \(0\) do the reverse. To guarantee prescribed tolerances \((\varepsilon_G,\varepsilon_V)\), it suffices to choose \(\alpha\) and the combined tolerance so that \(\varepsilon\le\min\{\alpha\varepsilon_G,(1-\alpha)\varepsilon_V\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted nonnegative certificate bounds gap and violation separately, but tightening one implied bound weakens the other unless the combined tolerance is also reduced.
assumptions_latex: \(G\ge0\) is a certified optimality gap and \(V\ge0\) is a certified feasibility violation.
A combined certificate establishes \(\alpha G+(1-\alpha)V\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined certificate implies \(G\le\varepsilon/\alpha\) and \(V\le\varepsilon/(1-\alpha)\), exposing the gap-feasibility tradeoff.

children.title: Inconclusive Certificate Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Situations where available first-order evidence cannot support a decisive conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconclusive Certificate Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for finite first-order robust-feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(u)=\prod_{q\in Q}(u-q)^2\) and \(M=\max_{u\in[0,1]}p(u)>0\). Consider \(g_0(u)=-1\) and \[g_1(u)=-1+\frac{2p(u)}{M}.\] At every \(q\in Q\), both functions satisfy \(g_0(q)=g_1(q)=-1\) and \(g_0'(q)=g_1'(q)=0\). However, \(g_0\) is robust feasible, whereas \(\max_{u\in[0,1]}g_1(u)=1\), so \(g_1\) is infeasible. Therefore finite value-gradient data are inconclusive unless additional structure, such as a known Lipschitz or curvature bound, an exact separation oracle, or a finite uncertainty set, controls behavior between queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite value-gradient samples cannot certify a continuum of robust constraints without regularity information: smooth feasible and infeasible constraints can agree at every sampled point.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset[0,1]\) is a finite set of oracle query points.
The oracle reveals only the value and first derivative of an unknown continuously differentiable constraint function at points in \(Q\).
Robust feasibility means \(g(u)\le0\) for every \(u\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite first-order observations without regularity bounds cannot distinguish a robust-feasible constraint from a robust-infeasible one.

notation.meaning: Normalization constant for the indistinguishable constraint

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Kuhn, Shafiee, and Wiesemann, Distributionally Robust Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Numerical solution of nature's problem and the full DRO problem
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Kuhn, Shafiee, and Wiesemann, Distributionally Robust Optimization

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set is \(\mathcal P_\rho=\{p\in\mathbb R_+^n:\sum_i p_i=1,\ D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\Vert q)\le\rho\}\).
The nominal probabilities satisfy \(q_i>0\), and losses \(\ell_i(x)\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case expected loss equals a one-dimensional convex infimum, and any positive minimizing temperature yields an exponential-tilted worst-case distribution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support KL-divergence ambiguity with exponential tilting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fixed decision \(x\), \[\sup_{p\in\mathcal P_\rho}\sum_{i=1}^np_i\ell_i(x)=\inf_{\eta>0}\left\{\eta\rho+
\eta\log\left(\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\exp\left(\frac{\ell_i(x)}{\eta}\right)\right)\right\}.\] The infimum includes limiting values as \(\eta\downarrow0\). If a positive minimizer \(\eta^*\) exists and the divergence constraint is active, a worst-case distribution is \[p_i^*=\frac{q_i\exp(\ell_i(x)/\eta^*)}{\sum_{j=1}^nq_j\exp(\ell_j(x)/\eta^*)}.\] Thus nature's finite-dimensional optimization can be replaced by scalar convex minimization and an analytical exponential tilt.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a finite-support KL ambiguity set, worst-case expectation reduces to scalar temperature minimization, with the worst-case probabilities given by exponential tilting when the optimum is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytical Worst-Case Distribution Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits analytical worst-case-distribution methods, and the KL dual formula and conditional exponential tilt are plausible. A specifically located DRO source is required to support the exact dual representation, limiting case at zero temperature, attainment conditions, and active-constraint qualification.

assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) is a decision set and \(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty ambiguity set of probability measures.
For every \(x\in X\), the expectation \(\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\) is defined for all \(P\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle either returns a violating distribution or certifies \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility of the distributional constraint.

notation.meaning: Loss at decision x under uncertainty xi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate separation for a worst-case expectation constraint over an ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \((x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R\), an \(\varepsilon\)-distributional separation oracle for the constraint \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\le t\) performs one of two valid actions: it returns \(P_x\in\mathcal P\) satisfying \(\mathbb E_{P_x}[\ell(x,\xi)]>t\), thereby exhibiting a violated inequality; or it certifies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\le t+\varepsilon\). An exact oracle is the case \(\varepsilon=0\). The returned distribution induces the valid master constraint \(\mathbb E_{P_x}[\ell(x,\xi)]\le t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributional separation oracle finds a distribution violating a candidate worst-case expectation bound or certifies that the bound is feasible within a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributional Separation Oracles

children.title: DRO Exchange Methods
children.top_down_role: Iterative enrichment of active distributional or uncertainty representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: DRO Exchange Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-exchange method applied to the distribution-indexed epigraph formulation of DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite \(\mathcal P_0\subseteq\mathcal P\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R} c(x)+t\) subject to \(\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\le t\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_k\), obtaining \((x_k,t_k)\). Invoke a distributional separation oracle at \((x_k,t_k)\). If it certifies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x_k,\xi)]\le t_k+\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise, for a returned violator \(P_k^+\), set \(\mathcal P_{k+1}=\mathcal P_k\cup\{P_k^+\}\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exchange method repeatedly solves a DRO problem over finitely many retained distributions and adds a violating distribution whenever the current solution fails separation over the full ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and each restricted master problem attains a solution.
A distributional separation oracle is available for \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration either returns an \(\varepsilon\)-feasible incumbent or enlarges the finite distribution set by a newly violated distribution.

notation.meaning: Finite set of distributions retained at iteration k

children.title: DRO Cutting-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Restricted DRO formulations enlarged through selected cuts or adversarial elements.

assumptions_latex: The DRO epigraph admits valid cuts generated from solved distributional or dual subproblems.
Each master problem over the accumulated cuts is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration either certifies the incumbent within tolerance or adds a globally valid cut violated by that incumbent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer approximation of a distributionally robust epigraph by accumulated valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite family \(\mathcal C_0\) of functions satisfying \(q(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(q\in\mathcal C_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R} c(x)+t\) subject to \(q(x)\le t\) for every \(q\in\mathcal C_k\), yielding \((x_k,t_k)\). Evaluate a distributional or dual subproblem at \(x_k\). If \(Q(x_k)\le t_k+\varepsilon\), stop. Otherwise generate a valid \(q_k\) with \(q_k(x_k)>t_k\), set \(\mathcal C_{k+1}=\mathcal C_k\cup\{q_k\}\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutting-set method outer-approximates the worst-case epigraph, adding a valid cut from the distributional subproblem whenever the current master underestimates the worst-case value.
knowledge_statements.title: DRO Cutting-Set Methods

children.title: Exchange–Cutting-Set Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where exchange and cutting-set viewpoints coincide or diverge.

assumptions_latex: Every retained distribution \(P\) defines the valid epigraph inequality \(\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\le t\).
The separation subproblem returns an actual distribution in \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distribution exchange and addition of distribution-induced cuts generate identical restricted feasible regions when initialized consistently.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for cuts indexed directly by distributions, excluding aggregated or purely dual cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any finite \(S\subseteq\mathcal P\), define \(F(S)=\{(x,t)\in X\times\mathbb R:q_P(x)\le t\text{ for every }P\in S\}\), where \(q_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)]\). Retaining \(P\) in a distribution-exchange master is therefore exactly equivalent to retaining the cut \(q_P(x)\le t\) in a cutting-set master. If both procedures start from the same \(S_0\), select the same violating distribution at each iteration, and solve their masters consistently, then their master feasible regions and optimal values coincide at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping a distribution in an exchange master is equivalent to keeping its expected-loss inequality as a cut; synchronized methods therefore produce the same restricted masters.
knowledge_statements.title: Exchange–Cutting-Set Correspondence

children.title: Finite-Representation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits imposed by infinite supports, weak separation, or noncompact ambiguity.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set may contain infinitely many distributions.
No structural assumption guarantees a finite exact epigraph description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination cannot be inferred solely from compactness or attainment of the distributional supremum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between finite exact distribution representations and genuinely semi-infinite DRO masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite distribution representation on \(X\) exists when there are \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\mathcal P\) such that \(Q(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}q_{P_i}(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Without such a representation, an exchange method need not terminate after finitely many additions, even if \(\mathcal P\) is compact and the supremum defining \(Q(x)\) is attained for each \(x\). Compactness ensures existence of pointwise maximizers under suitable continuity, but it does not ensure that one finite collection of distributions represents \(Q\) simultaneously over all decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise attainment of worst-case distributions does not imply that finitely many distributions represent the worst-case value for every decision, so finite exchange termination may fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Representation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between pointwise attainment and a uniform finite representation is plausible, but the cited generic cutting-plane section does not establish the asserted DRO finite-termination boundary. A precise theorem or DRO example with compact ambiguity set, attained pointwise suprema, and no finite exact representation is required.

children.title: DRO Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Master–subproblem decomposition for distributionally robust formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: DRO Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders outer approximation for a two-stage DRO value function with supporting cuts supplied by strongly dualized subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite cut set \(J_0\) for which the restricted master attains a solution. At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}c^{\mathsf T}x+\theta\) subject to \(\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(j\in J_k\), obtaining \((x_k,\theta_k)\). Solve the distributionally robust recourse subproblem at \(x_k\) to obtain \(Q(x_k)\) and dual data defining a supporting affine minorant \(\alpha_k+\beta_k^{\mathsf T}x\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with equality at \(x_k\). Stop when \(Q(x_k)-\theta_k\le\varepsilon\); otherwise set \(J_{k+1}=J_k\cup\{k\}\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DRO Benders decomposition alternates between an attaining first-stage master and a distributionally robust recourse subproblem whose dual solution supplies a supporting value-function cut.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty feasible set, and the distributionally robust recourse value \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\) is finite and admits affine supporting minorants.
For every evaluated \(x_k\in X\), strong subproblem duality supplies an affine function that is no greater than \(Q\) on \(X\) and equals \(Q\) at \(x_k\).
The initial and subsequently generated restricted master problems attain solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each master gives a valid lower bound, and the method stops when its evaluated incumbent gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: First-stage feasible set and cost vector

children.title: DRO Scenario Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition across scenarios, support points, or sampled distributional representatives.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty model has a finite scenario set \(S\).
For fixed master variables, scenario recourse subproblems are separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distributionally robust recourse evaluation decomposes into scenario subproblems coupled only through master or ambiguity-set variables.

notation.meaning: Scenario probability vector in an ambiguity set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support DRO decomposition across separable scenario recourse subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current decision \(x_k\), solve the scenario recourse problems defining \(Q_s(x_k)\) independently for all \(s\in S\). Then solve the coupling problem \(\max_{p\in\mathcal U}\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x_k)\), where \(\mathcal U\) is the ambiguity set of scenario probabilities. Use the resulting probabilities and scenario primal or dual solutions to update the master problem. Stop when the master lower bound and the evaluated distributionally robust objective differ by at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise repeat with the updated master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario decomposition solves recourse independently by scenario and then maximizes their weighted values over ambiguous probabilities before updating the shared master problem.
knowledge_statements.title: DRO Scenario Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario evaluation and ambiguity-coupling formula are plausible for finite-support probability ambiguity, but “update the master” does not specify a complete decomposition algorithm or the cuts used to maintain its lower bound. The cited stochastic-programming section does not establish this particular DRO version.

children.title: Benders–Scenario Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Architectures combining master cuts with scenario-partitioned subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The DRO model has finitely indexed, separable scenario recourse and a strongly dualizable ambiguity coupling problem.
Scenario solutions yield valid master cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hybrid adds selected scenario information and Benders cuts while preserving valid lower bounds on the full DRO objective.

notation.meaning: Active scenario subset at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid decomposition combining scenario activation with Benders value-function cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an active scenario set \(S_0\) and a valid Benders-cut family. At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master, evaluate recourse for scenarios in \(S_k\), and solve a distributional separation problem over the full ambiguity model. Add any scenario receiving relevant worst-case mass to \(S_{k+1}\), and add affine Benders minorants obtained from solved scenario or ambiguity subproblems. Return the incumbent when no omitted scenario or distribution produces violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\) and the master lower bound differs from the evaluated value \(Q(x_k)\) by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid method activates relevant scenarios while generating Benders cuts, stopping only when omitted scenarios are harmless and the master bound is sufficiently accurate.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders–Scenario Hybrids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The notions of relevant worst-case mass, omitted-scenario violation, and the valid cuts generated from partially active scenarios depend on the precise ambiguity model. The generic decomposition citations do not determine a reliable mathematical version of this hybrid.

children.title: Scenario Scalability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Support growth, weak cuts, or scenario proliferation limiting decomposition performance.

assumptions_latex: There are \(N\) explicitly enumerated scenarios.
A full iteration evaluates every scenario recourse subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full scenario evaluation requires at least \(N\) scenario accesses per iteration, although parallelism can reduce elapsed time.

notation.meaning: Cost of solving scenario s recourse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration scaling for explicit finite-scenario decomposition, excluding ambiguity-coupling and master costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the explicit-scenario oracle model, any iteration that exactly evaluates all scenario recourse values accesses \(N\) scenarios and has serial recourse work \(\sum_{s\in S}T_s\). With \(W\) identical workers and no communication overhead, its recourse makespan is at least \(\max\{\max_{s\in S}T_s,\,W^{-1}\sum_{s\in S}T_s\}\). Thus decomposition exposes parallelism but does not remove linear aggregate dependence on \(N\). Scenario generation or sampling can avoid full enumeration, but then exact separation requires additional structure or is replaced by a probabilistic accuracy guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact evaluation over N explicit scenarios performs N scenario accesses per iteration; parallel workers reduce wall time but not the total scenario work.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Scalability Boundaries
Stochastic Primal–Dual Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic primal-dual iteration for a convex-concave saddle reformulation of DRO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \((x_0,y_0)\in X\times Y\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(\zeta_k\), compute stochastic directions satisfying \(\mathbb E[g_k^x\mid x_k,y_k]\in\partial_xL(x_k,y_k)\) and \(\mathbb E[g_k^y\mid x_k,y_k]\in\partial_y^+L(x_k,y_k)\), where \(\partial_y^+\) denotes the superdifferential in the concave variable. Update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\eta_kg_k^x)\) and \(y_{k+1}=\Pi_Y(y_k+\eta_kg_k^y)\). After \(K\) iterations, return \(\bar x_K=(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_kx_k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_k)\) and \(\bar y_K=(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_ky_k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta_k)\), or stop earlier under a prescribed statistically valid gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic primal-dual method uses unbiased sampled subgradients for primal descent and supergradients for dual ascent on a DRO saddle formulation, then returns step-size-weighted averaged iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) are nonempty closed convex sets.
The saddle function \(L(x,y)=\mathbb E[\widehat L(x,y;\zeta)]\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(y\), and the sampled directions have the stated conditional subgradient and supergradient means.
The Euclidean projections \(\Pi_X\) and \(\Pi_Y\) are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns weighted averaged primal and dual iterates intended to have a small expected saddle-point gap under an applicable convergence guarantee.

notation.meaning: Stochastic primal subgradient and dual supergradient
Superdifferential of L in its concave dual variable

\(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration uses one sample and produces a projected stochastic subgradient update.

At iteration \(k\), draw one sample \(\zeta_k\), compute \(g_k=g(x_k;\zeta_k)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[g_k\mid x_k]\in\partial F(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\eta_kg_k)\). children.top_down_role: First-order DRO methods using grouped sampled contributions.

assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x_k\), the sampled subgradients are independent and identically distributed with mean in \(\partial F(x_k)\).
\(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A batch of size \(b_k\) yields an unbiased averaged direction whose conditional variance is reduced by the factor \(b_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected minibatch stochastic subgradient regime with independent within-batch samples.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), draw conditionally independent samples \(\zeta_{k,1},\ldots,\zeta_{k,b_k}\), form \(\bar g_k=b_k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{b_k}g(x_k;\zeta_{k,i})\), and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\eta_k\bar g_k)\). If each sample direction has conditional covariance \(\Sigma_k\), then \(\mathbb E[\bar g_k\mid x_k]\in\partial F(x_k)\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\bar g_k\mid x_k)=\Sigma_k/b_k\). After a fixed sample or iteration budget, output the prescribed last or averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minibatch DRO method averages independent sampled subgradients before each projected update, preserving unbiasedness and dividing conditional gradient variance by the batch size.

children.title: Adaptive Batch-Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Batch-size choices responsive to variance, progress, or computational budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Batch-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic first-order minimization with variance-driven batch growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(X\), objective \(F(x)=\mathbb E[\ell(x,\xi)]\), stepsizes \(\alpha_t>0\), tolerance \(\eta_t>0\), and initial \(x_0\in X\), draw samples until a batch of size \(b_t\) has sample-mean gradient \(g_t\) and estimated variance \(v_t\) satisfying \(v_t/b_t\leq \eta_t^2\). Set \(x_{t+1}=\Pi_X(x_t-\alpha_t g_t)\). Increase \(b_t\) whenever the inequality fails. Stop when a prescribed iteration or projected-gradient criterion is met; otherwise return the weighted average \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{t<T}\alpha_t x_t)/(\sum_{t<T}\alpha_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase each stochastic-gradient batch until its estimated mean-gradient noise meets a chosen tolerance, then take a projected step and return a stopping iterate or weighted average.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Conditional on \(x_t\), sampled gradients are unbiased with finite second moment.
The variance estimator and batch samples use a specified measurable sampling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t/b_t\leq\eta_t^2\) controls the estimated conditional variance of every accepted batch gradient.

children.title: Sampling-Noise Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where sampling noise or costly ambiguity evaluation impairs reliability.

assumptions_latex: The initial value \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) is deterministic.
\(\varepsilon_{t,i}\) are mutually independent, independent of \(x_0\), and satisfy \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{t,i}]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{t,i}^2]=\sigma^2\).
The batch size \(b\in\mathbb N\) is fixed and the constant step satisfies \(0<\alpha<2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb E[x_t^2]=\frac{\alpha\sigma^2}{b(2-\alpha)}>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact formula follows from the scalar AR(1) second-moment recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step minibatch SGD exhibits a nonzero noise floor even on a scalar quadratic.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) be deterministic. Consider \(F(x)=x^2/2\) and minibatch gradients \(g_t=x_t+\bar\varepsilon_t\), where \(\bar\varepsilon_t=b^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^b\varepsilon_{t,i}\), the noises are mutually independent, independent of \(x_0\), and have mean zero and variance \(\sigma^2>0\). If \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha g_t\), \(b\in\mathbb N\), and \(0<\alpha<2\), then \[\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb E[x_t^2]=\frac{\alpha\sigma^2}{b(2-\alpha)}.\] Consequently, fixed \(\alpha\) and finite \(b\) cannot yield mean-square convergence to the minimizer; reducing the error below an arbitrary prescribed level requires decreasing stepsizes, increasing batches, or variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a scalar quadratic, constant-step minibatch SGD started from a deterministic finite point has an exact positive mean-square noise floor proportional to the step size and inversely proportional to the batch size.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Inner Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner approximation of a robust feasible region, preserving robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For decision set \(X\), uncertainty set \(U\), and constraint mapping \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb R^m\), define the robust feasible set \(F(U)=\{x\in X:f_j(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). A tractable set \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq X\) is a safe inner approximation when \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq F(U)\). Hence every point feasible for the approximation satisfies every original uncertain constraint. For minimization, restricting to \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\) can increase the optimal value but cannot produce a falsely robust-feasible decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe inner approximation is a tractable subset of the true robust feasible set; every approximate-feasible decision is therefore robust feasible.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain inequalities are interpreted componentwise for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F_{\mathrm{in}}\Longrightarrow x\in F(U)\).

assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\widehat U\).
Both robust problems use the same decision set \(X\), constraint mapping \(f\), and objective \(c:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\widehat U)\subseteq F(U)\) and \(v(\widehat U)\geq v(U)\).
