knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superset approximations of uncertainty produce conservative robust feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(f:X\times\widehat U\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(U\subseteq\widehat U\). For every \(V\subseteq\widehat U\), define \(F(V)=\{x\in X:f_j(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in V,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Then uncertainty-set inclusion reverses feasible-set inclusion: \[F(\widehat U)\subseteq F(U).\] Thus enforcing the constraints over \(\widehat U\) is safe for \(U\). For an objective \(c:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define \(v(V)=\inf_{x\in F(V)}c(x)\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(v(\widehat U)\geq v(U)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the uncertainty set shrinks the robust feasible set, giving a safe but potentially conservative approximation and a no-smaller minimization infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer Approximations of Uncertainty Sets

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set, \(U\) is an uncertainty set, and \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb R^m\).
\(U_N=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) is a finite subset of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(U)\subseteq F_N\), and the inclusion can be strict.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set inclusion and counterexample are directly checkable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario enforcement is generally an outer relaxation of robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(U\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb R^m\). Define \(F(U)=\{x\in X:f_j(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). For a finite scenario set \(U_N=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\subseteq U\), define \(F_N=\{x\in X:f_j(x,u^i)\leq0\text{ for all }i=1,\ldots,N,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Then \(F(U)\subseteq F_N\), so scenario discretization alone need not certify robust feasibility. Concretely, with \(U=[0,1]\), \(X=\mathbb R\), and the constraint \(u-x\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\), the robust set is \([1,\infty)\), whereas any finite scenario set omitting \(1\) gives \(F_N=[\max_i u^i,\infty)\), which contains nonrobust decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite scenario subset enlarges, or leaves unchanged, the feasible region. The interval example shows that omitted worst cases can make scenario-feasible decisions nonrobust.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Discretization

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Robust Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-lemma semidefinite representation for one Euclidean-ball quadratic uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_x(u)=u^{\mathsf T}Q(x)u+2q(x)^{\mathsf T}u+q_0(x)\), where \(Q(x)\) is symmetric, and let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:\|u\|_2\leq1\}\). If \(U\) has a strict interior point, then the robust quadratic constraint \(q_x(u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying \[\begin{pmatrix}Q(x)-\lambda I&q(x)\\q(x)^{\mathsf T}&q_0(x)+\lambda\end{pmatrix}\preceq0.\] When the coefficient maps are affine in \(x\), this is a semidefinite-representable robust constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic constraint over one Euclidean ball, the S-lemma converts universal feasibility exactly into existence of a scalar multiplier satisfying one linear matrix inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=Q(x)^{\mathsf T}\).
The ball constraint satisfies Slater's condition.
Coefficient dependence is affine when SDP tractability is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_x(u)\leq0\ \forall u\in U\) is equivalent to the displayed LMI with some \(\lambda\geq0\).

children.title: Sum-of-Squares Robust Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Polynomial positivity relaxations for robust optimization structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Robust Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated quadratic-module certificate for polynomial robust inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:g_j(u)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(p_x(u)\) be a polynomial. A degree-\(2d\) SOS robust certificate is a collection of sum-of-squares polynomials \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) such that \[-p_x(u)=\sigma_0(u)+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(u)g_j(u),\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\leq2d.\] Because every term on the right is nonnegative on \(U\), the certificate implies \(p_x(u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\). Gram-matrix representations of the \(\sigma_j\) turn coefficient matching into semidefinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS decomposition of the negative uncertain polynomial using nonnegative set generators certifies the robust inequality and is checkable through semidefinite constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is described by polynomial inequalities \(g_j(u)\geq0\).
Each \(\sigma_j\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial satisfying the stated degree bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identity certifies \(p_x(u)\leq0\) for all \(u\in U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Moment–SOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-d moment relaxation and SOS dual for worst-case polynomial evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U=\{u:g_j(u)\geq0\}\) and polynomial \(p_x\), the order-\(d\) relaxation of \(\sup_{u\in U}p_x(u)\) is \[\rho_d(x)=\sup_y\{L_y(p_x):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \forall j\},\] where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Its SOS dual minimizes \(\gamma\) subject to \(\gamma-p_x=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\) with the corresponding degree bounds. Under strong duality these values coincide; under an Archimedean quadratic module, \(\rho_d(x)\downarrow\sup_{u\in U}p_x(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment SDPs upper-bound worst-case polynomial values, while dual SOS certificates provide the same bound under strong duality; Archimedean hierarchies converge monotonically.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation order is large enough that \(d\geq d_j\) for every generator.
Strong duality is assumed for equality of the finite-order primal and dual values.
The generated quadratic module is Archimedean for asymptotic convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The moment and SOS bounds coincide under strong duality, and \(\rho_d(x)\downarrow\sup_{u\in U}p_x(u)\) under the Archimedean condition.

notation.meaning: linear functional associated with truncated moments y

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Tightness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative polynomials need not possess an unweighted SOS certificate of fixed degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Motzkin polynomial \[m(a,b)=a^4b^2+a^2b^4+1-3a^2b^2\] is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) by the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality, but it is not a sum of squares of polynomials. Therefore nonnegativity, and hence a valid polynomial robust inequality, need not be captured by the unweighted SOS cone at the polynomial's degree. Set multipliers, higher relaxation orders, or stronger structural assumptions may restore certification; even under Archimedean convergence, finite-order exactness is an additional property and is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative Motzkin polynomial is not SOS, showing that a fixed unweighted SOS relaxation can miss valid robust inequalities and that finite convergence needs extra structure.
assumptions_latex: SOS means a finite sum of squares of real polynomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(a,b)\geq0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), but \(m\notin\Sigma[a,b]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Tractability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-dual reformulation of robust affine inequalities over bounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Du\leq d\}\) be nonempty and suppose \(\sup_{u\in U}a(x)^{\mathsf T}u\) is finite. Then \[a(x)^{\mathsf T}u+b(x)\leq0\quad\forall u\in U\] is equivalent, by linear-programming duality, to existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) such that \[D^{\mathsf T}\lambda=a(x),\qquad d^{\mathsf T}\lambda+b(x)\leq0.\] If \(a(x)\) and \(b(x)\) are affine and the remaining model is linear or convex-representable, the robust counterpart adds only linear constraints and nonnegative dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust affine inequality over a polyhedron becomes finitely many linear constraints through LP duality, provided the uncertainty maximization is feasible and bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(U=\{u:Du\leq d\}\) is nonempty.
The support problem in direction \(a(x)\) has a finite optimum.
Coefficient maps are affine when linear tractability is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying the displayed dual constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal Tractability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order-cone reformulation of robust affine inequalities over ellipsoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{\bar u+Pz:z\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|z\|_2\leq1\}\). For any coefficient vector \(a(x)\) and scalar \(b(x)\), \[a(x)^{\mathsf T}u+b(x)\leq0\quad\forall u\in U\] holds if and only if \[a(x)^{\mathsf T}\bar u+b(x)+\|P^{\mathsf T}a(x)\|_2\leq0.\] Thus, when \(a(x)\) and \(b(x)\) are affine, each such robust affine constraint is second-order-cone representable. The conclusion concerns affine uncertainty dependence; general uncertain quadratic systems need not admit this SOCP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing an affine expression over an ellipsoid yields a Euclidean norm, so robust affine constraints have exact second-order-cone formulations.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set has the stated affine image-of-a-ball representation.
The uncertain constraint depends affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal ellipsoidal constraint is equivalent to the displayed norm inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectrahedral Tractability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite-dual reformulation for affine optimization over a spectrahedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:A_0+\sum_{i=1}^ku_iA_i\succeq0\}\), and assume this spectrahedron has a strictly feasible point and the support value in direction \(a(x)\) is finite. Then \[a(x)^{\mathsf T}u+b(x)\leq0\quad\forall u\in U\] is equivalent to existence of \(Z\succeq0\) satisfying \[\langle A_i,Z\rangle=-a_i(x)\quad(i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad b(x)-\langle A_0,Z\rangle\leq0.\] Hence affine coefficient maps yield a semidefinite-representable robust counterpart under conic strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Slater regularity, a robust affine inequality over a spectrahedron is equivalent to an SDP-dual certificate consisting of one positive semidefinite matrix and linear equations.
assumptions_latex: The spectrahedron has a strictly feasible point.
Its support value in direction \(a(x)\) is finite.
The matrices \(A_i\) are symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal constraint is equivalent to existence of the displayed semidefinite dual certificate \(Z\succeq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: semidefinite conic duality under Slater regularity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source is supplied, and the displayed SDP certificate has an inconsistent objective sign. With the equations \(\langle A_i,Z\rangle=-a_i(x)\), weak duality gives \(\sup_{u\in U}a(x)^{\mathsf T}u\leq\langle A_0,Z\rangle\), so the robust inequality requires \(b(x)+\langle A_0,Z\rangle\leq0\), not \(b(x)-\langle A_0,Z\rangle\leq0\). The mathematical representation must be corrected and sourced.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^m\) and threshold \(\beta\in\mathbb{Q}\) are part of the input.
The uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) is represented by a polynomial-size system of rational linear inequalities.
Linear maximization over the represented family of uncertainty sets is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deciding whether \(c^{\mathsf T}u\leq\beta\) holds for every \(u\in U\) is coNP-hard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary nonconvex uncertainty represented by rational linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), let \(\beta\in\mathbb{Q}\), and let \(U\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) have a polynomial-size rational linear description. The robust constraint requires \(c^{\mathsf T}u\leq\beta\) for every \(u\in U\), and a violation exists exactly when \[\max_{u\in U}c^{\mathsf T}u>\beta.\] If linear maximization over the represented family of sets \(U\) is NP-hard, detecting a violation is NP-hard and deciding robust feasibility is coNP-hard. Thus a compact description of nonconvex uncertainty does not by itself imply a polynomial-time robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compactly described binary uncertainty set, robust feasibility is coNP-hard whenever linear maximization over that represented family is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Uncertainty Intractability

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, bounded, convex, and presented by a strong separation oracle.
The rational encoding and inner and outer radii of \(K\) have polynomial bit length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation and linear optimization over \(K\) are polynomial-time oracle equivalent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-oracle equivalence for bounded rational convex bodies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the rational oracle model, a strong separation oracle for \(K\) permits the ellipsoid method to compute, for every rational \(c\), a point attaining \(\min_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x\) using polynomially many oracle calls and arithmetic operations. Conversely, a strong linear-optimization oracle over \(K\) yields strong separation through the standard optimization-to-separation reduction. Polynomiality is measured in \(n\), input bit length, and the logarithms of the supplied radius bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded rational convex body with suitable radius data, strong separation and exact linear optimization can simulate one another in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation–Optimization Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is a theorem rather than a generic property, and its exact form depends on the strong-oracle definitions, rationality model, well-boundedness assumptions, and output convention. No source or inspectable locator is supplied for those details.

assumptions_latex: The domain \(D\) contains \(N\) distinct points.
An algorithm learns an arbitrary objective only through exact value-oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every deterministic exact minimization algorithm requires \(N\) oracle queries in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic hardness without convexity or structural assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{u_1,\ldots,u_N\}\), and let an algorithm query values of an otherwise unrestricted function \(f:D\to\{0,1\}\). After fewer than \(N\) queries, an adversary may answer \(1\) at every queried point and assign value \(0\) to one unqueried point. The transcript is also consistent with the constant-one function. Hence no deterministic algorithm can always return an exact minimizer with fewer than \(N\) value-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unstructured objective on an N-point domain, an adversary can force any deterministic exact optimizer to query every point.
knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial-Oracle Hardness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain lower bound is mathematically plausible and the complexity-bound role fits, but the record contains an adversary proof and supplies no citation. An authoritative oracle-complexity locator is required before a source-grounded statement can be settled.

assumptions_latex: The feasible domain is \(D=\{a,b\}\).
Each oracle response differs from the true function value by at most \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case deterministic optimization error below \(2\delta\) is impossible, and randomized expected error below \(\delta\) is impossible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp information limit for adversarial additive value errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f_a(a)=0\), \(f_a(b)=2\delta\), \(f_b(a)=2\delta\), and \(f_b(b)=0\). The oracle that returns \(\delta\) at both points is valid for either objective, so no sequence of queries distinguishes them. Every deterministic output has suboptimality \(2\delta\) for one objective. Under a uniform random choice between \(f_a\) and \(f_b\), every randomized algorithm has expected suboptimality at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive oracle error creates an unavoidable optimization-error floor, even on a two-point feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Oracle Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishability example supports the stated deterministic and randomized error floors, but it is presented as proof text and has no citation. A source must also fix the precise adversarial-error and randomized-performance model.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb{N}\) scenarios be explicitly listed with rational probabilities \(p_s\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s=1}^S p_s=1\). Let \(x\) be a continuous first-stage vector and \(y_s\) a continuous recourse vector for scenario \(s\). For rational data of compatible dimensions, the extensive form \[\min_{x,y_1,\ldots,y_S} c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s=1}^S p_s q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\geq b,\quad W_sy_s\geq h_s-T_sx,\quad y_s\geq0\quad(s=1,\ldots,S)\] is a rational linear program. Its numbers of variables and constraints grow linearly with the explicitly encoded scenario blocks, so it is solvable in time polynomial in the extensive-form bit length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicitly encoded finite-scenario problem with continuous linear recourse is a rational linear program of size linear in its scenario blocks and is polynomial-time solvable in that explicit encoding.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^k\) is an integer recourse decision, where \(k\) is part of the input.
The vectors and matrices \(q,W,h,T\) and any fixed first-stage vector \(x\) have rational entries of compatible dimensions.
The uncertainty set is permitted to be a singleton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Evaluating the integer-recourse value and optimizing a general model containing it are NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General rational integer recourse with dimension included in the input; hardness already occurs in the deterministic singleton case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be fixed and let \(q,W,h,T\) be rational data of compatible dimensions. For an input dimension \(k\), define the integer-recourse value \[Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\geq h-Tx,\ y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^k\}.\] When the uncertainty set is a singleton and \(x\) is fixed or absent, evaluating \(Q(x)\) contains rational integer linear optimization as a special case. Hence evaluating general integer recourse, and optimizing a general model containing such recourse, is NP-hard. This conclusion does not cover restricted regimes such as fixed dimension or specially structured matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General integer-recourse evaluation and optimization are NP-hard because rational integer linear optimization is recovered when uncertainty is a singleton and the first-stage decision is fixed or absent.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Recourse Complexity

assumptions_latex: A horizon has \(T\) decision stages and branching factor at most \(b\).
Decisions are continuous and constraints are rational linear constraints indexed by scenario-tree nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit formulation is polynomial in the tree size but can be exponential in \(T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit scenario-tree formulation with nonanticipative continuous policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign one decision vector to every scenario-tree node and identify decisions sharing the same observed history. The resulting nonanticipative extensive form is a linear program of size polynomial in the number \(M\) of explicitly represented nodes. For a full tree with branching factor \(b>1\), \[M=1+b+\cdots+b^{T-1}=\frac{b^T-1}{b-1}.\] Thus solution time is polynomial in the explicit tree encoding but the representation itself grows exponentially with the horizon \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous multistage model is polynomial in its explicit scenario tree, although that tree grows exponentially with the horizon under persistent branching.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Policy Complexity

assumptions_latex: There are \(N\) explicitly listed uncertainty scenarios and \(K\) candidate recourse policies.
Each scenario must be assigned to one feasible candidate policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit assignment enumeration has \(K^N\) cases; endogenous assignment admits a mixed-integer formulation with \(NK\) binary indicators.

There are \(K^N\) possible complete assignments of \(N\) scenarios to \(K\) labeled policies. A direct endogenous formulation uses \(NK\) binary variables \(z_{sk}\), together with policy parameters and indicator constraints enforcing feasibility whenever \(z_{sk}=1\). For any fixed assignment, continuous affine-policy subproblems may be linear, while optimizing the assignment remains combinatorial.

assumptions_latex: The outcome support \(\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\}\) is finite.
The ambiguity set of probabilities is a nonempty rational polytope \(P\subseteq\{p\geq0:\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case expectation evaluation is a linear program and has a finite-dimensional linear dual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support distributionally robust expectation with polyhedral probability ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P=\{p\in\mathbb{R}^N_+:Ap\leq d,\;\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=1\}\), then for every fixed decision \(x\), \[\sup_{p\in P}\sum_{i=1}^N p_i\ell_i(x)\] is a rational linear program in \(N\) probability variables. Its linear-programming dual is finite-dimensional and, under feasibility and boundedness, has the same optimal value. Consequently, when the dualized loss constraints and the decision set are linear-representable, the complete finite-support DRO problem has a finite linear robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite support and polyhedral probability ambiguity, worst-case expectation is an LP and can be dualized into a finite formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support DRO Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-decision worst-case expectation is an LP over a polyhedral probability set, but no DRO or linear-duality source is supplied. The additional conclusion about a complete finite linear robust counterpart depends on precise representability assumptions that also require support.

assumptions_latex: The support set is \(\Xi\), and \(g_j:\Xi\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(j=0,ldots,r\) are measurable moment functions with \(g_0\equiv1\).
The prescribed moments are \(m_j\in\mathbb{R}\), with \(m_0=1\), and the loss is a measurable function \(\ell:\Xi\to\mathbb{R}\).
The ambiguity set is nonempty, the worst-case expectation is finite, and conditions sufficient for strong generalized-moment duality hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case expectation equals a finite-variable semi-infinite dual problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-moment DRO under an explicit strong generalized-moment-duality assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_j:\Xi\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(j=0,\ldots,r\) be measurable moment functions, let \(g_0\equiv1\), and let \(m_0=1\). Define \(\mathcal P=\{P:\operatorname{supp}(P)\subseteq\Xi,\ \mathbb E_P[g_j(\xi)]=m_j\text{ for }j=0,\ldots,r\}\). If \(\mathcal P\) is nonempty, the worst-case expectation is finite, and strong generalized-moment duality holds, then \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(\xi)]=\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{r+1}}\left\{\sum_{j=0}^r\lambda_jm_j:\sum_{j=0}^r\lambda_jg_j(\xi)\geq\ell(\xi)\ \text{for every }\xi\in\Xi\right\}.\] The dual has finitely many variables and generally infinitely many constraints, so its tractability depends on the domination constraint over \(\Xi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong generalized-moment duality, equality-moment DRO has finitely many dual multipliers but generally retains one domination constraint for every point in the support set.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-DRO Complexity

assumptions_latex: \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}\) is empirical.
The ambiguity set is a radius-\(\rho\) 1-Wasserstein ball with lower-semicontinuous transport cost \(d\).
The loss satisfies conditions ensuring Wasserstein strong duality and finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case expectation has a scalar-plus-sample supremum representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical 1-Wasserstein ambiguity with transport-cost dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Wasserstein strong duality, \[\sup_{P:W_d(P,\widehat P_N)\leq\rho}\mathbb E_P[\ell(\xi)]=\inf_{\lambda\geq0}\left\{\lambda\rho+\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\sup_{\xi\in\Xi}\bigl(\ell(\xi)-\lambda d(\xi,\widehat\xi_i)\bigr)\right\}.\] Thus evaluation reduces to a one-dimensional outer minimization and \(N\) pointwise adversarial subproblems. Polynomial-time solvability follows only when these subproblems have polynomial-size tractable reformulations or polynomial-time separation oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wasserstein DRO reduces to one transport multiplier and one adversarial loss subproblem per sample; tractability depends on those subproblems.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport-DRO Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed transport dual is a standard form, but the precise theorem depends on the definition of W_d, the topology and measurability of Xi, properties of the transport cost, and growth or semicontinuity conditions on the loss. Those conditions are left schematic and no source is supplied, so the mathematical version cannot be certified.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity family permits a singleton distribution.
The recourse problem contains rational mixed-integer linear decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case expected mixed-integer recourse evaluation and optimization are NP-hard in general.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness inherited from deterministic mixed-integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the DRO objective contain \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\), where \(Q\) is the optimal value of a mixed-integer linear recourse problem. Choose \(\mathcal P=\{\delta_{\xi_0}\}\), a singleton ambiguity set. Then the worst-case expectation equals \(Q(x,\xi_0)\), so deterministic mixed-integer recourse is a special case. Because that special case contains integer linear optimization, general mixed-integer-recourse DRO evaluation and optimization are NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer-recourse DRO is NP-hard because a singleton ambiguity set recovers deterministic mixed-integer recourse as a special case.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer-Recourse DRO Hardness

assumptions_latex: The decision set is \(X\), the uncertainty set \(U\) is nonempty, and \(x\in X\).
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the constraint function \(g_i:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) is well-defined.
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(v_i\le 0\) for every \(i\), then \(x\) is robust feasible; if \(v_i\le\varepsilon\) for every \(i\), then its worst certified constraint violation is at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified upper bounds on worst-case violations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic certificate for a finite robust constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x\in X\) and the robust constraints \(g_i(x,u)\le 0\) for every \(u\in U\) and every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). A collection \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\in\mathbb R^m\) is a worst-case feasibility certificate when its entries are verifiable upper bounds satisfying \[\sup_{u\in U}g_i(x,u)\le v_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\] The bounds may come from exact maximization or from valid dual upper bounds; attainment of the supremum is not required. Defining \(v=\max_{1\le i\le m}v_i\), the condition \(v\le 0\) certifies robust feasibility, while \(v\le\varepsilon\) certifies that every worst-case constraint violation is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified upper bounds on all worst-case constraint violations provide a feasibility certificate: nonpositive bounds certify exact robust feasibility, and bounds no larger than the stated tolerance certify approximate robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Feasibility Certificates

assumptions_latex: The robust primal is a minimization problem with finite optimal value \(p^\star\).
The point \(x\) is primal feasible, the point \(y\) is feasible for a valid dual problem, and weak duality holds.
The requested tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f(x)-q(y)\le\varepsilon\), then \(0\le f(x)-p^\star\le\varepsilon\); if \(f(x)-q(y)=0\), then \(x\) and \(y\) are optimal and the primal and dual optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for robust minimization with a valid dual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be feasible for a robust primal minimization problem with objective \(f\) and finite optimal value \(p^\star\). Let \(y\) be feasible for a valid dual problem with objective \(q\) and optimal value \(d^\star\). Weak duality gives \[q(y)\le d^\star\le p^\star\le f(x).\] Hence the computable gap \(G(x,y)=f(x)-q(y)\) bounds the primal error \(f(x)-p^\star\) and the dual error \(d^\star-q(y)\). For every \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), the condition \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate for \(x\). If \(G(x,y)=0\), then \(x\) and \(y\) are optimal and \(p^\star=d^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust-primal feasible point and a valid dual-feasible point certify near-optimality when their objective gap is at most the nonnegative requested tolerance; a zero gap certifies optimality and equality of the optimal values.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Certificates

assumptions_latex: A separation oracle returns certified upper bounds on robust constraint violations.
A bounding oracle returns a certified lower bound on the robust optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping inequalities certify \(\varepsilon_f\)-robust feasibility and \(\varepsilon_o\)-optimality of \(x_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certified oracle bounds directly imply feasibility and objective-gap stopping guarantees
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping rule using certified separation and value bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let a certified separation oracle provide \(V_k\) such that \(\sup_{u\in U}g_i(x_k,u)\le V_k\) for every constraint \(i\). Let a certified bounding oracle provide \(L_k\le p^\star\), where \(p^\star\) is the robust optimal value. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_o\ge0\), the pair of tests \[V_k\le\varepsilon_f,\qquad f(x_k)-L_k\le\varepsilon_o\] is an oracle-based stopping certificate. The first test certifies approximate robust feasibility, and, when \(x_k\) is admissible at that tolerance, the second certifies an objective error of at most \(\varepsilon_o\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified oracle bounds permit stopping once worst-case violation and the objective's lower-bound gap both fall below their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Based Stopping Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the terminal container and the stopping logic is plausible, but no citation is supplied. A dedicated source is needed for the certified separation and lower-bound oracle framework, including the precise admissibility condition under which the objective-gap test certifies optimality.

assumptions_latex: The data-dependent ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_N\) satisfies \(\Pr(P_0\in\mathcal P_N)\ge1-\delta\).
The candidate \(x_N\) satisfies the robust risk bound for every distribution in \(\mathcal P_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr\!\left(\rho_{P_0}(x_N)\le0\right)\ge1-\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coverage of an ambiguity set transfers uniform feasibility to an out-of-sample confidence statement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample certificate induced by ambiguity-set coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be the unknown data-generating distribution and let \(\mathcal P_N\) be constructed from \(N\) observations so that \(\Pr(P_0\in\mathcal P_N)\ge1-\delta\). Suppose the computed decision \(x_N\) has the verifiable uniform certificate \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N}\rho_P(x_N)\le0.\] On the event \(P_0\in\mathcal P_N\), this inequality implies \(\rho_{P_0}(x_N)\le0\). Hence the ambiguity-set coverage statement together with the uniform bound is a statistical robustness certificate with confidence at least \(1-\delta\). The probability here is over the sample used to construct \(\mathcal P_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a confidence region contains the true distribution and the portfolio is feasible throughout that region, true-distribution feasibility holds with the region's confidence level.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Robustness Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf and the coverage-transfer argument is mathematically standard, but it has no cited source. The plain statement also narrows the general decision to a portfolio although the LaTeX statement is not portfolio-specific.

assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
The nominal mean is \(\mu_0\in\mathbb R^n\), the matrix is \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), and the radius satisfies \(\rho\ge 0\).
The uncertain mean-return set is \(M=\{\mu_0+Au:u\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|u\|_2\le\rho\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), the worst-case expected return is \(\mu_0^\top x-\rho\|A^\top x\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoidal mean-return uncertainty with static portfolio weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty feasible portfolio set, let \(\mu_0\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), and let \(\rho\ge 0\). For \[M=\{\mu_0+Au:u\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|u\|_2\le\rho\},\] the robust expected return of every \(x\in X\) satisfies \[\inf_{\mu\in M}\mu^\top x=\mu_0^\top x-\rho\|A^\top x\|_2.\] Consequently, maximizing worst-case expected return has the representation \[\max_{x\in X}\left\{\mu_0^\top x-\rho\|A^\top x\|_2\right\}.\] For a specified target \(r_0\in\mathbb R\), the requirement \(\mu^\top x\ge r_0\) for every \(\mu\in M\) is equivalent to \(\mu_0^\top x-\rho\|A^\top x\|_2\ge r_0\), a second-order-cone representable inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For ellipsoidal mean-return uncertainty, worst-case expected return equals nominal expected return minus a norm penalty, giving a second-order-cone representable robust portfolio model.
knowledge_statements.title: Return-Uncertainty Portfolios

assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
Every matrix in the compact uncertainty set \(S\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) is a valid covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust variance is the support value \(\sigma_S(xx^\top)\).

notation.meaning: support function of the covariance set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quadratic portfolio variance equals a matrix inner product and robustification gives the support function
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static minimum-variance portfolio with covariance uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\) and uncertain covariance \(\Sigma\in S\), portfolio variance is \(x^\top\Sigma x=\langle\Sigma,xx^\top\rangle\). Its robust value therefore has the support-function representation \[\sup_{\Sigma\in S}x^\top\Sigma x=\sup_{\Sigma\in S}\langle\Sigma,xx^\top\rangle=\sigma_S(xx^\top).\] A covariance-robust minimum-variance portfolio solves \[\min_{x\in X}\sigma_S(xx^\top).\] If a claimed variance bound \(t\) is imposed, its robust counterpart is \(x^\top\Sigma x\le t\) for every \(\Sigma\in S\), equivalently \(\sigma_S(xx^\top)\le t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case portfolio variance is the covariance set's support function evaluated at the portfolio outer product, yielding a robust minimum-variance formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Covariance-Uncertainty Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf and the support-function identity is mathematically precise, but no source is cited for the covariance-robust portfolio formulation.

assumptions_latex: Trading occurs at dates \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\).
Uncertainty histories belong to a nonempty scenario set \(U\).
Portfolio policies are nonanticipative and satisfy the specified self-financing and trading constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A robust policy maximizes the minimum terminal wealth over all histories in \(U\).

notation.meaning: terminal wealth under a policy and history

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: robust dynamic optimization uses nonanticipative policies and worst-case terminal performance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-based robust formulation with pathwise trading constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiperiod portfolio policy is a sequence \(\pi=(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{T-1})\) in which each decision \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the observed history \(u_{0:t-1}\), so decisions cannot depend on future uncertainty. Let \(\Pi\) denote the policies satisfying the pathwise self-financing, budget, and trading constraints for every history in \(U\). The robust terminal-wealth model is \[\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\inf_{u_{0:T-1}\in U}W_T(\pi,u_{0:T-1}).\] Thus feasibility is required on every admissible path, while the objective selects a nonanticipative policy with the largest guaranteed terminal wealth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust multiperiod portfolio is a nonanticipative, self-financing trading policy chosen to maximize guaranteed terminal wealth across all admissible return histories.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Multiperiod Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but the model lacks a dedicated source and does not specify the measurable history spaces needed to state nonanticipativity rigorously.

The return uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case relative performance is \(\inf_{r\in U}r^\top(x-b)\).

children.title: Regret-Based Portfolios
children.top_down_role: Robust portfolios organized around worst-case opportunity loss.

assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
The return uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust regret is \(\sup_{r\in U}\left[\max_{y\in X}r^\top y-r^\top x\right]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax regret compares a fixed decision with the scenario-wise hindsight optimum
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static minimax regret relative to hindsight-optimal portfolios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a realized return vector \(r\in U\), the hindsight-optimal return is \(h(r)=\max_{y\in X}r^\top y\). The regret of choosing \(x\in X\) is \[\operatorname{Reg}(x;r)=h(r)-r^\top x\ge0.\] Its robust regret is \(\mathcal R(x)=\sup_{r\in U}\operatorname{Reg}(x;r)\). A regret-based robust portfolio is any solution of \[\min_{x\in X}\sup_{r\in U}\left(\max_{y\in X}r^\top y-r^\top x\right).\] The comparator \(y\) may depend on \(r\), whereas the selected portfolio \(x\) is fixed before \(r\) is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimax-regret portfolio minimizes its largest return shortfall relative to the portfolio that would have been optimal after observing returns.
knowledge_statements.title: Regret-Based Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the minimax-regret leaf and compactness makes the scenario-wise maximum well-defined, but the portfolio-specific regret formulation has no cited source.

children.title: Benchmark Selection Regimes

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty history space is \(U\).
Admissible benchmark portfolios belong to a nonempty set \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed, static-selected, and adaptive regimes differ by whether and when the benchmark may depend on uncertainty.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: information structure distinguishes exogenous, ex-ante selected, and history-adaptive benchmarks
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benchmark regimes classified by decision timing and information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed exogenous regime specifies one benchmark \(b_0\in B\) outside the optimization. A static-selection regime chooses one \(b\in B\) before uncertainty is observed and uses that same benchmark for every \(u\in U\). An adaptive regime chooses a rule \(b:U\to B\), subject to nonanticipativity: whenever two histories agree through time \(t\), their benchmark decisions through time \(t\) must agree. Thus the admissible benchmark classes are respectively \(\{b_0\}\), the constant maps from \(U\) into \(B\), and a specified family of nonanticipative maps. Robust relative-performance or regret criteria must state which class is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benchmark regimes are distinguished by whether the benchmark is exogenous, selected once before uncertainty, or adapted nonanticipatively as information arrives.
knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the classification leaf, but the proposed regime terminology has no source. The statement also mixes a generic history space with decisions indexed by time without defining the time-indexed benchmark policy or filtration.

children.title: Relative-Regret Tradeoffs

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is convex.
The worst-case absolute-loss function \(A\) and worst-case relative-regret function \(R\) are finite and convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every minimizer of \(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)R\) with \(0<\lambda<1\) is weakly Pareto efficient.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive weighted-sum scalarization yields weak Pareto efficiency for convex bicriteria optimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex scalarization of absolute robustness and relative regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)\) measure worst-case absolute loss and let \(R(x)\) measure worst-case relative regret for \(x\in X\). For \(0<\lambda<1\), consider \[\min_{x\in X}\;\lambda A(x)+(1-\lambda)R(x).\] Every minimizer is weakly Pareto efficient for the bicriteria problem \(\min_{x\in X}(A(x),R(x))\): no feasible portfolio can strictly reduce both criteria. If \(X\) is convex and both criteria are convex, every properly supported Pareto-efficient tradeoff is obtained by a nonnegative weighted scalarization. Varying \(\lambda\) therefore traces the supported portion of the absolute-loss versus relative-regret frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted sums generate weakly efficient compromises between worst-case absolute loss and worst-case regret; under convexity they recover supported frontier points.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Regret Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the tradeoff leaf, and the positive-weight scalarization implication is standard. A source is still required, especially for the stronger converse concerning properly supported efficient points and for the exact definition of supported efficiency being used.

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) is nonempty and contains probability laws on \(\mathbb R^n\) satisfying specified moment restrictions.
The feasible portfolio set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The portfolio minimizes worst-case expected loss over all distributions satisfying the moment information.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: moment-based distributional robustness optimizes the worst expectation over laws satisfying moment constraints
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributionally robust portfolio model with first and second moment information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given mean \(\mu\), covariance bound \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_+^n\), and support set \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a moment ambiguity set may be written as \[\mathcal P=\left\{P:P(\xi\in Z)=1,\;\mathbb E_P[\xi]=\mu,\;\mathbb E_P[(\xi-\mu)(\xi-\mu)^\top]\preceq\Sigma\right\}.\] For portfolio weights \(x\in X\) and a measurable loss \(\ell(x,\xi)\) whose expectations are finite, the moment-ambiguous portfolio problem is \[\min_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)].\] Feasibility and performance are thus protected against every return distribution consistent with the specified support and moment information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A moment-ambiguous portfolio minimizes expected loss under the worst return distribution consistent with prescribed support, mean, and covariance information.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Ambiguous Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the distributionally robust portfolio leaf and the ambiguity-set model is coherent, but no authoritative source is cited for this moment-based portfolio formulation.

assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set is a nonempty set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The return vector \(\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n\) has unknown law in \(\mathcal P_\varepsilon:=\{P:W_p(P,\widehat P_N)\leq\varepsilon\}\), where \(p\geq1\).
The loss \(\ell(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected portfolio minimizes its worst-case expected loss over the transport ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wasserstein-ball formulation around an empirical return distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(\widehat\xi_1,\ldots,\widehat\xi_N\) and \(\widehat P_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\widehat\xi_i}\), a transport-ambiguous portfolio is any solution of
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\varepsilon}\mathbb E_P[\ell(x,\xi)],\qquad
\mathcal P_\varepsilon=\{P:W_p(P,\widehat P_N)\leq\varepsilon\}.
\]
The radius \(\varepsilon\geq0\) controls ambiguity: \(\varepsilon=0\) recovers optimization under the empirical law, while larger radii protect against distributions reachable from \(\widehat P_N\) within the prescribed optimal-transport budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transport-ambiguous portfolio minimizes the worst expected loss over all return distributions within a Wasserstein radius of the empirical distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport-Ambiguous Portfolios

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Wasserstein-ball template fits the terminal container, but no citation is supplied and the class of probability measures, transport ground metric, and finite-moment conditions needed for W_p are not specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Tail-Risk Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case CVaR portfolio template for a fixed ambiguity set, without an unjustified minimax interchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distributionally robust tail-risk portfolio solves
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha,P}(L(x,\xi))
=
\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}
\left\{t+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\mathbb E_P[(L(x,\xi)-t)_+]\right\}.
\]
Here \((u)_+=\max\{u,0\}\). Replacing \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}\) by \(\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\) requires additional minimax conditions and is not asserted here.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The portfolio minimizes worst-case CVaR, with the CVaR threshold optimized separately for each distribution; a common threshold requires additional minimax conditions.
assumptions_latex: The feasible portfolio set is a nonempty set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) is a nonempty collection of probability laws for \(\xi\).
The confidence level satisfies \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and \(L(x,\xi)\) is integrable under every \(P\in\mathcal P\) for each \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha,P}(L(x,\xi))=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}\{t+(1-\alpha)^{-1}\mathbb E_P[(L(x,\xi)-t)_+]\}.\)
