assumptions_latex: Candidate facilities and demand nodes form finite sets \(I\) and \(J\).
Demand vectors belong to a nonempty uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R_+^{|J|}\).
Recourse flow is selected after demand is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A design is robustly feasible exactly when every \(d\in U\) admits flows satisfying demand and installed-capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage feasibility condition with uncertain customer demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For facility capacities \(u_i\geq0\), an opening vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^{|I|}\) is demand-robust if
\[
\forall d\in U\ \exists q(d)\geq0:\quad
\sum_{i\in I}q_{ij}(d)\geq d_j\ \ (j\in J),\qquad
\sum_{j\in J}q_{ij}(d)\leq u_i y_i\ \ (i\in I).
\]
A demand-robust network-design model minimizes first-stage design cost, optionally plus the worst recourse cost, over opening vectors satisfying this quantified condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Installed facilities must support feasible demand-dependent shipments for every demand vector in the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.title: Demand-Robust Network Design

assumptions_latex: Candidate facilities and customers form finite sets \(I\) and \(J\).
Available-capacity vectors belong to a nonempty set \(U_c\subseteq\mathbb R_+^{|I|}\).
Customer demands \(d_j\geq0\) are fixed, while flows adapt to realized capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility requires feasible shipments for every capacity vector in \(U_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjustable-flow feasibility under uncertain facility capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An opening vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^{|I|}\) is capacity-robust when
\[
\forall c\in U_c\ \exists q(c)\geq0:\quad
\sum_{i\in I}q_{ij}(c)\geq d_j\ \ (j\in J),\qquad
\sum_{j\in J}q_{ij}(c)\leq c_i y_i\ \ (i\in I).
\]
Thus capacity uncertainty enters the supply constraints, while shipment flows are recourse decisions. A robust design minimizes its prescribed design and operating objective over all opening vectors satisfying these constraints for every \(c\in U_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The installed network must meet fixed demand through adaptive shipments under every admissible capacity realization.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Robust Network Design

assumptions_latex: Candidate facilities and customers form finite sets \(I\) and \(J\).
Each disruption scenario \(s\in S\) specifies availability indicators \(a_i^s\in\{0,1\}\).
Shipment flows may adapt after the disruption scenario is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The design survives all modeled disruptions exactly when each scenario admits flows through its available opened facilities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario survivability with adaptive post-disruption flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given capacities \(u_i\) and demands \(d_j\), an opening vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^{|I|}\) is disruption-robust if
\[
\forall s\in S\ \exists q^s\geq0:\quad
\sum_{i\in I}q_{ij}^s\geq d_j\ \ (j\in J),\qquad
\sum_{j\in J}q_{ij}^s\leq u_i a_i^s y_i\ \ (i\in I).
\]
Because \(a_i^s=0\) suppresses all flow from a disrupted facility, this condition certifies service feasibility under every disruption pattern represented in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every modeled disruption must leave enough opened, available capacity for adaptive flows to satisfy all customer demands.
knowledge_statements.title: Disruption-Robust Network Design

assumptions_latex: Uncertainty \(\xi\) ranges over a nonempty set \(U\).
The first-stage design belongs to \(Y\), and the recourse set \(Q(y,\xi)\) is defined for each \((y,\xi)\).
Recourse decisions are chosen after observing \(\xi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adaptive design minimizes first-stage cost plus worst-case optimal recourse cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage adjustable robust supply-chain design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An adaptive robust supply-chain design is represented by
\[
\inf_{y\in Y}\left\{c^\top y+\sup_{\xi\in U}\ \inf_{q\in Q(y,\xi)}g(q,\xi)\right\},
\]
with the convention that \(\inf_{q\in\varnothing}g(q,\xi)=+\infty\). Equivalently, finite robust value requires \(Q(y,\xi)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(\xi\in U\). The quantifier order \(\inf_y\sup_\xi\inf_q\) distinguishes irreversible design decisions from operating decisions that adapt to observed demand, capacity, or disruption data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed network design is chosen before uncertainty, while operating decisions adapt afterward to minimize the worst realized recourse cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Supply-Chain Design

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage robust representation is plausible, but the cited generic robust-optimization section does not inspectably support this supply-chain specialization, and the dimensions and domains of c and g are not introduced.

children.title: Robust Inventory Control
children.top_down_role: Inventory policies under uncertain demand, supply, or lead times.

assumptions_latex: The horizon is \(t=1,\ldots,T\), with initial inventory \(I_0\).
Demand paths belong to a nonempty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R_+^T\).
Order \(q_t\) is nonanticipative: it depends only on demand observed before period \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy minimizes worst-case holding, shortage, and ordering cost while satisfying inventory balance on every demand path.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon robust inventory control with backlogging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With inventory balance
\[
I_t(d)=I_{t-1}(d)+q_t(d_1,\ldots,d_{t-1})-d_t,
\]
a robust inventory policy solves
\[
\inf_{q\ \mathrm{nonanticipative}}\ \sup_{d\in U}\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(c_tq_t+h_t[I_t(d)]_++p_t[-I_t(d)]_+\bigr),
\]
subject to prescribed order bounds. Here \(h_t,p_t\geq0\), and negative inventory represents backlog. Nonanticipativity prevents period-\(t\) orders from using current or future demand before it is revealed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonanticipative ordering policy balances inventory and minimizes worst-case ordering, holding, and backlog cost over all admissible demand paths.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Inventory Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust inventory template fits the leaf, but the cited generic section does not inspectably support this application-specific model. The admissible order-policy class, order bounds, and ordering-cost coefficients are not fully specified.

children.title: Robust Lot-Sizing Models
children.top_down_role: Production-lot decisions under uncertain requirements or capacity.

assumptions_latex: Demand paths lie in a nonempty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R_+^T\).
Production quantities satisfy \(0\leq q_t\leq M_ty_t\), where \(y_t\in\{0,1\}\).
Production decisions use only demand information available when they are made.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model chooses setup and production policies minimizing total cost under the worst admissible demand path.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic robust lot sizing with setup decisions and backlogging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A robust lot-sizing model has the form
\[
\inf_{y,q\ \mathrm{nonanticipative}}\ \sup_{d\in U}\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(K_ty_t+c_tq_t+h_t[I_t(d)]_++p_t[-I_t(d)]_+\bigr),
\]
subject to
\[
I_t(d)=I_{t-1}(d)+q_t-d_t,\qquad 0\leq q_t\leq M_ty_t,
\]
for every \(d\in U\). The binary variable \(y_t\) incurs the setup cost \(K_t\) and activates production capacity \(M_t\) in period \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust lot sizing combines binary setups, production, and inventory balance while minimizing cost under the worst admissible demand path.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Lot-Sizing Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed lot-sizing model is plausible, but the cited sections do not inspectably establish the robust dynamic formulation. The history dependence of q_t and y_t is suppressed in the constraints, and several cost and capacity parameters lack explicit domains.

children.title: Inventory–Lot-Sizing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Joint planning regimes linking replenishment states with production lots.

assumptions_latex: The planning horizon is finite and demand paths belong to \(U\).
Inventory obeys material balance, and production is activated by binary setup decisions.
All adjustable decisions satisfy the specified information structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling is enforced jointly by inventory balance and setup-linked production bounds for every demand realization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-level coupling of inventory dynamics and lot activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Inventory and lot sizing are coupled on every demand path \(d\in U\) by
\[
I_t(d)=I_{t-1}(d)+q_t(d)-d_t,
\qquad 0\leq q_t(d)\leq M_ty_t(d),
\qquad y_t(d)\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The first equality propagates replenishment into the inventory state; the second makes positive replenishment contingent on a setup. Robust feasibility requires these relations for all \(d\in U\), together with nonanticipativity whenever \(q_t\) or \(y_t\) is adjustable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inventory balance propagates each replenishment lot, while setup-linked bounds determine when positive replenishment is permitted on every demand path.
knowledge_statements.title: Inventory–Lot-Sizing Coupling

children.title: Service–Cost Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Robust operating regimes balancing protection, shortage exposure, plus holding cost.

assumptions_latex: Policies belong to a common feasible class \(\Pi\).
For each \(\pi\in\Pi\), worst-case cost \(C(\pi)\) and worst-case service shortfall \(S(\pi)\) are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weighted-penalty and service-constrained formulations describe supported service-cost regimes, with larger penalties weakly discouraging shortfall.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto tradeoff between robust cost and worst-case service shortfall.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda\geq0\), define
\[
V(\lambda)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\{C(\pi)+\lambda S(\pi)\}.
\]
If \(\pi_1\) and \(\pi_2\) are optimal at \(0\leq\lambda_1<\lambda_2\), respectively, then \(S(\pi_2)\leq S(\pi_1)\) and \(C(\pi_2)\geq C(\pi_1)\). Alternatively, a service regime with tolerance \(\tau\geq0\) is obtained from \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\{C(\pi):S(\pi)\leq\tau\}\). Thus penalty and constraint parameters trace supported robust service-cost compromises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the service-shortfall penalty weakly improves worst-case service while weakly increasing the unpenalized cost of an optimal policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Service–Cost Tradeoff Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonic service-shortfall and unpenalized-cost conclusions follow from the stated optimality assumptions and fit the property container, but this nontrivial scalarization claim has no citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust scheduling under uncertain processing data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A static robust scheduling problem is
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{\xi\in U}f(x,\xi).
\]
The schedule \(x\) fixes the required assignment and sequencing decisions before \(\xi\) is known. Any precedence, machine-capacity, release-date, or deadline constraint containing uncertain data must hold for every \(\xi\in U\). Thus a robustly feasible schedule remains feasible throughout \(U\), and the objective minimizes its worst-case performance value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust schedule fixes assignment and sequencing decisions that remain feasible and minimize worst-case performance over every admissible processing-data realization.
assumptions_latex: Jobs form a finite set \(J\), and feasible schedules belong to a nonempty set \(X\).
Uncertain processing data \(\xi\) range over a nonempty set \(U\).
The performance measure \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\sup_{\xi\in U}f(x,\xi)\) minimizes worst-case scheduling performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Facility Location
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated robust facility location with adjustable assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A capacitated robust facility-location model is
\[
\inf_{y\in\{0,1\}^{|I|}}\left\{\sum_{i\in I}F_i y_i+
\sup_{d\in U}\inf_{q\in Q(y,d)}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}c_{ij}q_{ij}\right\},
\]
where
\[
Q(y,d)=\left\{q\in\mathbb R_+^{|I|\times|J|}:\sum_{i\in I}q_{ij}\geq d_j\ \text{for every }j\in J,\quad \sum_{j\in J}q_{ij}\leq u_i y_i\ \text{for every }i\in I\right\}.
\]
The inner value is defined as \(+\infty\) when \(Q(y,d)=\varnothing\). Consequently, every finite-valued solution admits capacity-feasible assignments for each \(d\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facilities are opened before demand is known, and demand-dependent assignments must serve every admissible demand vector within installed capacities.
assumptions_latex: Candidate sites and customers form finite sets \(I\) and \(J\).
Demand vectors range over a nonempty uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R_+^{|J|}\).
Opening costs satisfy \(F_i\in\mathbb R\), capacities satisfy \(u_i\geq0\), and assignment costs satisfy \(c_{ij}\in\mathbb R\) for \(i\in I\) and \(j\in J\).
Facility openings are selected before demand is observed, while assignments may depend on the realized demand vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite-valued solution \(y\) satisfies \(Q(y,d)\neq\varnothing\) for all \(d\in U\).

notation.meaning: Demand-dependent assignment quantity from site i to customer j
Feasible assignment set for design y and demand d

children.title: Robust Transportation Models
children.top_down_role: Flow allocation across networks with uncertain supply, demand, capacity, or cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Transportation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage capacitated transportation with uncertain supplies and demands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let directed network \(G=(V,E)\) have capacity decisions \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\), costs \(c\), and uncertain net demands \(d\in\mathcal U\subseteq\{d:\mathbf 1^\top d=0\}\). A robust transportation model is
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c^\top x+\max_{d\in\mathcal U}\min_{f\in\mathbb R_+^E}\left\{q^\top f:Bf=d,\ 0\le f\le x\right\}\right\}.\]
A capacity vector is robustly feasible precisely when the inner flow-feasibility set is nonempty for every \(d\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose capacities before demand is known, then route flow at minimum cost for each demand realization while satisfying conservation and capacity constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite directed network with node-arc incidence matrix \(B\).
\(\mathcal U\) is nonempty and contains only balanced demand vectors.
All capacity and flow costs are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible if and only if \(\forall d\in\mathcal U\;\exists f\ge0:Bf=d,\ f\le x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the transportation-model leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the cited general robust-optimization section does not establish this application-specific two-stage network formulation. The role of q is not explicitly introduced, and the objective needs a convention for scenarios with no feasible recourse. A transportation or robust-network source with a precise model locator is required.

children.title: Robust Routing Models
children.top_down_role: Route design under uncertain travel, service, or demand conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Routing Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static route selection under uncertain arc costs and availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(\mathcal R\subseteq\{0,1\}^E\) encode admissible routes, and let \((c,a)\in\mathcal U\) denote arc costs and binary availability. A static robust routing problem is
\[\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \max_{(c,a)\in\mathcal U}c^\top r\quad\text{subject to}\quad r_e\le a_e\ \text{for every }e\in E\text{ and every }(c,a)\in\mathcal U.\]
Thus a selected route must remain available in every admitted disruption scenario, and its objective value is its worst-case traversal cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select one admissible route that survives every modeled disruption and minimizes its largest possible traversal cost.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and \(\mathcal R\) correctly encodes the required path or tour constraints.
\(\mathcal U\) is a nonempty set of finite cost and availability scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimizer minimizes \(\sup_{(c,a)\in\mathcal U}c^\top r\) over routes satisfying \(r\le a\) throughout \(\mathcal U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The static robust-routing representation and content kind fit the leaf, but the cited general robust-optimization section does not support the specific route-availability formulation. An inspectable robust-routing source is required to confirm the uncertainty model and static information pattern.

children.title: Integrated Transport–Route Planning
children.top_down_role: Joint network-allocation and route-design regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Transport–Route Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint first-stage network planning and adaptive routing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) choose transportation assets, and let scenario \(u\in\mathcal U\) determine demands, costs, and available arcs. If \(Y(x,u)\) is the set of routes and flows satisfying scenario-wise service, conservation, availability, and installed-capacity constraints, integrated robust planning has the form
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{C(x)+\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\min_{y\in Y(x,u)}Q(y,u)\right\}.\]
It is robustly feasible when \(Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\); routing decisions may adapt to \(u\), whereas \(x\) may not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plan transportation assets before uncertainty, then adapt routes and flows after each scenario while guaranteeing service under every admitted realization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the nonempty set of admissible first-stage plans.
\(\mathcal U\) is nonempty and all recourse costs are well-defined.
The information pattern permits \(y\) to depend on \(u\), but not \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to \(\forall u\in\mathcal U,\ Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible recourse set under scenario u.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage representation fits integrated transport-route planning, and the first-stage/recourse distinction is clear. However, the generic citation does not support the integrated application model, and the displayed max-min objective does not state how empty recourse sets are valued. A model-specific source is needed.

children.title: Network Disruption Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transportation or routing templates exposed to arc, node, or capacity disruptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Disruption Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted simultaneous failures of network components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For components \(E\), nominal availability \(\bar a_e=1\), and disruption budget \(\Gamma\in\{0,\ldots,|E|\}\), the cardinality-bounded disruption regime is
\[\mathcal U_\Gamma=\left\{a\in\{0,1\}^E:\sum_{e\in E}(1-a_e)\le\Gamma\right\}.\]
A network decision \(x\) is feasible in this regime exactly when its operational constraints are satisfiable for every \(a\in\mathcal U_\Gamma\). The cases \(\Gamma=0\) and \(\Gamma=|E|\) respectively represent no admitted failures and unrestricted simultaneous component failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most Γ components may fail simultaneously; robust feasibility requires operability under every failure pattern within that budget.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite component set.
Each component is modeled as either available or failed.
\(\Gamma\) is an integer between \(0\) and \(|E|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible if and only if its operational feasibility predicate holds for every \(a\in\mathcal U_\Gamma\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly describes a cardinality-bounded binary disruption regime and fits the terminal container. The cited general robust-optimization section does not support this particular uncertainty set or its network interpretation; a specific disruption or network-interdiction locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case compliance-constrained structural sizing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) be structural sizes, \(K(x)\) the stiffness matrix, and \(\mathcal F\) a prescribed set of loads. A robust minimum-weight design can be written
\[\min_{x\in X}w^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad K(x)u=f,\quad f^\top u\le\bar C\quad\text{for every }f\in\mathcal F.\]
Equivalently, whenever \(K(x)\) is positive definite, the robust compliance constraint is \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}f^\top K(x)^{-1}f\le\bar C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize structural weight while bounding compliance for every allowed load, using the equilibrium displacement induced by each load.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) enforces physically admissible positive member sizes.
\(K(x)\) is symmetric positive definite for every \(x\in X\).
\(\mathcal F\) is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}f^\top K(x)^{-1}f\le\bar C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A robust compliance representation fits Structural Design, but the cited source is not a structural-optimization reference. In the first formulation, displacement u must be explicitly scenario-dependent or existentially quantified for each load f. A structural robust-optimization source is required before selecting the exact corrected formulation.

children.title: Robust Linear Estimation
children.top_down_role: Linear estimators exposed to uncertain operators, noise, or covariance structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Linear Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax linear estimation with bounded measurement uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose measurements satisfy \(y=(A+\Delta)x+n\), with signal \(x\in\mathcal X\), operator perturbation \(\Delta\in\mathcal D\), and noise \(n\in\mathcal N\). For a linear estimator \(\widehat x=Hy\), the robust design problem is
\[\min_{H\in\mathcal H}\ \sup_{x\in\mathcal X,\,\Delta\in\mathcal D,\,n\in\mathcal N}\left\|H\bigl((A+\Delta)x+n\bigr)-x\right\|.\]
Its objective is the largest estimation error over the prescribed signal, mismatch, and noise sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a linear estimator whose largest error over all allowed signals, operator perturbations, and noise vectors is minimal.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\), \(\mathcal D\), and \(\mathcal N\) are nonempty bounded sets.
\(\mathcal H\) is a nonempty class of dimensionally compatible linear maps.
The displayed norm is fixed before optimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal \(H\) minimizes the worst-case error \(\sup_{x,\Delta,n}\|H((A+\Delta)x+n)-x\|\).

notation.meaning: Signal, mismatch, and noise uncertainty sets.

source_refs.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
source_refs.locator: 3 Applications in Signal Processing, Communications, and Adaptive Control p. 63

source_witnesses.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
source_witnesses.locator: 3 Applications in Signal Processing, Communications, and Adaptive Control p. 63

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimax representation fits Robust Linear Estimation, but the cited signal-processing chapter does not specifically support the displayed robust estimator design. The dimensions and spaces of y, A, x, n, and Delta are not explicitly introduced. An exact minimax-estimation locator is required.

children.title: Robust Signal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Signal reconstruction under measurement uncertainty, corruption, or model mismatch.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Signal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized recovery under norm-bounded operator mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), nominal operator \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), perturbation set \(\mathcal D\), regularizer \(R\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), robust signal recovery solves
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\sup_{\Delta\in\mathcal D}\left\|(A+\Delta)x-y\right\|+\lambda R(x)\right\}.\]
The recovered signal trades structural regularity against the largest residual generated by any admissible measurement-operator perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover a structured signal by minimizing regularization plus the worst residual over all admitted perturbations of the measurement operator.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\) is nonempty and bounded.
\(R:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper.
The residual norm and \(\lambda\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any minimizer is a robust recovered signal for the uncertainty set \(\mathcal D\).

notation.meaning: Nominal measurement operator and its perturbation.

source_refs.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
source_refs.locator: 3 Applications in Signal Processing, Communications, and Adaptive Control p. 63

source_witnesses.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
source_witnesses.locator: 3 Applications in Signal Processing, Communications, and Adaptive Control p. 63

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Robust Signal Recovery, but the cited broad applications chapter does not support this exact operator-uncertainty formulation. Properness of R and boundedness of the perturbation set do not ensure that a minimizer exists, so the conclusion is only conditional. A robust-recovery source is required to settle the intended assumptions and formulation.

children.title: Estimator–Recovery Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural overlap between robust estimation and reconstruction formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Estimator–Recovery Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean operator uncertainty induces norm regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\rho\ge0\), let \(\mathcal D_\rho=\{\Delta\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\|\Delta\|_2\le\rho\}\), where the matrix norm is spectral. Then
\[\max_{\Delta\in\mathcal D_\rho}\left\|(A+\Delta)x-b\right\|_2=\|Ax-b\|_2+\rho\|x\|_2.\]
Consequently, minimizing the worst-case residual over \(x\) is exactly equivalent to minimizing the nominal residual plus the induced Euclidean regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral-norm operator uncertainty converts worst-case least-squares residual minimization exactly into residual minimization with an added Euclidean norm penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(b\), and \(x\) are finite-dimensional real arrays of compatible dimensions.
The perturbation radius satisfies \(\rho\ge0\).
Both vector norms are Euclidean and the matrix norm is spectral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\max_{\|\Delta\|_2\le\rho}\|(A+\Delta)x-b\|_2=\min_x\{\|Ax-b\|_2+\rho\|x\|_2\}\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean vector norm or spectral matrix norm, by argument.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-norm identity is mathematically plausible and the representation fits the correspondence leaf, but no citation is supplied for this nontrivial exact equivalence. An authoritative theorem, proposition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Measurement-Mismatch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Inference regimes shaped by sensing-operator errors or misspecified noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Measurement-Mismatch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined additive-noise and operator-mismatch uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nominal measurements \(y=Ax\), define the bounded mismatch regime
\[\mathcal U_{\rho,\eta}=\left\{(\Delta,n):\|\Delta\|_2\le\rho,\ \|n\|_2\le\eta\right\}.\]
For fixed \(x\) and residual \(r=Ax-y\), its worst-case measurement discrepancy is
\[\sup_{(\Delta,n)\in\mathcal U_{\rho,\eta}}\|r+\Delta x+n\|_2=\|r\|_2+\rho\|x\|_2+\eta.\]
The regimes \(\rho=0\) and \(\eta=0\) isolate additive noise and operator mismatch, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded operator error and additive noise enlarge the nominal residual by the operator radius times signal norm plus the noise radius.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional and use Euclidean norms.
The matrix norm on \(\Delta\) is spectral.
The radii satisfy \(\rho,\eta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case discrepancy equals \(\|Ax-y\|_2+\rho\|x\|_2+\eta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the mismatch-regime leaf, but no source supports the exact worst-case identity. The phrase 'nominal measurements y=Ax' forces the subsequently defined residual r=Ax-y to zero; the intended setup should instead introduce y as an observed vector unless a zero nominal residual is deliberate. A source is needed before fixing the precise model.

knowledge_statements.title: Control Synthesis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-quadratic robust state-feedback synthesis for polytopic systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(x_{t+1}=A_i x_t+B_i u_t\) at each vertex \(i=1,\ldots,N\). If there exist \(Q=Q^\top\succ0\) and \(Y\) satisfying
\[\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_iQ+B_iY\\(A_iQ+B_iY)^\top&Q\end{bmatrix}\succ0\quad\text{for every }i,\]
then \(K=YQ^{-1}\) robustly stabilizes every convex combination of the vertex systems under \(u_t=Kx_t\). The matrix \(P=Q^{-1}\) supplies the common quadratic Lyapunov function \(V(x)=x^\top Px\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible vertex LMIs certify a state-feedback gain that quadratically stabilizes every system in a polytopic uncertainty family.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain pair \((A,B)\) belongs to the convex hull of finitely many vertices \((A_i,B_i)\).
Full-state feedback \(u_t=Kx_t\) is available.
The system is discrete-time and time invariant within each admissible realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=YQ^{-1}\) makes every admissible closed-loop matrix Schur stable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind is appropriate for this sufficient common-quadratic stabilization condition, and the discrete-time vertex LMI is internally coherent. Because no source is supplied for the nontrivial LMI implication and convex-hull guarantee, an authoritative robust-control theorem locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trajectory Equivalence and Bi-Affinity of Two Affine Control-Law Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The two affine control-law parameterizations specified by equations (14.45) and (14.51.d) for closed-loop system (14.51).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every affine control law of form (14.45), there exists a control law of form (14.51.d) that produces exactly the same closed-loop state-control trajectories for every initial state and every input sequence, and conversely. Furthermore, if \(\eta=\{h_t,H_{t\tau}\}_{0\leq \tau\leq t\leq N}\), then
\[
w^N=\omega[\eta]+\Omega_z[\eta]z+\Omega_d[\eta]d^N,
\]
for vectors \(\omega[\eta]\) and matrices \(\Omega_z[\eta],\Omega_d[\eta]\) depending affinely on \(\eta\). Thus \(w^N\) is affine in \((z,d^N)\) for fixed \(\eta\), and affine in \(\eta\) for fixed \((z,d^N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine control-law forms in equations (14.45) and (14.51.d) can represent one another without changing any closed-loop state-control trajectory, for any initial state and input sequence. The trajectory is affine in the initial state and inputs when the controller parameters are fixed, and affine in those parameters when the initial state and inputs are fixed.
assumptions_latex: \text{The closed-loop system and affine control-law forms are those specified in (14.51), (14.45), and (14.51.d).}
\eta=\{h_t,H_{t\tau}\}_{0\leq \tau\leq t\leq N}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The two affine control-law forms are trajectory-equivalent in both directions, and }w^N=\omega[\eta]+\Omega_z[\eta]z+\Omega_d[\eta]d^N\text{ with coefficient maps affine in }\eta.

children.title: Robust Energy-System Planning
children.top_down_role: Capacity, infrastructure, or investment planning under energy-system uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Energy-System Planning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage capacity expansion with robust operational recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) denote generation, storage, and transmission investments, and let \(u\in\mathcal U\) describe uncertain demand and renewable availability. If \(Y(x,u)\) contains dispatches satisfying balance, capacity, ramping, storage, and network constraints, robust energy planning is
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{C^\top x+\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\min_{y\in Y(x,u)}q(u)^\top y\right\}.\]
A plan is robustly adequate exactly when \(Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\) for every admitted realization \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose energy infrastructure before uncertainty and guarantee a feasible operating schedule for every modeled demand and renewable realization.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set of admissible investments.
\(\mathcal U\) is a nonempty uncertainty set for demand and renewable availability.
Operational decisions may adapt to the realized \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust adequacy is equivalent to \(\forall u\in\mathcal U,\ Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-stage representation fits robust energy-system planning, but the general robust-optimization citation does not substantiate the listed energy constraints or adequacy interpretation. The objective also needs a convention for empty recourse sets. A robust capacity-expansion or energy-planning source is required.

children.title: Robust Energy-System Operations
children.top_down_role: Dispatch, commitment, storage, or reserve decisions under operational uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Energy-System Operations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case dispatch with uncertain net demand and availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u\in\mathcal U\) specify net demands, renewable injections, and component availabilities. With dispatch vector \(y\), operating cost \(q(u)^\top y\), and feasible set \(Y(u)\) encoding nodal balance, available capacity, ramping, storage dynamics, and network limits, robust operation is
\[\min_{\pi}\ \max_{u\in\mathcal U}q(u)^\top\pi(u)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \pi(u)\in Y(u)\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\]
The policy \(\pi\) must obey the specified information pattern, so each action uses only uncertainty revealed by that time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an information-feasible dispatch policy that operates the energy system feasibly in every scenario and minimizes worst-case operating cost.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is nonempty and all operational data are finite.
\(Y(u)\) represents the complete physical operating constraints.
Policies are restricted to the stated uncertainty-revelation pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal \(\pi\) minimizes worst-case cost among policies satisfying \(\pi(u)\in Y(u)\) for every \(u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjustable-policy representation fits robust energy-system operations, but the cited general section does not support this application-specific model. The statement invokes a temporal information pattern while u and Y(u) are written as whole-scenario objects, so the admissible policy class and nonanticipativity domains require precise specification from a suitable source.

children.title: Planning–Operations Coordination
children.top_down_role: Cross-horizon coupling between infrastructure choices and operational recourse.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\) is the set of admissible planning decisions.
For each uncertainty realization \(u\in\mathcal U\), \(Y(x,u)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}\) is the set of feasible operational responses.
\(C(x)\) and \(Q(x,y,u)\) are extended-real planning and operating costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{C(x)+\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\inf_{y\in Y(x,u)}Q(x,y,u)\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: operational recourse decision after uncertainty is observed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage robust coordination with here-and-now planning and wait-and-see operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Planning–operations coordination is represented by the robust two-stage problem
\[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{C(x)+\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\inf_{y\in Y(x,u)}Q(x,y,u)\right\}.\]
A planning decision \(x\) is robustly operable precisely when \(Y(x,u)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). Thus planning selects capacity or infrastructure before uncertainty, while operations adapt to the realized uncertainty subject to the capabilities installed by \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Planning minimizes investment plus worst-case optimized operating cost, while requiring an admissible operating response for every modeled uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.title: Planning–Operations Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent and fits the planning–operations interface, but it has no citation supporting its energy-system interpretation or the exact two-stage template.

children.title: Renewable-Variability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Energy models shaped by renewable generation, demand, or price variability.

assumptions_latex: \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_T)\in\mathbb{R}^{T}\) denotes renewable availability over a finite horizon.
Nominal availability \(\bar r\in\mathbb{R}^{T}\), scales \(d_t>0\), and budget \(\Gamma\in[0,T]\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal U_{\Gamma}=\left\{r:\ r_t=\bar r_t+d_tz_t,\ |z_t|\leq1,\ \sum_{t=1}^{T}|z_t|\leq\Gamma\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted trajectory regimes for bounded renewable deviations over a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A budgeted renewable-variability regime is the uncertainty set
\[\mathcal U_{\Gamma}=\left\{r\in\mathbb{R}^{T}: r_t=\bar r_t+d_tz_t,\ |z_t|\leq1,\ \sum_{t=1}^{T}|z_t|\leq\Gamma\right\}.\]
Here \(\Gamma=0\) gives the nominal regime, increasing \(\Gamma\) admits more simultaneous or sustained deviations, and \(\Gamma=T\) gives the full componentwise box. Operational constraints are required to hold for every trajectory \(r\in\mathcal U_{\Gamma}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variability regime bounds each renewable deviation and limits their aggregate magnitude through a budget parameter ranging from nominal to full-box uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.title: Renewable-Variability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The budgeted set is internally correct, including the endpoint regimes, but it is only one modeling choice under the broader plural title and lacks a renewable-energy uncertainty source.

children.title: Robust Model Failure-Diagnostic Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Modeling, statistical, dynamic, and computational boundaries used to diagnose inappropriate robustness claims.

assumptions_latex: For each uncertainty set \(U\), define \(v(U)=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x):g(x,u)\leq0\ \forall u\in U\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
The modeled set \(U_m\) strictly contains a smaller credible set \(U_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[U_c\subseteq U_m\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(U_m)\subseteq F(U_c),\qquad v(U_m)\geq v(U_c).\]

notation.meaning: robust feasible region for uncertainty set U

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion diagnostic for conservatism in robust minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(U)=\{x\in X:g(x,u)\leq0\text{ for all }u\in U\}\). If the modeled uncertainty set is oversized, so that \(U_c\subsetneq U_m\), then
\[F(U_m)\subseteq F(U_c),\qquad v(U_m)\geq v(U_c).\]
The enlargement can therefore exclude decisions feasible for every credible realization and can increase the robust cost; it may also create \(F(U_m)=\varnothing\) even when \(F(U_c)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging an uncertainty set can only shrink the robust feasible region and worsen a minimization value, potentially causing artificial infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Uncertainty Sets

assumptions_latex: The true uncertainty satisfies \(u=(u_1,u_2)=(t,t)\) with \(|t|\leq1\).
The modeled set is the marginal box \(U_m=[-1,1]^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete overconservatism caused by replacing perfect dependence with a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[U_c=\{(t,t):|t|\leq1\},\qquad U_m=[-1,1]^2.\]
Both coordinates have the same marginal range under either description, but \(U_m\) ignores their perfect positive dependence. For the uncertain expression \(h(u)=u_1-u_2\),
\[\sup_{u\in U_c}h(u)=0,\qquad \sup_{u\in U_m}h(u)=2.\]
Thus enforcing \(h(u)\leq b\) over the product set requires \(b\geq2\), whereas the dependence-aware model requires only \(b\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing perfectly dependent uncertainties by their marginal box creates impossible joint realizations and can strictly inflate a robust constraint bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Ignored Dependence Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and its extrema are correct and directly illustrate conservatism from ignoring dependence, but no inspectable source is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(U\neq\varnothing\) is an uncertainty set.
\(Y(x,u)\) is the feasible second-stage action set.
Static policies use one action \(y\), while adaptive policies may choose a mapping \(\pi:U\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_{\mathrm{stat}}\subseteq F_{\mathrm{ad}},\qquad v_{\mathrm{ad}}\leq v_{\mathrm{stat}}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and value gap between static and fully adjustable recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\{x:\exists y\ \forall u\in U,\ y\in Y(x,u)\}\]
and
\[F_{\mathrm{ad}}=\{x:\exists\pi\ \forall u\in U,\ \pi(u)\in Y(x,u)\}.\]
Every static action induces the constant policy \(\pi(u)=y\), hence \(F_{\mathrm{stat}}\subseteq F_{\mathrm{ad}}\). For minimization with the same robust objective, \(v_{\mathrm{ad}}\leq v_{\mathrm{stat}}\). Strict inclusion or inequality measures conservatism caused solely by forbidding adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static recourse is a special case of adaptive recourse, so it can only reduce feasibility and worsen a robust minimization value.
knowledge_statements.title: Static-Policy Conservatism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-set inclusion is correct, but the values v_ad and v_stat and the shared robust objective are not defined precisely. An adjustable-robust-optimization source is also required before the value comparison can be reviewed reliably.

assumptions_latex: The robust decision \(x_m\) satisfies \(g(x_m,u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U_m\).
The true admissible set \(U_t\) contains at least one point outside \(U_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[U_t\nsubseteq U_m\quad\text{and}\quad \exists u^{\star}\in U_t\setminus U_m:\ g(x_m,u^{\star})>0\ \Longrightarrow\ x_m\notin F(U_t).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic set-coverage boundary for out-of-set constraint violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Robust feasibility over \(U_m\) certifies only
\[g(x_m,u)\leq0\quad\text{for every }u\in U_m.\]
If \(U_t\nsubseteq U_m\), this certificate does not extend to \(U_t\). In particular, if some \(u^{\star}\in U_t\setminus U_m\) satisfies \(g(x_m,u^{\star})>0\), then \(x_m\notin F(U_t)\). An uncertainty set is operationally undersized whenever such an omitted realization invalidates its robust solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust guarantee stops at the modeled set; an omitted true realization that violates a constraint exposes underprotection.
knowledge_statements.title: Undersized Uncertainty Sets

assumptions_latex: The model assumes that uncertainty lies in a support set \(S_m\).
The true law \(P_t\) assigns positive probability outside \(S_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_t(S_m^{c})>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P_t\bigl(g(x,\xi)>0\bigr)\geq P_t\bigl(\{\xi\notin S_m:g(x,\xi)>0\}\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Out-of-support failure of deterministic or distributional robustness guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a guarantee is established only for \(\xi\in S_m\). Support misspecification occurs when
\[P_t(S_m^{c})>0.\]
The guarantee then gives no restriction on \(g(x,\xi)\) over \(S_m^{c}\). Consequently,
\[P_t\bigl(g(x,\xi)>0\bigr)\geq P_t\bigl(\{\xi\notin S_m:g(x,\xi)>0\}\bigr).\]
Thus positive out-of-support mass can produce positive violation probability even when \(g(x,\xi)\leq0\) holds throughout the modeled support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the true distribution places mass outside the modeled support, constraints guaranteed only on that support may fail with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Misspecification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability inequality is correct and the statement appropriately says failure may occur rather than must occur, but no source supports the support-misspecification interpretation.

children.title: Distribution Shift Beyond the Ambiguity Set

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_m\) is the modeled ambiguity set of probability laws.
A decision \(x_m\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_m}E_P[\ell(x_m,\xi)]\leq\tau\).
The deployment law is \(P_t\notin\mathcal P_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_t\notin\mathcal P_m\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E_{P_t}[\ell(x_m,\xi)]\leq\tau\ \text{is not certified}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of a distributionally robust expectation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A distributionally robust bound
\[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_m}E_P[\ell(x_m,\xi)]\leq\tau\]
certifies the threshold only for laws in \(\mathcal P_m\). If the deployment law satisfies \(P_t\notin\mathcal P_m\), the implication \(E_{P_t}[\ell(x_m,\xi)]\leq\tau\) is unavailable. Indeed, any such \(P_t\) with \(E_{P_t}[\ell(x_m,\xi)]>\tau\) is a concrete failure witness for shift beyond the ambiguity set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributionally robust bound applies only inside its ambiguity set; an outside deployment law may exceed the certified loss threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Distribution Shift Beyond the Ambiguity Set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical boundary of the distributionally robust certificate is stated correctly, but the record has no authoritative distributionally robust optimization citation.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the deterministic decision domain.
\(U\neq\varnothing\) is the uncertainty set.
\(g:X\times U\to\mathbb{R}^{p}\) is interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_U=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall x\in X\ \exists u\in U\ \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(x,u)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantified definition for finite-dimensional inequality-constrained robust feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 1.7.1 The Feasible Set and Solvability p. 54

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The robust feasible region is
\[F_U=\{x\in X:g_i(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U\text{ and }i=1,\ldots,p\}.\]
It is empty precisely when no decision satisfies all uncertain constraints, equivalently,
\[F_U=\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall x\in X\ \exists u\in U\ \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(x,u)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust feasible region is empty exactly when every candidate decision is defeated by some uncertainty realization and some violated constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Robust Feasible Region

source_witnesses.locator: 1.7.1 The Feasible Set and Solvability p. 54

assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\) is fixed before uncertainty is observed.
For each \(u\in U\), \(Y(x,u)\) is the admissible recourse set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\ \text{has robust recourse}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall u\in U,\ Y(x,u)\neq\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete-recourse condition over a deterministic uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A first-stage decision \(x\) has robust recourse over \(U\) if and only if
\[\forall u\in U,\quad Y(x,u)\neq\varnothing.\]
It lacks robust recourse if
\[\exists u^{\star}\in U\quad\text{such that}\quad Y(x,u^{\star})=\varnothing.\]
The witness \(u^{\star}\) shows that no admissible second-stage response can repair \(x\) after that realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-stage decision lacks robust recourse when at least one modeled realization admits no feasible second-stage response.
knowledge_statements.title: Lack of Robust Recourse

assumptions_latex: Individual uncertainty coordinates range over nonempty sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_k\).
The model uses the Cartesian product \(U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_k\).
\(F(u)=\{x\in X:g(x,u)\leq0\}\) is the feasible set at realization \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigcap_{u\in U}F(u)=\varnothing\quad\text{while possibly}\quad F(u)\neq\varnothing\ \text{for every }u\in U.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jointly quantified uncertainty can destroy common feasibility despite scenario-wise feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Joint uncertainty is incompatible with robust feasibility when
\[\bigcap_{u\in U}F(u)=\varnothing.\]
This can occur even though \(F(u)\neq\varnothing\) for every individual \(u\in U\): each joint realization is separately feasible, but no single here-and-now decision belongs to every scenario-wise feasible set. If the Cartesian product \(U_1\times\cdots\times U_k\) includes physically impossible coordinate combinations, such combinations may be the sole cause of the empty intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every joint scenario may be feasible separately while no single decision works for all scenarios, especially when a product set admits impossible combinations.
knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Joint Uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empty-intersection condition and distinction from scenario-wise feasibility are correct, but the claim concerning impossible Cartesian-product combinations lacks an inspectable source.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Pflug and Pichler, Multistage Stochastic Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Pflug and Pichler, Multistage Stochastic Optimization

assumptions_latex: A two-stage ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) contains joint laws of \((\xi_1,\xi_2)\).
After observing history \(h=\xi_1\), admissible continuation laws are the conditionals induced by members of \(\mathcal P\).
The set \(\mathcal P\) is not stable under pasting these admissible conditionals across histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{\pi}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E_P[L(\pi,\xi)]\ \text{need not equal the value obtained by nested conditional reoptimization}.\]

notation.meaning: nonrectangular ambiguity set of joint laws

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage distributional form of time inconsistency under failure of rectangularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(\mathcal P\) is not stable under history-wise pasting of its admissible conditional laws, then a conditional worst-case law selected separately after each observed history need not correspond to any joint law in \(\mathcal P\). Consequently, the ex ante problem
\[\inf_{\pi}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}E_P[L(\pi,\xi)]\]
need not agree with its nested conditional reoptimization, and an ex ante optimal policy can cease to be optimal after \(\xi_1\) is observed. This is nonrectangular time inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without rectangularity, history-wise worst-case conditionals may not form an admissible joint law, so ex ante optimization can disagree with later reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonrectangular Time Inconsistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement matches the standard role of rectangularity in dynamic consistency, but the exact pasting convention, nested value comparison, and policy-consistency conclusion require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy Reoptimization Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic robust policies whose prescribed continuations disagree with later conditional reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^*\) minimize a time-zero robust objective over an admissible policy class, and let \(\pi^*_{t:}(h_t)\) denote its continuation after history \(h_t\). For the conditional ambiguity set \(\mathcal P_t(h_t)\), define \[V_t(h_t,\pi)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_t(h_t)}\mathbb E_P[L_{t:T}(\pi,\xi)\mid h_t].\] Policy reoptimization inconsistency occurs when, for some \(t\), histories of positive probability satisfy \[\pi^*_{t:}(h_t)\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi_{t:}}V_t(h_t,\pi_{t:}).\] Thus a policy optimal before uncertainty unfolds is not sequentially optimal when its continuation is recomputed using the model's conditional ambiguity specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-zero robust policy is inconsistent when its prescribed continuation is not optimal after some reachable history under the conditional ambiguity model.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi^*\) is time-zero optimal and admits history-dependent continuations.
Conditional objectives and ambiguity sets are well-defined at each reachable history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists t,h_t:\ \pi^*_{t:}(h_t)\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi_{t:}}V_t(h_t,\pi_{t:})\).

notation.meaning: information history available at stage t
conditional ambiguity set after history h_t
remaining cumulative loss from stage t through T

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sequential inconsistency is characterized by disagreement between an ex ante policy continuation and conditional reoptimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role fits the terminal diagnostic container, but no source is cited. The formulation also alternates between histories of positive probability and an unrestricted existential history; singleton histories may have probability zero in continuous models. An authoritative dynamic robust-optimization locator and a precise reachable-history or almost-sure conditional formulation are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Ambiguity Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between declared conditional ambiguity sets and conditionals induced by the joint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a set of joint laws for \(\xi_{1:T}\), and let \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\) be the conditional ambiguity set used by a stagewise recursion. The induced conditional set is \[\mathcal P_t(h_t)=\{P(\xi_{t+1:T}\in\cdot\mid h_t):P\in\mathcal P,\ P(h_t)>0\}.\] A stagewise ambiguity mismatch occurs at \((t,h_t)\) when \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\ne\mathcal P_t(h_t)\). If \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\supsetneq\mathcal P_t(h_t)\), the recursion protects against unattainable conditional laws; if \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\subsetneq\mathcal P_t(h_t)\), it omits conditionals admitted by the joint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise ambiguity is mismatched when the recursion uses conditional distributions different from those induced by the specified joint ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: Regular conditional distributions exist for every relevant history.
\(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\) refer to the same uncertainty process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q_t(h_t)\ne\mathcal P_t(h_t)\) identifies a stagewise ambiguity mismatch.

notation.meaning: conditionals induced by the joint ambiguity set
conditional ambiguity set used by the recursion

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consistency requires agreement between joint-law conditionals and stagewise ambiguity sets
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role fits the mismatch diagnostic. However, the definition using P(h_t)>0 applies directly only to atomic histories and does not adequately define induced conditional ambiguity sets for continuous histories, where regular conditional distributions are version-dependent. A source on rectangularity or dynamically consistent ambiguity sets is required to fix the exact formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Counterpart-Size Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding growth caused by explicit deterministic robust reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider robust instances with input encoding length \(L\), and let \(R(I)\) be an exact deterministic counterpart constructed by explicitly enumerating uncertainty realizations or uncertainty-set faces. Counterpart-size explosion occurs for a family \(I_k\) when \[\operatorname{size}(R(I_k))\ge 2^{\Omega(L_k)}.\] In particular, if \(m_k\) independent binary uncertainty coordinates are enumerated, the counterpart can contain \(2^{m_k}\) scenario-indexed constraint blocks although the uncertainty description has size \(O(m_k)\). Consequently, merely writing or reading this explicit counterpart requires exponential time and storage, independently of the subsequent solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact robust counterpart suffers size explosion when a compact uncertainty description produces exponentially many explicit variables or constraints.
assumptions_latex: The reformulation explicitly enumerates scenarios, faces, or equivalent combinatorial objects.
Encoding size counts scalar coefficients, variables, and constraints in a standard finite representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}(R(I_k))\ge 2^{\Omega(L_k)}\), so explicit construction is not polynomial in the original input length.

notation.meaning: encoding length of the original robust instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit enumeration of exponentially many binary scenarios yields exponential formulation size
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind is appropriate because the record asserts an exponential formulation-size lower bound. Explicitly enumerating 2^{m_k} scenarios establishes exponential growth in m_k, but it does not by itself establish 2^{Omega(L_k)} without a stated relation such as L_k=Theta(m_k). A class-specific encoding analysis and inspectable source are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial-Subproblem Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational obstruction caused by an intractable worst-case uncertainty oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate decision \(x\), define the adversarial separation value \[s(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u).\] Suppose deciding whether \(s(x)>0\) is NP-hard for the represented class of uncertainty sets and constraint functions. Then exact robust-feasibility separation is NP-hard, because \(x\) is robust feasible exactly when \(s(x)\le0\). Any cutting-plane or decomposition method requiring an exact maximizer of this subproblem therefore has no polynomial-time implementation for the whole class unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), even when its master problem is polynomially solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If finding a worst-case uncertainty realization is NP-hard, exact robust-feasibility separation and oracle-based decomposition inherit that hardness.
assumptions_latex: \(g(x,u)\) and \(\mathcal U\) have finite encodings.
The decision problem \(s(x)>0\) is NP-hard for the chosen instance class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact separation is NP-hard; a polynomial exact oracle would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: constraint violation at decision x and uncertainty u

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: robust feasibility is equivalent to nonpositivity of the adversarial separation value
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound role is suitable for an NP-hardness boundary, and the separation equivalence is structurally correct. The actual hardness is assumed rather than supported for a specified representation class, and methods requiring only a violation certificate or approximate oracle are not distinguished from those requiring an exact maximizer. A class-specific reduction or authoritative theorem locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Decomposition Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition stagnation diagnosed through a persistent certified optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let a decomposition method produce valid bounds \(L_k\le v^*\le U_k\) after iteration \(k\). Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\rm abs},\varepsilon_{\rm rel}\ge0\), define \[G_k=U_k-L_k,\qquad \tau_k=\varepsilon_{\rm abs}+\varepsilon_{\rm rel}\max\{1,|U_k|,|L_k|\}.\] The bounds are weak at iteration \(k\) when \(G_k>\tau_k\). A persistent weak-bound failure occurs when \(G_k>\tau_k\) throughout the allotted iterations or time, so no requested-accuracy certificate is obtained despite valid master and adversarial bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition bounds are weak when their certified upper–lower gap remains above the chosen absolute and relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) is a valid lower and upper bound on the same optimum.
At least one finite incumbent upper bound is available when the gap is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_k>\tau_k\) prevents certification of the requested optimality accuracy.

notation.meaning: certified bound gap at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid upper and lower bounds certify accuracy only after their gap meets the stopping tolerance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits a decomposition-stagnation diagnostic. The displayed gap test is a coherent operational definition, but persistence only through an allotted time or iteration budget does not establish an intrinsic failure of the decomposition bounds. No decomposition or solver-stopping reference is supplied.

children.title: Numerical Scaling Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by disparate coefficient, variable, or constraint magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Scaling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision failure caused by extreme coefficient or residual magnitude disparities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite robust counterpart \(Ax\le b\), define the nonzero coefficient spread \[\rho(A)=\frac{\max_{i,j:A_{ij}\ne0}|A_{ij}|}{\min_{i,j:A_{ij}\ne0}|A_{ij}|}.\] Numerical scaling failure is present when the formulation's units make \(\rho(A)\) or analogous objective and bound spreads so large that the solver's absolute feasibility test accepts a materially infeasible original-unit solution, or rejects a materially feasible one. A direct diagnostic is disagreement between solver status and recomputed dimensionless residuals \(r_i=(A_i\hat x-b_i)/(1+|b_i|+\|A_i\|\,\|\hat x\|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling fails when disparate numerical magnitudes make solver tolerances misrepresent feasibility in the model's original units.
assumptions_latex: The deterministic counterpart is evaluated in finite-precision arithmetic.
Residuals are independently recomputed using the reported solution \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Material disagreement between solver feasibility and normalized residuals identifies a numerical scaling failure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scale-dependent absolute tolerances can disagree with dimensionless residual checks
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role matches the leaf. Coefficient spread alone does not determine numerical failure, and the terms 'so large' and 'materially' lack thresholds. The normalized residual also leaves the vector norm unspecified. An authoritative numerical-optimization source and an explicit diagnostic convention are needed.

children.title: Numerical Conditioning Failures
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity caused by ill-conditioned counterpart or subproblem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Conditioning Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution unreliability caused by high sensitivity of the counterpart to small perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a locally unique solution \(z^*\) of a deterministic robust counterpart be characterized by \(F(z,d)=0\), where \(d\) denotes problem data. If \(J=\nabla_zF(z^*,d)\) is nonsingular, the local absolute sensitivity is governed by \(J^{-1}\nabla_dF\). Numerical conditioning failure occurs when its relative condition measure is large enough that data or rounding perturbations of relative size \(\delta\) can induce unacceptable relative solution or residual changes of order \(\kappa\delta\). Near-singularity of \(J\), unstable active sets, or materially different solutions under tiny controlled perturbations are corresponding diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning fails when small data or rounding perturbations can produce unacceptably large changes in the robust solution or residuals.
assumptions_latex: A local equation system \(F(z,d)=0\) represents the relevant optimality conditions.
The Jacobian \(J=\nabla_zF(z^*,d)\) exists near the reported solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large local sensitivity or near-singularity makes the computed solution numerically unreliable under small perturbations.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the local optimality system

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inverse-Jacobian sensitivity characterizes local conditioning of a regular equation system
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate, and the statement is explicitly limited to a differentiable local equation system. However, kappa is not defined by a formula or norm, 'unacceptable' is not quantified, and the text mixes the nonsingular sensitivity model with near-singularity and unstable active-set diagnostics. A numerical optimization source is needed to delimit these cases.

children.title: Scaling–Conditioning Interactions
children.top_down_role: Cases where poor scaling amplifies conditioning problems in robust computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Conditioning Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of representation scaling on numerical conditioning and solver reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear constraint system \(Ax=b\), nonsingular diagonal row and column scalings give the equivalent system \[(D_rAD_c)y=D_rb,\qquad x=D_cy.\] Exact feasibility is unchanged, but the numerical condition number generally is not: \(\kappa(D_rAD_c)\) may be much smaller or larger than \(\kappa(A)\). Hence poor scaling can amplify an underlying conditioning problem, while equilibration can reduce representation-induced sensitivity without removing intrinsic near-dependence. Reliability should therefore be assessed after mapping residuals and solutions back to original units, not solely from the scaled solver system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent row and variable scalings preserve exact solutions but can improve or worsen numerical conditioning and reported residual reliability.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are nonsingular diagonal matrices.
Condition numbers use a fixed subordinate matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equivalence does not imply equal conditioning: generally \(\kappa(D_rAD_c)\ne\kappa(A)\).

notation.meaning: matrix condition number in the selected norm

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonsingular diagonal scaling preserves exact feasibility while changing matrix condition numbers
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind correctly captures the effect of equivalent scaling on conditioning. The exact-equivalence claim is correct for nonsingular diagonal scalings, but the condition number convention should specify that the matrices are square and nonsingular or define the rectangular/pseudoinverse convention. No inspectable numerical linear algebra citation is supplied.

children.title: Numerical Reliability Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Solver signals and reproducibility checks associated with numerical unreliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Reliability Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Post-solution checks for feasibility, robustness, and perturbation stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed decision \(\hat x\), a numerical reliability report consists of independently recomputed normalized deterministic residuals, an adversarial violation bound, and perturbation tests. Define \[r_{\rm det}=\max_i\frac{(A_i\hat x-b_i)_+}{1+|b_i|+\|A_i\|\|\hat x\|},\qquad r_{\rm rob}=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(\hat x,u).\] Given tolerances \(\tau_{\rm det},\tau_{\rm rob}\), robust feasibility is certified only if \(r_{\rm det}\le\tau_{\rm det}\) and a validated upper bound on \(r_{\rm rob}\) is at most \(\tau_{\rm rob}\). Stability under small rescalings and data perturbations is supplementary evidence, not a replacement for these bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability requires independently checked normalized residuals and a validated upper bound on worst-case constraint violation; perturbation stability provides an additional diagnostic.
assumptions_latex: The adversarial computation returns a mathematically valid upper bound on worst-case violation.
Residuals are evaluated independently of the solver's internal stopping test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities certify tolerance-level feasibility; their failure flags an unreliable solution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: independently validated residual and worst-case violation bounds directly certify tolerance-level feasibility
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the terminal diagnostic. A validated upper bound on worst-case violation can certify robust feasibility to tolerance, but the relation between the deterministic residuals and the robust constraints is not specified. Moreover, failure of these sufficient checks means 'not certified,' not necessarily that the solution is unreliable. A supporting numerical robust-optimization source is required.
