knowledge_statements.title: Out-of-Sample Stress Testing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical validation of a fixed robust decision on unseen and deliberately stressed scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a fixed decision \(\hat x\), an independent evaluation sample \(\xi^{1:N}\), loss \(\ell\), constraint violation \(g\), and stress transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_K\). Compute losses and violations on every \(T_k(\xi^j)\), including \(T_0\) equal to the identity. Report, for each \(k\), empirical mean and upper loss quantiles, violation frequency, and maximum violation. If confidence bounds are required, construct them using a prespecified simultaneous procedure. The output is a diagnostic table indexed by stress regime; \(\hat x\) is never refitted on the evaluation sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a fixed robust decision on independent and stressed scenarios, reporting losses, tail behavior, violations, and prespecified uncertainty intervals without refitting.
assumptions_latex: The baseline evaluation observations are independent of all data used to select \(\hat x\).
Stress transformations and reported metrics are specified before inspecting evaluation outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs out-of-sample performance diagnostics for every baseline and stressed regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate for this validation workflow. The cited simulation-and-sensitivity chapter is too broad to support the complete stress-testing protocol, including transformed-sample dependence, simultaneous confidence bounds, tail metrics, and the no-refitting requirement. A specific validation or stress-testing source is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Set Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variation of robust value and decisions under controlled uncertainty-set perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\mathcal U(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\) be a nested uncertainty-set family, with \(\mathcal U(\theta_1)\subseteq\mathcal U(\theta_2)\) whenever \(\theta_1\le\theta_2\). For the minimization value \[v(\theta)=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U(\theta)}f(x,u),\] one has \(v(\theta_1)\le v(\theta_2)\). Uncertainty-set sensitivity analysis records changes in \(v(\theta)\), selected optimizers, worst-case scenarios, and active robust constraints over a prespecified parameter grid. Large changes under small changes of \(\theta\) identify calibration sensitivity even though value monotonicity is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging a nested uncertainty set cannot improve a minimization robust value; sensitivity analysis tracks resulting changes in value, optimizer, and active worst cases.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is independent of \(\theta\), and all displayed infima and suprema are well-defined.
The uncertainty sets are nested in the parameter order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_1\le\theta_2\Rightarrow v(\theta_1)\le v(\theta_2)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity follows directly from nesting of the inner supremum domains

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness-Frontier Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto representation of nominal performance versus worst-case protection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)\) be nominal cost and \(r(x)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)\) be worst-case loss or violation for \(x\in X\). The robustness frontier is the nondominated set \[\mathcal F=\{(c(x),r(x)):x\in X,\ \nexists y\in X\text{ with }c(y)\le c(x),\ r(y)\le r(x)\text{ and at least one strict inequality}\}.\] Its constraint-sweep representation solves \(\min_{x\in X}c(x)\) subject to \(r(x)\le\rho\) over protection levels \(\rho\). Each attained solution is weakly nondominated; every properly supported frontier point is recoverable by a positive weighted-sum scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robustness frontier contains decisions not simultaneously improvable in nominal cost and worst-case performance, and can be traced by protection constraints or scalarization.
assumptions_latex: Nominal cost and worst-case performance are minimized under the stated sign convention.
The relevant infima are attained for the protection levels considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) represents the nondominated nominal-cost versus worst-case-performance tradeoff.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the frontier is the Pareto-nondominated image of nominal and worst-case criteria
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind appropriately describes a criterion-space frontier. The nondominance definition is coherent, but the recovery claims require a source and clearer terminology: positive weighted sums recover supported efficient points under the relevant attainment assumptions, while 'properly supported' is not defined here. No multiobjective robust-optimization citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial-Scenario Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility diagnostic for a fixed robust decision over a designated validation uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a decision \(\bar x\), a nonempty compact validation set \(\mathcal V\), constraint functions \(g_j(\bar x,\xi)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), initialize the incumbent score to \(s=-\infty\). Use a globally valid maximization oracle to compute
\[
(\xi^\star,j^\star)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\xi\in\mathcal V,\,1\le j\le m} g_j(\bar x,\xi),\qquad s^\star=g_{j^\star}(\bar x,\xi^\star).
\]
Stop when global optimality is certified. If \(s^\star>\varepsilon\), output \((\xi^\star,j^\star,s^\star)\) as an adversarial witness that \(\bar x\) violates validation robustness. If \(s^\star\le\varepsilon\), certify that every tested constraint satisfies \(g_j(\bar x,\xi)\le\varepsilon\) for all \(\xi\in\mathcal V\) and \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally maximize constraint violation over the validation scenarios. A value above tolerance supplies an adversarial failure witness; otherwise the decision is tolerance-feasible throughout the validation set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is nonempty and compact.
For each \(j\), the map \(\xi\mapsto g_j(\bar x,\xi)\) is upper semicontinuous on \(\mathcal V\).
The maximization oracle returns a globally optimal scenario and constraint index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either certifies \(g_j(\bar x,\xi)\le\varepsilon\) on \(\mathcal V\) or provides an explicit scenario \(\xi^\star\) witnessing failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the Adversarial-Scenario Diagnostics leaf, and the compactness, upper semicontinuity, and global-oracle assumptions make the stated maximizer-based certificate mathematically coherent. However, the cited robust-optimization and scenario-analysis sections do not specifically establish this adversarial maximization diagnostic or its global feasibility certificate. A source with a precise locator for robust constraint separation, worst-case violation search, or adversarial feasibility certification is required before the formulation can be reviewed reliably as sourced candidate knowledge.
